narrative: On December 11, 2020 at 3:00pm Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Emelyn Sanchez P. made an announced visit to The House of Bethesda for the purpose of conducting a Case Management- Licensee Initiated (Pre-Licensing) inspection visit. LPA Sanchez P. met with Dr. Aline Smith, Facility Administrator and Robert Smith, Facility Director who granted access to the facility and a toured was conducted. The facility will be licensed to provide care and supervision to six (6) children ages 13 through 17. Ambulatory only. There are no bodies of water on the premises. The census today is zero (0). The home is set up as follows: This is a one story house with three (3) bedrooms, two (2) bathrooms, living room, family room, staff office, dining area, kitchen/laundry area, and outdoor space. Living Room: There is adequate furniture which appears to be in good condition there is one sofa, a desk with a operating computer and a locked file cabinet. Family Room: There is adequate furniture which appears to be in good condition there is one love seat and one sofa, a desk with a operating computer, center table, a covered fire place, and an operating sliding door that exits out into the left side of the home. Staff Office: Located to the right of the family room. There is a desk with a operating computer, fax machine, and closet space. All medication will be kept double locked in the staff office inside a locked box. Dining Area: One table with six (6) chairs. Kitchen/Laundry Area: There is a stove/oven with four (4) burners, all working at this time. There is a microwave and two refrigerators/freezers. The food service in the home will be adequate with perishable/nonperishable food supplies. There is a fire extinguisher located to the right once entering the kitchen. Trash can has a tight lid on. All cleaning supplies are kept locked in cabinets above the washer and dryer. The knives are kept locked in the kitchen cabinet and will be made accessible only to employees. Bedroom #1: Is vacant. The room is equipped with two twin size beds. There are adequate drawers, closet space, and lighting in this room. Bedroom #2: Is vacant. The room is equipped with two twin size beds. There are adequate drawers, closet space, and lighting in this room. Bedroom #3: Is vacant. The room is equipped with two twin size beds. There are adequate drawers, closet space, and lighting in this room. Report Cont. on LIC 809-C. Bathrooms: There are two (2) bathrooms. One (1) bathroom is located inside the staff office and the other bathroom is located next to Bedroom #3. The bathroom located inside the staff office will only be used by the facility staff. All bathrooms were checked and were in operating conditions. The faucets that are used by the children were tested and delivered hot water at a safe temperature range. There are security bars on the windows in Bedroom #1 and #3. The emergency release handle is in working conditions. Outdoor Space: LPA Sanchez P. observed the entrance area and backyard to be free of debris and hazardous materials. Garage: The detached garage will be kept locked and will only be used for storage space. LPA Sanchez P. also observed a freezer that will be used to store extra food. The home was inspected and the following was observed: The facility is clean, safe, sanitary, and in good repair. Medicines, disinfectants, and cleaning solutions are inaccessible to children in care. No more than two (2) children will share a bedroom. Children have comfortable mattresses, clean linens, blankets, and pillows which are all in good repair. Outdoor activity space is free of obstructions. There are no weapons in the facility. Sharp knives are stored in a locked cabinet and inaccessible to children. Staff will conduct a sharps count to ensure all sharp objects are returned and locked in the lock box. Adequate supervision will be provided for children in care. Staff will ensure three nutritious meals and snacks. Food supply will be ample in the home. Children will be accorded personal rights. Children in care will be supported and encouraged to participate in extracurricular activities. Children in care will be able to contact the licensing agency or Ombudsman person in confidence without threats or punishment for making complaints. All posting requirements were met. Children in care will not be restricted in telephone use except by court order. There is a working telephone line available for clients to use. All smoke detectors and carbon monoxide are operable and meet statutory requirements. The home will operate within capacity and limitations of license. LPA Sanchez P. observed age appropriate First Aid supplies. However, LPA Sanchez P. encouraged Licensee to obtain a regular thermometer to have instead of the disposable thermometers located inside the first aid kit. Also, fire extinguishers require service. There was no deficiencies cited at this time of the visit. Exit Interview was conducted, and a copy of this report will be mailed or e-mailed to the facility for signature due to COVID-19 restrictions.

On this date, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Cynthia Galindo conducted an unannounced Case Management visit, via telephone as a result of Covid-19 related restrictions and spoke with Administrator Shannon Blanchard. The purpose of the phone call was to discuss a few concerns on the facility. LPA discussed the following with Administrator: Runaway Plan, Emergency Intervention Plan (EIP), staff training, admission determination and procedures, reporting requirements and supervision concerns. LPA conducted a thorough review of the facility's staff training records, incident reports and the facility's plan of operation and program statement as well as interviewed staff and Administrator. Based on record review, staff training records do not include training received on physical and psychosocial needs of children, including behavior management, de-escalation techniques and trauma-informed crisis management planning as required by regulation 87065.1 (c)(3)(X). Training records do not demonstrate how much time is spent on this required topic. According to training records, staff receive ongoing training from Managing Aggressive Behavior (MAB) however the Program Statement states training is to be provided by Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI). The MAB training is not in compliance with the regulations as it was not approved by the Department prior to implementation as required by regulation 87095.22(c). next page... Additionally, facility is not following the Plan of Operation and Program Statement in the following sections as required by regulation 87022(f): Staff training plan- facility does not provide some of the training listed in Section D, page 4-12. Admission process and procedures- facility is not completing pre-screening triage and assessments to determine the appropriateness of placement as stated in Section F, page 2. EIP- facility does not utilize manual restraints as an emergency intervention when a resident is in imminent danger of self-harm or harm to others in the home as stated in the Program Statement Section 22, page 6. After a review of the facility's Law Enforcement contact reports and service calls from the local police department, it was revealed the facility is under reporting incidents and late reporting to the Department as required by regulation 87061(k)(1). Late reporting has been addressed with facility on several occasions. LPA discussed with Administrator concerns over staff's supervision on youth due to a few incidents that occurred in the home. An incident report emailed to the Department where staff provided youth with a cleaning product to complete chores. Staff did not supervise youth who later drank some of the disinfectant spray in attempt to self-harm. Youth was taken to the ER for ingestion of a toxin. On another occasion, a youth obtained access to a facility phone in the middle of the night and made unapproved and unsupervised phone calls. Based on incident reports and interviews, staff did not supervise youth on these occasions as part of their duties and required by regulation 87065.2(b)(1). The facility is being cited for the deficiencies listed above. The plan of correction discussed with Administrator will also include a submission of an updated Plan of Operation and Program Statement to the Department for approval. A copy of this report and appeal rights were sent via email to Administrator for signature.

investigation_findings: 13Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Cynthia Galindo conducted a complaint inspection at Inspiring Pathways and met with Jessica Ford. The purpose of the inspection was to deliver the findings for the above complaint allegations. During the investigation, LPA interviewed staff and clients which revealed that staff left youth unsupervised and an uncleared adult was supervising youths. On April 4, 2020, a client (see 811 for confidential names) was taken to the hospital for an assessment. While at the hospital, the staff (S1) accompanying the client became concerned of a potential COVID-19 exposure. As a result of this concern, S1 left the client unsupervised at the hospital and contacted the facility for someone to replace her. According to interviews, there was only one staff on shift back at the house. Due to the facility being short staffed, S2 left the home to cover S1 but asked her boyfriend to cover S2's shift at the house. S2's boyfriend did not have a background check record clearance or exemption with the Department on this date but was approved to cover the shift by the Administrator under the presumption of the statewide waivers due to COVID-19. S2's boyfriend stayed with residents alone for a few hours until S2 returned with the client. Although the Department did issue statewide waivers for background check requirements due to COVID-19 (PIN 20-04), Administrator did not follow the terms and conditions set forth in PINs 20-04 and 20-09. The boyfriend's presence at the facility on April 4, 2020 was not approved by the Department because there no written waiver submitted as required by PINs 20-04 and 20-09. Based on the information obtained, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be SUBSTANTIATED. California Code of Regulations are being cited on the attached LIC 9099D. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of the report and appeal rights were provided to the facility via email due to COVID restrictions. SubstantiatedEstimated Days of Completion:

13Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Cynthia Galindo conducted a complaint inspection at Inspiring Pathways and met with Shannon Blanchard. The purpose of the inspection was to deliver the findings for the above complaint allegations. During the investigation, LPA interviewed staff and clients as well as obtained relevant documents. Interviews and documents reveal that youth accessed a sharp object that was used to injure another youth during a fight. On April 16, 2022, staff provided the youth with an eyebrow razor and when the eyebrow razor was returned later that day, the blade was missing. Interviews confirm that staff was aware that the blade was missing but yet no attempts were made to locate the blade. Staff did not provide the proper care and supervision by locating the missing blade after becoming aware that it was missing. The next day, the same youth who returned the eyebrow razor with the missing blade, got into that fight with another youth and staff did not intervene. The youth sustained injuries during the fight. Staff failed to protect the youth by not stopping the fight. On this date, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Cynthia Galindo conducted an unannounced Case Management visit, via telephone as a result of Covid-19 related restrictions and spoke with Administrator Shannon Blanchard. The purpose of the phone call was to discuss the facility's Needs and Services Plan (NSP) LPA obtained several NSP from current and previous clients placed in the home. Based on record review, the NSP are not in compliance with the Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards. LPA observed the NSP lacked written approval from the child or authorized representative; lacked information regarding services necessary to meet the clients' needs. Additionally, the NSP modifications did not include the facility's recommendation regarding the feasibility of the child's return to a less restrictive family-like setting; the need for modification in services and the progress of the child toward a transfer goal. All the NSP reviewed by LPA contained the same information with no changes in the language. Based on the information obtained, the facility is being cited for violation of California Code of Regulations, Title Division Six regulations 87068.2 and 87068.3. A copy of this report and appeal rights were sent via email to Administrator for signature.

On August 9, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Jean Herring, Juliet Robles and Raymond Wu conducted an unannounced inspection at the facility at 10: AM. LPAs met with Danielle Bell, Facility Manager (FM). The purpose of the inspection was to conduct an Annual/Required inspection of the facility. The facility currently has a provisional Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) license. The STRTP's Mental Health Program Application is pending approval. The STRTP has not submitted an application for National Accreditation. This STRTP is licensed to serve up to six (6) ambulatory children ages 11-17 years of age. The facility also provide services to non-minor dependents pursuant to W&I Code 16501.1 (C)(1). There are four (4) ambulatory minors and one(1) ambulatory non-minor dependent currently in placement. This facility is a one-story home with three (3) bedrooms, two (2) bathrooms, one (1) office, kitchen, dining, formal living rooms, and family room. Physical Plant The license is posted in a prominent, publicly accessible location in the facility. Disinfectants, cleaning solutions and sharps are locked in a walk-in closet located in the office. Facility has non-perishable foods for at least one week and perishable foods for at least two days. Facility provides at least three(3) meals per day. Medications are centrally stored and locked in the office. All kitchen, food preparation, and storage areas are kept clean and free of rodents and other vermin. Facility has one or more carbon monoxide detectors in the facility. Facility provides basic laundry services. Room temperatures are maintained at 76 degrees F. The hot water temperature was tested and measured at 115 degrees F. All toilets, handwashing and bathing facilities are maintained in safe and sanitary operating condition and meet the requirements. No more than 2 children share a bedroom. All beds are in good repair; equipped with good springs and a clean mattress; and supplied with pillows which are clean and in good repair. Facility provides age-appropriate clothing items and hygiene products. Overall, facility is clean, safe sanitary and in good repair. Operations Facility maintains a current, written plan of operation that meets licensing standards. Facility maintains a register of clients and the register is available upon request. Facility maintains and implements written complaint procedures and the procedures are posted in a publicly accessible location in the facility. The board of directors regularly conducts meeting to review and discuss the STRTP's operation. Cash resources are kept on the facility premises in a locked and secure location. Client Records All client records are available to the licensing agency to inspect, audit and copy upon demand. Client records contain required information including, but not limited to, consent forms, court orders, needs and services plan, removal/discipline/complaint procedures; medical assessment; safeguards for cash resources, personal property and valuables; education records; personal rights forms; and medication administration records. LPAs interviewed two(2) clients during the inspection. Core/Therapeutic Services Facility provides core services and supports to children and non-minor dependents as appropriate or necessary that are trauma informed, culturally relevant, age and developmentally appropriate and include the following: Medi-Cal specialty mental health services; transition support services; educational and physical, behavioral, and mental health supports; activities to support children and non-minor dependents and services to achieve permanency. One(1) Type A Deficiency cited during this inspection. LPAs provided three (3) Advisory Notes-Technical Violation (LIC9102TV) and one (1) Advisory Notes-Technical Assistance (LIC 9102TA). Appeal rights provided. An Annual/Required Continuation inspection is required. An exit interview was completed and a signed copy of this report was provided to the facility representative.

On August 10, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Jean Herring and Raymond Wu conducted an unannounced inspection of the facility at 9: AM. LPAs met with Danyelle Jones, Unit Coordinator and Robert Carter, STRTP Director. The purpose of the inspection was to conduct a Case Management - Annual Continuation inspection of the facility. During this inspection, LPAs reviewed the Emergency Intervention Plan, Emergency and Disaster Preparedness Plan, and Staff Records. Emergency Intervention Plan Facility maintains a monthly log of each use of manual restraints that contains all required information. The log is available for review by the Department upon request. LPAs observed documentation of Emergency Intervention Training and on-going training. Disaster Preparedness Plan Facility maintains a current, written disaster and mass casualty plan of action. Facility conducts disaster drill at least quarterly for each shift. The drills are documented and the documentation is maintained in the facility for at least a year. Facility maintains an emergency and disaster plan, register of clients, Needs and Services Plan for each client, medication records, and contact information for each client's responsible party and physician. Staff Records LPAs reviewed seven(7) personnel records. All individuals subject to criminal records review have been fingerprinted and signed a Criminal Record Statement. Personnel records are maintained on the licensee, administrator and each employee. The administrator meets the required qualifications and/or experience. Documentation of the required education and experience requirements are maintained in the personnel file. Facility Managers meet requirements. Personnel records contain documentation of 24-hour initial training, and 40-hour annual training in addition to CPR and First Aid. This inspection reveals that seven (7) out of 7 personnel records reviewed by LPAs, do not contain health screening and TB test documents. There are two(2) Type B deficiencies cited and two (2) Advisory Notes-Technical Violation (LIC9102TV) provided during this inspection. Appeal rights provided. An exit interview was conducted and a signed copy of this report was provided to the facility representative.

narrative: Licensing Program Analyst Dina Camara and Licensing Program Manager Angela King conducted a case management inspection 08/09/22 at 9: AM based on the number of relevant law enforcement contacts reported by the facility, pursuant to Health and Safety Code section 1538.7. During this inspection, 9 out of Direct Care Staff and 6 out of 6 youth files were reviewed. 2 out of Direct Care Staff and 4 out of 6 youth were interviewed. (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, dated 08/09/2022). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Minutes from the board of directors' meetings related to the facility's incidents involving contact with law enforcement were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments and youth case plans, the licensee uses trauma-informed and evidence-based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. LPA Dina Camara and LPM Angela King observed documentation of completed training on policies and procedures on when and how to involve law enforcement in response to an incident. Training records show staff have been trained on Emergency Intervention as required. The licensee is contacting law enforcement in accordance to their Emergency Intervention Plan when there is an immediate risk of serious harm to a child or others. There are no deficiencies cited at this time. A copy of this report was discussed and provided to Calissa Walker, Administrator.

An unannounced case management inspection was conducted by Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Christopher Larios on 6/9/25, at 9: AM. During the inspection LPA Larios met with Administrator, Raeanna Howard. Information obtained from record review and interviews conducted revealed that on the afternoon of 1/5/25 incidents occurred at the facility requiring staff to restrain a client multiple times over a three-hour period. Statements obtained from confidential interviews conducted indicate that during this time a staff (S1) (See Confidential Names form LIC811 dated 6/9/25) obtained a water hose and sprayed a client (C1) with water due to the client's confrontational behavior. (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, 08/26/25). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments, and youth safety plans, and crisis prevention intervention plan and client intake information sheet, the licensee uses trauma-informed and evidence-based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. LPA, Camara observed documentation of completed training on policies and procedures on when and how to involve law enforcement in response to an incident. LPA reviewed the following domains of the Compliance and Regulatory Enforcement (CARE) tool: Physical Plant and Disaster Preparedness Physical Plant The license, facility sketch, personal rights, emergency disaster form, complaints poster, emergency phone numbers and food menu are posted in a prominent, publicly accessible location in the facility. Disinfectants and cleaning solutions are kept inaccessible and locked in a cabinet located in the kitchen and staff office. Sharps/knives are inaccessible and stored in a locked drawer in the kitchen. Facility has non-perishable food for at least one week and perishable food for at least two days. Medications are centrally stored in a locked cabinet in the office. Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were tested and in proper working order. Fire extinguishers were fully charged. Room temperatures are maintained at around 66-71 degrees F. The hot water temperature was tested and measured at 135-140 degrees F (Please see LIC 9102). All sinks, showers and toilets are in working order. All beds are in good repair; equipped with good springs, clean mattresses and pillows. Adequate supply of beddings and linens were observed. Identified within the special incident report (SIR) submitted on 7/11/2020 by facility; C1 was taken on a personal outing to the dollar store to buy a notebook. At the time of leaving the store C1 got upset with staff and started walking away from staff disappearing into the store. Staff paid for items and walked outside of the store and C1 was not present. Before leaving the store staff notified local law enforcement and overseeing agencies. Staff left the store but returned to the store to pick up C1 after receiving a call from C1's family identifying C1's whereabouts. Interviews conducted with staff state that C1 hid from staff and staff was unable to be located at the time of the incident. Staff denied leaving C1 stranded or locking C1 out of the facility or vehicle. Based on interviews with C1, C1 stated she did not want to talk about the incident or anything pertaining to time in facility. Documents provided by facility show staff receiving required training in reasonable prudent parenting, trauma care and medications. Interviews conducted with other children in facility identify home and staff as being attentive, present and available to assist children with their needs. Statements made during confidential interviews and documents reviewed do not corroborate with complaint allegations. LPA was unable to ascertain whether or not child was stranded at store or if child ran away. Additionally, LPA was unable to identify an incident or occurrence where C1 or any child was locked out of the facility. Although the allegations may have happened or may be true there is not a preponderance of evidence to identify that the allegations did or did not happen; therefore, this complaint is being closed Unsubstantiated. Exit interview completed, no deficiencies cited and a copy of this report was emailed to Administrator for signature and review.

narrative: One client who was allegedly hit and yelled at moved to a lockdown facility and LPA was not granted permission by client's guardian to conduct an interview. LPA attempted to interview additional clients who were allegedly yelled at and threatened but attempts were unsuccessful. LPA's calls to the guardian of one client were not returned while another client is AWOL and whereabouts are unknown. One client interviewed refused to address the allegations but stated that client had no issues with staff and other clients during placement, and that there was no issue with food. Staff denied hitting and yelling at clients. Staff reported that clients were questioned by law enforcement during AWOL and then brought back to the facility by staff. Clients were upset and threatened to call licensing. Staff reported that one client made the call. Staff stated they were redirecting clients prior to AWOL but clients were non complaint. Another staff denied yelling and making threats towards clients. Staff reported engaging positively with clients and redirects clients when they exhibit negative behavior. Statements obtained from other clients interviewed did not support the allegations. Clients reported not being aware of the allegations and claimed no maltreatment by staff and no issues with food. LPA observed adequate perishable and non-perishable food supply during the unannounced inspection. Photos were taken by LPA for proof of facility meeting regulatory requirements. Staff informed LPA that meals are prepared based on the menu and that there are options available to clients who refuse any meal served. Clients are encouraged to participate in menu preparation. Staff follow the posted menu but are open to accommodating requests during meal preparation, with concurrence from all clients. LPA did not find evidence to support the allegations in interviews with other parties and during the records review. Based on information gathered, although the allegations may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegations was not met, therefore the allegations are unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted. A copy of this report, Confidential Names Form and Appeal Rights were emailed to the facility representative. narrative: It was alleged that at least one staff member (S1; See LIC Confidential Names Form) at the facility failed to meet the needs of one client (C1) in care. More specifically, it was alleged that the staff member failed to take C1's comments seriously during an incident in which they were in a mental crisis. No injuries were sustained although C1 was taken to the hospital as a precaution. In interviews conducted with clients in the home, the clients all stated that they felt safe in the home and felt that the staff were able to meet their needs. The clients all denied feeling dismissed by the staff members in the facility and any time issues were brought up were addressed in a timely manner. In an interview conducted with C1, C1 stated that S1 was their favorite staff member in the facility and denied ever feeling dismissed by S1. S1 was always helpful and took their comments seriously. In interviews conducted with staff, the above comments were corroborated. S1 stated that on the date of the incident, they stayed with C1 the whole time that they were in a state of crisis and played games with them to try and redirect them per their individualized safety plan. S1 denied being dismissive of C1's feelings and stated that the facility had procedures in place to try and redirect clients in crisis prior to calling emergency services. An interview conducted with the facility social worker confirmed these statements. The social worker stated that they had never seen or heard of any staff members in the home being dismissive of clients and they had no concerns about it. Comments made by clients during times of crisis were always taken seriously. A review of C1's Needs and Services Plan and Admissions Agreement confirmed that C1 was known to have episodes of mental crisis and that attempts to redirect them prior to calling emergency services was standard. Based on interviews, redirection procedures for C1 involved constant supervision, board games, car rides, and more. Based on interviews conducted and records reviewed, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove that the above allegation occurred. Although the allegation may have happened or may be valid, the preponderance of evidence standard has not been met. Therefore, the allegations are deemed UNSUBSTANTIATED. An exit interview was conducted and a signed copy of this report, along with the Licensee's Appeal Rights (LIC 9058 01/16) was provided to the Licensee.

narrative: It was alleged that staff members (S1, S3) made inappropriate comments while minors were present and encouraged the client (C1) to fight another client residing in the home. All staff members denied encouraging anyone to fight, however, further disclosed that an incident occurred involving two clients (C1, C5) who were involved in a physical altercation outside of the facility. Clients indicated that the staff does a good job of avoiding shouting matches and de-escalating situations that may arise in the facility between clients. Clients further stated that they feel safe and supported by the staff members at the facility. Clients denied that staff encourage them to fight each other. C1 further disclosed that she did get into an altercation outside the facility with a former client (C5). C1 indicated that they were being transported by S1 back to the facility and they had stopped to pick up C5 who had just gone AWOL. It was alleged that the facility staff handled a client (C4) in a rough manner while trying to redirect them resulting in staff pushing the client into a wall and hitting said client with an object. Information obtained from staff members (S1, S2, S3) denied the alleged allegations further indicating that all staff members are trauma informed and understand the importance of maintaining a healthy relationship with all clients and supporting them in successfully completing their individual programs. Facility staff further indicated that the facility is a hands-off facility and will only place hands on a client to prevent self-harm or bodily harm to others. Staff further disclosed that an incident involving (S3) and C4 occurred on 9/23/22 where (C4) had taken the cell phone into their room knowing that their CSW had informed staff that (C4) was not allowed to use their cellphone unless being supervised by a staff member. S4 indicated that supervision was required due to (C4) sending and receiving inappropriate messages from an unknown male. S3 indicated that when they attempted to retrieve the cell phone C4 ran into the room and began punching a hole in the wall, S4 attempted to verbally redirect and de-escalate the situation from the bedroom doorway when C4 ran and nudged S3 out of the way. S3 further disclosed that after two minutes of using verbal redirection C4 calmed down and proceeded to the living room where staff gave C4's phone back without further incident. Staff indicated that the incident was documented and sent to the appropriate agencies. Information obtained from CSW indicated that they were aware of the incident and when they spoke with C4, they didn't disclose any information indicating that everything was good and that they felt safe. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegations are determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred, therefore the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated. Licensing Program Analysts (LPA)s T. Davis and Dawn Mahecha went to John and Dorothy Almklov House on November 30, 2023 at 09:10am for the purposes of a joint unannounced Random Annual inspection. LPAs met with Crisol Jimenez, Head of Service and Robert Carter, Executive Vice President and discussed the purpose of today's inspection. The STRTP is located in a residential neighborhood and currently has six youth in placement. LPAs observed the facility's kitchen to be clean and well stocked with several food items (perishable and nonperishable). Sharp knives, chemicals, cleaning supplies, and medications are kept locked in areas inaccessible to clients. Each bedroom contained twin beds, dressers, and closet space. There is adequate seating in the dining area and the living room. LPAs also observed the bathrooms to be in good repair and working order. There is no swimming pool or other bodies of water on the premises. The Executive Vice President stated that there weren't any firearms or other weapons on the premises. The last fire drill occurred on October 27, 2023 at 9:05am. There is adequate space for indoor and outdoor activities. Smoke alarms were operable throughout the facility. The outdoor areas were observed to be free of debris and hazards. LPAs reviewed five client and three staff files and found the reviewed files to be in order. LPAs conducted staff Interviews. Clients were either sleeping, sick, or refused to speak with LPAs. LPAs obtained an updated LIC500 (Personnel Report) and a client roster. LPAs also obtained Board of Director's meeting minutes dated August 08, 2013 and September 12, 2023, respectively. The facility will be undergoing renovations in the foreseeable future. Licensee will email LPAs a copy of the facility's plans going forward as it relates to the renovations. LPAs obtained sketches regarding the future project. LPAs found no Title 22/ILS deficiencies on this date. Exit interview done LPAs discussed the cold weather conditions and precautions with licensee and provided licensee with the department's website address (www.ccld.ca.gov).

On 08/27/25, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Joe Martinez initiated an annual/random inspection at the Short Term Residential Treatment Program (STRTP) and met with the facility representative listed above. During the inspection, LPA Martinez interviewed 3 staff. and observed the following: The interior of the facility was observed clean, sanitary, and in good repair Indoor temperatures were maintained within the required range of 68-85 degrees. All hallways and stairways were free of obstruction. Smoke detectors were tested and found operational. Carbon monoxide detectors were present and functional. At least one fully charged fire extinguisher was available At the time of the inspection, there were no clients present. Construction was going on in the facility and water was shut off. LPA Martinez was not able to inspect water temperature. Water will be turned back on prior to youth returning to the facility. The kitchen and food preparation areas were sanitary and well organized. Cleaning supplies and toxic substances were locked and inaccessible. Food storage areas were clean and sufficient supplies of perishable and nonperishable food were available. Sharps are locked in the facility office and inaccessible to youth placed in the home. The facility has readily accessible first aid supplies maintained in a central location in the facility. Three bedrooms were observed during the inspection. All individual beds were clean, safe, and comfortable, with pillows, mattresses, and linens provided. Each child have their own bed and adequate supply of linens (sheets, blankets/coverings, towels, and washcloths) available to allow for weekly changes or more frequent changes. Adequate storage space for each child's clothing and personal belongings were observed. The facility also has a separate, lockable locker for each youth to store their personal belongings. Due to time constraints, the annual review will need to be completed at a later time. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. LPA Martinez conducted an exit interview and provided the STRTP Representative with a signed copy of the LIC 809 and LIC809C.

narrative: Investigation revealed the following: It was alleged facility staff are not appropriately supervising minor in care. Interview conducted with staff were similar and denied the allegation. Staff stated that they have adequate staff throughout each shift to monitor the children in care. Staff stated that children get passes to walk or be in the community but that when children do not return on time or if they aren't allowed to be gone proper agencies are notified and local law enforcement is called, and reports are filed. Staff stated they typically are unaware of what transpires when children run away from facility. However, one staff stated that they were made aware of one incident occurring while one child was on runaway status due to local law enforcement telling them what happened, but staff stated they were not given specifics only questioned about potential locations of child's whereabouts. Children had similar statements and denied the allegation. Children stated that there are adequate staff and that there is adequate staff to meet their needs. Two children had contradictory statements. Children stated that there was adequate staff to supervise them in the home, but that staff don't always answer the phones when children are on outings or wanting to get picked up. Additionally, one child stated that staff don't intervene when children are fighting. However, the information provided for staff was unclear as to if incident occurred in the home or while children were outside on runaway or outing. Child in which this investigation was generated denied speaking with LPA. Documents reviewed identified proper notifications were made pertaining to incident referenced within this investigation and all incidents leading up to and after child returned were documented. Licensing Program Analyst attempted to reach county social worker but was unable to speak with county worker regarding incident but documents reviewed identified no issues or concerns with facility or children being placed in facility. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. narrative: LPA also reviewed pertinent STRTP records, Department databases, and reports from other agencies. The STRTP has three bedrooms for clients. Two are along the left side of the home with the third bedroom, the master bedroom, being across a hallway that bisects the home. The facility has three restrooms in total. One is located within the master bedroom, one located in the hallway, and a third in the rear of the home, near staff offices. According to S1, The rear restroom is for staff only. Staff restroom has a toilet and sink and is used for multi-purpose storage. The hallway restroom is designated for use by the clients whose bedroom is on the left side of the home. The remaining restroom, in the master bedroom, is for the occupants of that bedroom. Interviews with S1, C1, C2, C4, and C5 were consistent in revealing that the restroom located in the master bedroom was being used by all clients as an auxiliary restroom if the hallway restroom was occupied. Based on LPA's observations and interviews which were conducted, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be SUBSTANTIATED. Interim Licensing Standards Article 7 are being cited on the attached LIC9099-D. Exit Interview conducted. Plans of Correction discussed. A signed copy of this report, LIC9099-C, LIC9099-D, and LIC811 were provided to Henry Trochez, Administrator. Appeal rights provided. This is an amended finding delivered on 12/15/23. LPA also reviewed pertinent STRTP records, Department databases, and reports from other agencies. Interviews with clients (C1, C2, C4, C5) and staff (S1) returned answers inconsistent with the allegation of staff allowing youths to smoke in the facility. The STRTP has signs prominently posted stating that smoking/vaping is not allowed in the facility. Clients denied having seen anyone smoking or smelling smoke. Clients stated everyone was pretty much sober. Staff said they did not allow anyone to smoke in the home, and denied having smelled anything either. Staff did indicate that vape pens are seen on the client's person occasionally, but when seen, staff asks for the client to turn it in. In cases where a client did not surrender, then staff would allow them to go on, but wait for the client to leave the pen lying in plain sight or inside their laundry on laundry day to confiscate it. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violation did or did not occur, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. No deficiencies were cited during this inspection. Exit Interview conducted. A signed copy of this report, LIC9099-C, and LIC811 were provided to Henry Trochez, Administrator. Appeal rights provided.

narrative: LPA also reviewed pertinent STRTP records, Department databases, and reports from other agencies. The STRTP has two facility vehicles. LPA observed a small sedan, and a white Toyota minivan. LPA was shown the inside of both vehicles. Of note, the white Toyota minivan has capability for seating eight (8) passengers, with the first row consisting of two (2) bucket seats, the rear row consisting of a bench seat for three (3) passengers, and the middle row consisting of two (2) dedicated bucket seats and a fold down seat with seat belt attached to the bucket seats allowing for a third passenger. LPA observed the fold down seat to be cocked in an unusual way, and asked Administrator (A1) about it. A1 said seat was working and attempted to put the seat in place, but being unable to, actually pulled the seat off the hinges and told LPA, "Oh, I guess it 's broken." Interviews with clients (C1, C2, C4, C5) and staff (S1, A1) reveal knowledge of the seat being in disrepair, however LPA is unable to determine whether facility staff allowed clients to use broken seat during transport due to conflicting statements. Further investigation revealed that the facility van was taken to an auto shop on April 20, 2023, for a seat repair. However, the seat is a special order from the dealer and the part is on back order as stated in the work order. The work order was not provided to the LPA during the investigation. The STRTP also states that the facility has another vehicle which can be used to transport clients if additional seats are needed. Although one of the facility van seats is not in good repair, the facility took the van to the repair shop to obtain a work order. Based on the information gathered, although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violation did or did not occur, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. No deficiencies were cited during this inspection. Exit Interview conducted. A signed copy of this report, LIC9099-C, and LIC811 were provided to Shaderian Williams. Appeal rights provided.

narrative: It was alleged that minor had access to illegal drugs while in care and staff did not provide adequate supervision resulting in minor consuming hand sanitizer. The investigation revealed that the minor returned to the facility from being AWOL and appeared to be under the influence. The minor exhibited unusual behavior and later on asked staff to contact 911 after the minor started vomiting. The minor disclosed drinking hand sanitizer during AWOL. The minor was transported by emergency personnel to the hospital where the minor reported drinking hand sanitizer and using methamphetamines. It was discovered during confidential interviews that the minor obtained hand sanitizer from school and drank it inside the bedroom, after returning to the facility. There was no witness to the incident. The minor engaged in substance abuse while away from the facility and no one from the facility provided the minor with methamphetamines. Staff on duty responded appropriately by monitoring the minor's behavior after returning from AWOL and by immediately seeking medical attention for the minor. Based on the information gathered, the allegation of neglect/lack of supervision is unsubstantiated. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was not met. An exit interview was conducted, and copies of the following licensing reports were provided: LIC 9099, LIC 9099-C, LIC Confidential Names and Appeal Rights. There were no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

narrative: The staff members (S1, S2, and S3) refuted the accusations, asserting that they have no knowledge of, and C1 has not disclosed any information about being associated with adult females. They emphasized their active involvement with the clients, staying informed about each client's daily activities. The staff also assured that they would intervene when necessary to guide clients in adhering to and completing their program. Both the staff and support team stressed the significance of educating clients on condom availability and safe sex practices. They consistently remind clients about the dangers of unprotected sex and the risks of contracting sexually transmitted diseases. Regarding the drug use allegation, the staff explained that the facility implements measures to prevent contraband from entering, including conducting self-searches on clients and inspecting all bags. Despite these precautions, clients have succeeded in smuggling contraband by hiding items in areas not easily accessible to staff. If contraband is found, the staff will confiscate, document, and dispose of it appropriately. Information provided by C1 corroborated the aforementioned details, expressing a sense of security while residing at the facility and acknowledging the staff's assistance in achieving their individualized plan. C1 denied involvement with adult females or mistreatment of animals, stating that the only substances used were marijuana and alcohol during AWOL. C1 admitted to fabricating the claims to provoke a reaction from their teacher. Additionally, C1 mentioned that the facility staff are vigilant, conducting visual searches of items brought back to the facility and confiscating any contraband discovered. Therefore, based on the information received, the above allegation(s) is determined to be unsubstantiated. Although the allegation(s) may have happened are valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred, therefore the allegations are found to be unsubstantiated. Appeal Rights were provided and discussed with the STRTP Facility Manager. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time. On 4/24/24, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins conducted a case management visit. LPA met with Administrator George Jordan and Executive Assistant Betheny Jordan and informed of the purpose of the visit. During an investigation at the facility, LPA became aware of deficiencies and areas in which technical support may be beneficial. Based on confidential observations, interviews, and record review, the licensee revised the plan of operation without providing to the licensing agency for review and approval prior to implementation. LPA is issuing a citation of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section Plan of Operation. Additionally, the licensee indicated in the revised plan of operation that per county, state, and team recommendations, the facility "holds sole responsibility" for visitation procedure changes. LPA advises that per the above cited ILS section, the facility must submit revised plan of operation procedures to the licensing agency for approval. LPA discussed that approval should be obtained prior to implementation. LPA also advised that individual visitation, transportation, and other service plans, and any modifications, be documented in the resident's needs and services plan and that, per ILS Section 87068. Modifications to the Needs and Services Plan, the facility ensure written approval of such modifications is obtained from the authorized representative(s) prior to implementation. Lastly, a transportation arrangement to a resident's medical appointment was made and when the assigned staff member could not provide transportation that day, an on-call staff member or other staff was not made available to ensure transportation. LPA advised that, per ILS Section Transportation, the facility is to ensure transportation to health related services, so to avoid missing future appointments, utilization of on-call staff is encouraged. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report left with Executive Assistant Betheny Jordan.

On 06/10/24, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Celeste Aparicio and Kristin Pierotti conducted a facility evaluation visit for a case management regarding an observed deficiency from a complaint investigation; control number 14-CR-20240506113008. LPA met with Facility Manager and informed on the purpose of the visit. During the investigation, confidential interviews and records review were conducted. Based on interviews, record review, and observation the following deficiency was discovered regarding background clearance for staff member S1. (See LIC811) LPA observed S1 to be working at the facility on 05/08/24. Upon LPA's arrival at the facility on 05/08/24, LPA observed S1 exiting the facility vehicle from the driver's seat. During records review conducted on 06/04/24, LPA observed the initials of an unknown staff member on the facility transportation log starting from 03/25/24 to 05/20/24. LPA also did not observe S1 on be on the LIC500. During a confidential interview, LPA learned S1 was still in training. Upon further review, LPA observed that S1's criminal background clearance with facility is in pending status. Therefore, S1 has been working at the facility since 03/25/24 without a criminal background clearance associated to the facility. LPA is issuing a citation of California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 1, Article 3, Section Criminal Record Clearance, Subsection (e). Additionally, pursuant to Subsection (g) of this regulatory section, LPA is assessing an immediate civil penalty of one hundred dollars ($100) per violation (1) for a maximum of 5 days, for a total of five hundred dollars ($500). See attached LIC 809-D and LIC 421. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was provided to Facility Manager, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

Paramedics were contacted, but when C1 regained consciousness and was informed that emergency services had been called, C1 became upset and AWOLed from the facility. Paramedics and a clinician searched for C1, who was located on the same block returning to the facility. C1 was evaluated by paramedics, vitals were checked, and C1 was cleared to return to the facility. During the visit, LPA interviewed the Administrator to obtain additional information regarding the facility's plan to ensure C1 follows the safety plan discussed in the Child and Family Team (CFT) meeting and updated needs and services plan to address alcohol consumption. The Administrator stated: "We do bed checks routinely every hour. We can't control what she does off-site. She is working daily with her clinician but continues to decline all medication. We requested that she be placed in a higher level of care." Additionally, LPA discussed with the Administrator the proper procedure for documenting incidents involving law enforcement contact. LPA provided the Administrator with the LIC 624-LE form for reference, as well as PIN 23-02-CRP and PIN 17-04-CRP. No deficiencies were observed or cited during this inspection. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report was provided to Maria Castaneda, Youth Advocate.

On Friday May 13, 2022 at 11: AM Regional Manager, Nelson Martinez, Licensing Program Managers (LPM's) Carolyn Flynn, Helga Wong and Isabel Mendoza conducted an office meeting virtually via Microsoft Teams. Community Care Licensing (CCL) met JR Northstar I Administrator, Rachel McCormick and Consultant, Tricca Leverenz. Tandreya Jackson was unable to attend. A copy of this report was emailed to the facility for signature.

narrative: On May 6, 2021, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Regina Martin conducted a Case - Management Incident inspection to deliver and discuss findings from the Department's Investigation on self- reported incident received July 21, 2020. LPA met with Facility Representatives, Shannon Walling, Facility Manager and Andrea Espinosa Senior Facility Manager and together discussed investigation details. On July 21, 2020, Community Care Licensing received an incident report from facility representatives reporting that Staff member #1 (S1) contributed marijuana to minors. The incident was referred and assigned to Investigations Bureau, Investigator, Dennis Douglas. The investigation revealed, according to gathered information from independent interviews and review of corresponding records including incident reports and reports from the Ventura County Police Department, S1 provided and smoked marijuana with several of the clients at the facility. The marijuana was provided by S1 to the clients in the form of a "wax pen" and a "pipe". Sources revealed the encounters would occur outside of the facility during "walks" or while S1 was in the facility vehicle with the clients. S1 admitted to Investigator Douglas that she provided and smoked marijuana with the minor clients. Confidential independent interviews with clients residing in the facility at the time, further corroborate claims as some residents admitted to smoking marijuana out of S1's "wax pen" with S1 on several occasions and S1's "pipe" on at least one occasion. Upon discovery of said incident, S1 was terminated from her position at the facility. Facility representatives notified all required parties and conducted an internal investigation pertaining to the incident. (Continued on pg. Lic809d) Corrections concerning facility policy and procedures pertaining to this incident were reviewed and updated as necessary. Based on gathered information there is corroborating evidence to support reports of S1 contributing marijuana to minors. S1's actions towards clients poses an immediate health, safety and personal rights risk to children placed in care. The facility is issued a citation in accordance with Health and Safety code HSC 1558 (a)(2) Conduct inimical. See page 809D for deficiency. Exit interview conducted; Appeal Rights issued. A copy of this report was emailed to Facility Representatives.

narrative: The investigation revealed C1 was first placed August 18, 2021 with a history of anxiety, depression and prior suicide ideation without a plan. Confidential interviews and review of records indicates C1 was planning to graduate from facility's program and high school. On November 12, 2021, C1 appeared to be in a good mood and was last seen alive approximately 15 to 20 minutes before being found unresponsive. On November 12, 2021 at approximately 1: PM, Staff member found C1's bedroom door barricaded with a dresser. The door was pushed open and C1 was found partially suspended by a black cable cord secured to dresser drawers. Resuscitative efforts were begun, 911 emergency was called, and C1 was transported to a hospital where C1 was subsequently pronounced dead. Witness statements obtained indicate C1 appeared to be in a positive mood on the morning of the incident and showed no obvious signs of distress, plans to harm self or plans to commit suicide. Ventura County Police Department responded to the incident and found there was no crime committed. Ventura County Medical Examiner Investigator determined no suspicions of foul play regarding the incident. Based on gathered information obtained, there is not enough evidence to prove C1's untimely passing resulted from questionable death, but rather by suicide by hanging self from a closet drawer in their room. The findings are deemed Unsubstantiated. There are no deficiencies cited per California Code of regulations at this time. Exit Interview conducted. A copy of this report, LIC811 and appeal rights are provided to Facility Representative.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Marla Horne conducted a case management via telephone with the facility social worker. The case management was to follow up on incident reports dated 9-13-20 and 9-15-20. It was reported on 9-13-20 that a youth (C1) had gotten into the medicine safe as well as the sharp knives drawer. C1 was able to get into the safe because she had seen the PIN number as a staff person opened the safe while C1 was in the staff office. C1 was able to access a sharp knife when the drawer was unlocked during a meal preparation. C1 threatened to harm herself and was transported to a hospital to be assessed for a 5150 hold. C1 was released later that evening (9-13-20) and returned to the facility. On 10/20/22, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility for a case management inspection. LPA met with Administrator Sonam Prasad and informed of the purpose of the visit. The Licensing agency was informed that the facility caught a staff member on camera footage smoking marijuana on facility grounds. Based on record review and interview with Administrator, the staff member continued to work their shift after smoking marijuana, there were three residents present at this time, and one staff lead working with the staff. The facility had faced some challenges with the staff prior, provided the staff member additional training, and when other staff reported a concern that the staff member had smelled like marijuana one day when they were on shift, the Administrator spoke to the staff member about this less than a month prior and sent a follow-up email. Once the facility became aware of the incident, by seeing the facility camera footage, the staff member was directed to not come to their shift and instead report to the office. The staff member was to be terminated. However, the staff member resigned before showing to the office. LPA reviewed and obtained copies of staff records, including the follow-up email and staff training documentation. Per Administrator, the smoking policy is to not smoke on the premises, inside or outside, and this covers all substances. Staff are not to be intoxicated in any way on their shifts. Apart from onboarding training that all staff receive, no training or reminder about smoking and intoxication has been provided to the staff yet following this incident, but a staff meeting is planned for today, and Administrator agreed to include this as a topic. LPA is issuing a citation of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section Buildings and Grounds and a citation of California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Section Responsibility for Providing Care and Supervision. See attached LIC 809-D. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was provided to Administrator Sonam Prasad, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

On 2/17/23, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins conducted a facility evaluation visit for a case management regarding observed deficiencies. LPA met with Administrator Sonam Prasad and informed of the purpose of the visit. During an investigation at the facility, LPA conducted confidential interviews with staff, residents, and witnesses and review of facility records. Through this, the following was learned and/or observed. The facility does not have a facility manager designated for each shift. Per the plan of operation (POO), "At least one staff member each shift shall be designated as Facility Manager. When the House Manager is working a shift, he is considered the Facility Manager for that shift." Per applicable licensing requirements, there shall be a facility manager present whenever the administrator is absent and children are present, including the night shift. Currently, the facility has one designated facility manager, who is also not fully qualified, and who does not work the night shift. LPA is issuing a citation of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section Personnel Requirements. The facility admitted a youth without consulting with the full team as indicated in the POO, and only provided 1-2 days of notice of the intake. Per the POO, "When possible, the intake interview will include the La Cheim STRTP psychiatric nurse as well as the La Cheim STRTP Program Administrator... Emergency Placements are discussed with our Program Director who will then consider the case and consult with our Psychiatric Team before giving a decision on intake." A recently admitted youth was admitted without consultation with the CCL approved administrator and without the psychiatric team. LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section Plan of Operation. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights were discussed and provided, and a copy of this report was provided to Administrator Sonam Prasad, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

met_with: Head of Services Dae'Jah Foster; Administrator Sonam Prasad
narrative: On 3/9/23, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility to review and discuss plans of corrections (POCs). LPA met with Head of Services Dae'Jah Foster and Administrator Sonam Prasad and informed of the purpose of the visit. The POCs were developed and agreed upon on 2/17/23 for five citations issued on that day, under an LIC 809 and a LIC 9099, both dated 2/17/23. The due date for all POCs was 3/3/23. Submissions were received for 3, and 2 were missing. After the due date, licensee made a request for an extension but did not specify for what or until when. On 3/8/23, a complete request was received. Due to being past the initial due date, the extension is not being granted. At visit, LPA confirmed that the 2 missing POCs were incomplete. These were Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87022(f), due to not following intake procedures outlined in the plan of operation, and Section 87065(f) due to not having facility manager coverage during administrator absence. LPA is assessing two civil penalties for failure to correct, each of $100 per day beginning 3/4/23 and continuing until complete, for a total of $600 each as of today. LPA emphasizes that POCs should be submitted by tomorrow to avoid continuing fees. Additionally, during review of the LIC POC requiring training on consequences, LPA observed that the submitted training slides included discussion of a 10-day consequence for returning after curfew where home visits would be prohibited for 6-9 days. LPA confirmed this has been implemented as a consequence, although it has only recently been implemented for curfew violations. However, the plan of operation (Section 17 of the program statement) states that "discipline will not be used to deny home visits." LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section Plan of Operation as well as assessing a civil penalty for repeat violation of $250, as this section was previously cited on 2/17/23. LPA also advises that per STRTP ILS Section 87072, denying home visits without a court order is personal rights violation, so this policy would not be approved. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report left with Head of Services.

Lastly, per applicable licensing requirements and the POO, the facility manager shall have either a bachelor's degree or two years of experience working with the population to be served or equivalent. When hired in October 2022, the facility manager had five months of experience as a direct care staff at the facility. The facility manager had multiple years of experience working with populations outside of the age range and care needs / behavioral backgrounds of the facility population. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the allegation "Facility Manager not qualified" is found to be substantiated. investigation_findings: 13On 2/17/23, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins conducted a complaint investigation visit to deliver findings. LPA met with Administrator Sonam Prasad and informed of the purpose of the visit. The investigation consisted of confidential interviews with staff, residents, and witnesses and review of relevant facility records. Based on LPA's investigation, there have been multiple observations among staff and residents of inappropriateness from staff member(s), including wearing inappropriate clothing, inappropriate interactions with clients, and bias/favoritism. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the allegation "Staff being inappropriate with clients" is found to be substantiated. Additionally, based on LPA's investigation, both the Head of Service and Facility Manager are not qualified. The Head of Service may be filling the role as listed in the facility plan of operation (POO), based on review of applicable requirements and the POO, of the Social Worker/Clinical Coordinator or the Program Director. narrative: Based on confidential interviews, the food supply was less than the required amount to meet the needs of the residents in care, including an empty refrigerator in the kitchen. Additionally, at least one resident has purchased their own food and keeps their own food supply in their room and has done so after requesting staff purchase preferred foods and those foods not being obtained and/or prepared. LPA observed the facility to require cleaning and multiple repairs. Outside, LPA observed trash and contraband in the side yard, including an empty water jug, two empty cigarette packs, and one lighter with lighter fluid. LPA removed the cigarette packs and lighter and handed to Administrator for disposal. LPA observed a broken support beam under the back deck that had swung to the ground. Downstairs, LPA observed the bathroom toilet roll holder to be missing with a large screw exposed. The bathroom light switch cover was loose with a loose nail. The dressers in both downstairs bedrooms had missing drawer knobs and sharp screws exposed where the knobs would screw on. In one of the downstairs bedrooms, there is a heavily stained mattress with a hole in it, which Administrator stated would be replaced. The window screens were torn, and the curtain rod was pulled from the wall fixture. Upstairs, LPA observed a dresser with no drawer knobs, resulting in difficulty opening the drawers. There were two large holes in the wall of one of the bedrooms, graffiti on a ceiling beam, on the window, on the dresser, and on the front and back of the door. The graffiti on the door included gang-related symbols/lettering and profanity that speaks negatively of the facility and specific staff members. The door frame is also broken. There is currently a resident in this room, and Administrator stated the graffiti and holes were caused by a former resident and that the current resident moved into the room with this damage present. Administrator stated that the resident cannot be moved to one of the vacant bedrooms downstairs due to a runaway risk. When LPA arrived, there were two residents and one staff, Administrator. One of the residents is a known runaway risk. Staffing should be increased to provide extra supervision and meet this resident's needs. Administrator provided evidence of their correspondence with licensee on getting these issues addressed. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the above allegations are found to be substantiated. LPA is issuing citations of California Code of Regulations, Title 22, sections 80087 and 80088 and Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards sections 87076 and 87065.5. narrative: The allegation that facility staff did not ensure that C1 participates in school is related to C1 not attending schooling since October 2020. While the facility staff interviewed stated that they witnessed C1 logging in virtually and engaging in school, regularly. Staff reported that they witnessed C1 completing school work and engaging with teachers while logged on. Facility staff states that C1 was in attendance almost daily and states that despite being in attendance, the facility would get calls daily about not attending school. Staff states that they even called the school office in hopes to rectify the situation but the daily calls continued to be received. CSW states that C1 missing that many days and not being in school is not true. CSW states that C1's school was in direct contact with CSW and had CSW's email but CSW was not notified of any concerns about this prolonged absence(s) from school. LPA sent emails to C1's school requesting information related to C1's attendance 4/9/21 and 8/24/21 and no information was received. LPA was also informed when attempting to contact the school that LPA is not authorized to receive this information without written consent or court order. The allegation that S1 utilized an improper restraint is a result of C1 reporting that C1 was not allowed to leave the staff office when C1 wanted to and that S1 placed themselves between C1 and the exit door. C1 reported that S1 blocked C1 in the staff office and denied C1 the ability to leave the office when C1 wanted to exit. C1 could not recall when this happened. There are no witnesses found and no incident reported that would indicate when this allegation happened or if it happened. S1 denied that C1 was ever blocked in the staff office and prevented to leave at any time. As a result of the investigation and interviews conducted, LPA Hill finds that the allegations that facility staff did not provide minor adequate supervision, facility staff did not ensure that minor participates in school and facility staff utilized an improper restraint are UNSUBSTANTIATED at this time meaning that the allegation may have happened or is valid, but there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred. Exit interview conducted with Ms. Johnson and documents were provided.
investigation_findings: 13Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Tamara Hill made an unannounced tele inspection on 8/27/21 at 10: AM and met with Yoldanda Johnson, Administrator to discuss findings of the complaint allegations as stated. LPA was also provided with C1's Needs and Services Plan and staff contact information. The allegation that facility staff did not provide adequate supervision is related to C1 leaving on an unauthorized absence and staff not shadowing or looking for C1. Incident report received 4/3/21 indicates that C1 did go on an unauthorized absence 3/27/21. After C1 did not return on their own "after giving C1 time", and C1 could not be located in the area, law enforcement was contacted and a missing persons report was filed. CSW stated that they were aware that the facility would give C1 time to calm down and did sometimes follow but not always due to the availability of staff to do this. CSW stated that C1 would usually return on their own after calming down. CSW stated that there was no formal plan related to this time away in the Needs and Services Plan. narrative: On 12/22/ Licensing Program Analysts (LPA's) Jean Stidman and Maignacia Villapudua-Soto conducted a Pre-Licensing Inspection via FaceTime with Yolanda Johnson, Executive Director, and Reverend Randolph Johnson, Sr, .Administrator. LPA's observed the home is a two story five bedroom and three bathroom home. Three bedrooms are used for the clients and two for staff offices. The clients rooms have two beds in each room and two dressers. Two bedrooms have one desk and one bedroom has two desks for the clients. One bathroom downstairs is for staff and two bathrooms upstairs are for clients. All three bathrooms did not have paper towels. LPA observed staff put paper towels in all three bathrooms. The facility has a visitor sign-in sheet, hand sanitizer, temperature check log inside the front entrance. The medications are kept locked in the downstairs office inside a locked file cabinet. The facility has one 'no touch' thermometer that is in the downstairs office. The kitchen sink has paper towels and a bottle of dish soap available for hand-washing. The facility has at least two days supply of perishable and seven days of non-perishable food. The facility has two refrigerators and four freezers full of food. The laundry room, staff offices, staff bathroom, and downstairs closet were locked. The garage has extra cleaning supplies in a cabinet and the hall closet upstairs has extra hygiene supplies that are locked. The backyard has chairs and a punching bag for the clients. The facility has three fire extinguishers that have been serviced within the last 12 months. The facility has two vans. The main van has gloves, hand sanitizer, a mileage log and both vehicles started. The vehicles only have one first aid kit that must be moved between vehicle use. The facility has three clients in placement and three staff were at the facility. LPA's recommended the bedrooms with one desk be sanitized between client use, paper towels be available for use in all the bathrooms, a soap dispenser is available for use at the kitchen sink, the facility obtain an additional first aid kit for the backup van and the facility place extra face masks in the vehicles. The facility will be a granted provisional Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) license effective 12/22/2020 with conditions.

New direct care staff shall complete a minimum of 24 hours of initial training within 90 days of hire. Training shall include oversight and monitoring of psychotropic medications. The file review for staff S1, S2, S3, S4 shows the only time staff were trained on psychotropic medication was on 2/2/21. All four staff have been employed more than 90 days. Facility cited for violation of STRTP ILS 87070(b)(12) Children's Records. A separate log for each psychotropic medication prescribed to a child documenting all of the following: (B) The date of the prescription, (C) The quantity of medication and number of refills initially prescribed, (D) When applicable, any additional refills prescribed, (G) Documentation of each refusal shall include the reason for the refusal. Record review of the Medication Dispensing Logs (MAR) for clients C1, C2 and C3 are missing the date of prescription and number of refills.
