On Friday 9/24/21, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) for an annual continuation inspection. LPA met with Administrator Nina Davis and informed of the purpose of the visit. There were no children present during today's visit. The inspection was initiated on Tuesday 9/21/21. Refer to LIC Facility Evaluation Report, dated 9/21/21. LPA used the Inspection Tool to conduct the inspection. LPA inspected the facility site, conducted interviews with all present staff and residents, and reviewed current staff and client files, including files for recently discharged resident and staff who recently left facility. The facility was observed to be safe and free of immediate hazards. There are no firearms on the premises, per Administrator. Chemicals and medications are properly stored and inaccessible to residents. Medication administration is logged correctly and, based on staff interviews, medication administration procedures are thorough and followed correctly. Facility is maintained at a comfortable temperature. Residents report that the program provides a supportive environment. The facility is operating in accordance with their license. Staff have background clearances and are associated to the facility. The following concerns were observed: LPA observed the following: Sliding door handle broken; curtain rod over sliding door needs to be drilled back into the wall; large tear in living room sofa with stuffing spilling out; broken microwave door and handle; 3 bedroom doors are broken and/or have large holes, and 1 of those doors does not close due to damage; 4 holes in walls upstairs that have not been repaired; lights in the large bedroom's en-suite bathroom were non-functioning, including the toilet room light. Some items are pre-existing, and LPA was advised they would be fixed soon, so the repairs are still in-progress. Damages at site are not determined to cause an immediate risk to residents. LPA issued a citation of Title 22, Section Buildings and Grounds. LPA observed that the needs and services plans for resident R1, R2, and R3 (Refer to LIC Confidential Names, dated 9/24/21) were not available on site for review. LPA was informed by clinician that a needs and services had not been updated for resident R1 since the pre-placement. R1 was placed on 7/2/21. LPA issued a citation of STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87068. Modifications to the Needs and Services Plan. Needs and services plans should be updated every 30 days, noting any progress in the youth's case plan and can provide an opportunity to document what, if any, information from outside agencies is still being obtained. LPA observed that documentation of successful completion of training was not maintained in the personnel record for each staff. LPA is unable to verify training and that all hours of initial training and the 40 hours of annual training have been completed if not properly documented/logged. Current records do not reflect that all training was met, including for staff S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, and S6. LPA issued a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87065. Training Requirements. LPA observed that the facility has developed and is using a clearly organized chart for initial training that could be adapted for documenting annual training. LPA observed that the hot water in the upstairs hallway bathroom measured at a high of 154. F, which exceeds the permitted ranged. A hot water warning notice was posted at the sink, complying with Title 22, Section Furniture, Fixtures, Equipment, and Supplies. LPA advises that the facility continue to monitor the hot water temperature at vanity sinks and adjust hot water settings as necessary to ensure temperatures do not go above F. Three citations and one advisory were issued at this visit. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was provided to Administrator Nina Davis, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

Licensing Program Analyst Britanee Windom conducted a case management inspection on 03/15/22 at 9: AM based on the number of relevant law enforcement contacts reported by the facility, pursuant to Health and Safety Code section 1538.7. During this inspection, 10 out of Direct Care Staff and 3 out of 3 youth files were reviewed. 4 out of Direct Care Staff and 3 out of 3 youth were interviewed. (See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, March 15, 2022). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Minutes from the board of directors' meetings related to the facility's incidents involving contact with law enforcement were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments, quarterly assessments, and crisis intervention plans, the licensee uses trauma informed and evidence based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. LPA Windom observed documentation of completed training on policies and procedures on when and how to involve law enforcement in response to an incident. Training records show staff have been trained on Emergency Intervention as required. The licensee is contacting law enforcement in accordance to their Emergency Intervention Plan when there is an immediate risk of serious harm to a child or others. There are no deficiencies cited at this time. A copy of this report was discussed and provided to Administrator Davis.

On 4/20/22 at 3PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility regarding deficiencies that were discovered during an investigation at the facility. LPA met with Administrator Nina Davis and informed of the purpose of the visit. Safety precautions were taken, including mask-wearing and screening call. The investigation was conducted by the Investigations Branch. During investigation, confidential interviews were conducted with residents, staff, and authorized representative, and police report was reviewed. Based on interviews and record review, the following deficiencies were found. Staff S1 (See LIC Confidential Names, dated 4/20/22) used a disallowed restraint technique, by placing resident R1 in a prone restraint, per the program statement emergency intervention plan, which states, "Interventions Never to Be Used... Prone restraint, unless written authorization has been provided by the youth's physician, based upon their prior physical examination of the youth." Based on file review, the facility did not obtain such written authorization documentation, as R1 was not in placement long enough to get a medical and physical assessment. Additionally, the file contains a Health & Education Passport, dated 12/28/21, that lists asthma as one of R1's conditions, which is listed as a risk factor in prone restraints in the Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87095. Emergency Intervention Prohibitions. LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87022(f) Plan of Operation. During the prone restraint, R1 placed R1's own hands behind their back, and S1 held R1's hands down to keep R1 down in the restraint, as witnessed by S2, and by doing so held R1 in a prohibited restraint. LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section Section 87095.01(a)(5) Emergency Interventions Prohibition, which specifically prohibits the use at any time of any restraint that places a child in a prone position with their hands behind their back. LPA also advises, per STRTP ILS Section 87095.66(c) that any restraint requiring two staff, such as prone restraints, must be performed with two staff. Additionally, at visit LPA inspected the personnel record for S1 and found there was no intervention training certificate. The program statement indicates the facility will use Pro-Act, but Administrator stated the facility does not perform restraints. The personnel record does not reflect that S1 was properly trained and certified prior to using the restraint technique, and S1 and Administrator confirmed that S1 has not been trained since working with licensee's facilities. LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87095.65(a) Emergency Intervention Staff Training. It was also learned during the investigation, based on S1's statements, that S1 made statements to R1 such as, "This is the best home you'll ever be in, don't mess it up." This statement does not align with supported trauma-informed care practices and is emotionally abusive in nature. Staff statement that R1 is "bad for business" also indicates an inappropriate attitude toward R1. LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87072(c)(11) Personal Rights. Lastly, the incident report submitted by licensee and written by staff S1 for the incident during which S1 performed the prone restraint does not include information about the restraint. As such, Administrator stated she was unaware that a restraint had been performed. The incident report is also lacking detail of the events, does not indicate when staff notified law enforcement or what items were damaged, and includes language (i.e. "verbal judo") that Administrator is unfamiliar with and cannot verify as part of the progam's intervention plan. LPA is issuing a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87095.61(a) Documentation and Reporting Requirements. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Administrator Nina Davis, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

narrative: On Tuesday, September 14, 2021 at 9:54AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility for a required annual inspection. LPA met with Administrator Nina Davis and informed of the purpose of the visit. LPA used the Inspection Tool to complete the annual inspection. LPA toured the facility site and observed the facility to be clean and sanitary. Administrator informed LPA that the facility plans to get a new dusting rod to remove a hanging web/dust web in the entry way and to haul the old mattresses currently stored in the garage to the dump. Commonly touched services are sanitized regularly. Pool in backyard has a pool cover. Per Administrator, there are no firearms on the premises. Sharps and medications are stored in the locked closet in the entryway. First aid kit is stored centrally. Scissors and tweezers are missing from the first aid kit. Bedrooms are tidy, residents have individual beds, and beds have clean linens. The room temperature and hot water temperature measured within permitted ranges, at F and 114. F, respectively. The kitchen was in sanitary condition with functioning equipment and dishware, cookware, and utensils to meet the needs of residents in care. Food storage was sanitary, food was fresh and in date, and there was food storage to meet the 7-day nonperishable, 2-day perishable mandate. LPA reviewed all client files and staff files. Staff files were complete, and training record shows that the facility has been conducting trainings in 2021. Per Administrator, who is new in this position, the 2020 training record has not been found yet. 2019 training was complete for staff who were working at the facility that year. 1 file had a first aid certificate that was expired by just under a month, but the refresher training had been conducted, and the certificate needed to be placed in the file. 1 file for new hire was missing health screening, but the doctor visit to complete this was scheduled and evidence of the appt being scheduled was in file. [] Client files were mostly complete. See LIC Confidential Names for the following: - The file for R1 was missing or had incomplete: Identification/Emergency Info (LIC 601); Personal Rights (LIC 613B); Cash resources (LIC 405); and Physician's Report w/ TB Test (LIC 602). NOTE: R1 was placed a few days ago on 9/10/21. - The files for R2, R3, and R4 were missing: Personal Rights (LIC 613B). LPA issued 2 advisories per California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Section Health Related Services and STRTP Interim Licensing Standards Personal Rights. No citations were issued. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report left with Administrator Nina Davis, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

On Thursday 2/3/22 at 9:16AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility to review training records, per the agreement established at the Noncompliance Conference on 9/23/21. The agreed upon terms were that the licensee would be subject to increased monitoring for at least 12 months and the licensee is to conduct monthly trainings on any of these topics: trauma-informed care practices, safe vehicle operation, proper de-escalation procedures when following residents in a vehicle, and firearm storage and safety. LPA met with Administrator Nina Davis and informed of the purpose of the visit. LPA also spoke to Assistant Director La Tanya Harper over the phone to discuss the report. Safety precautions were taken, including LPA wearing an N95 mask, hand hygiene and gloves, and screening call. LPA reviewed the training binder, training logs, and training certificates and obtained copies of the training logs. LPA observed the following: 1) Staff S1, S2, and S3 (See LIC Confidential Names) have not attended a training on firearms, per the logs. LPA advises that a make-up training be held for these staff members. 2) The AWOL Procedures training covered safe vehicle operation, based on the training materials previously provided to LPA, but the training log does not clearly reflect this, and the materials were not available in the binder due to being stored at the administrative office location. LPA advises that, since the requirement to have trainings on safe vehicle operation is in response to a staff member's unsafe operation of a vehicle during an AWOL incident, the materials be available for review at the facility site to verify for anyone reviewing the logs that it covered safe vehicle operation and/or that another all-staff training be conducted that specifically covers safe vehicle operation and is titled to reflect that. The training log is otherwise complete, and the licensee is in compliance. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator Nina Davis and Assistant Director La Tanya Harper over the phone. There are no citations. A copy of this report was provided to Administrator Nina Davis, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

Licensing Program Analyst Britanee Windom conducted a case management inspection on 05/12/22 at 9: AM based on the number of relevant law enforcement contacts reported by the facility, pursuant to Health and Safety Code section 1538.7. During this inspection, 6 out of Direct Care Staff and 1 out of 1 youth files were reviewed. 2 out of Direct Care Staff and 1 out of 1 youth were interviewed.(See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, May 12, 2022). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Minutes from the board of directors' meetings related to the facility's incidents involving contact with law enforcement were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments, monthly assessments, and crisis intervention plans, the licensee uses trauma informed and evidence based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. LPA Windom observed documentation of completed training on policies and procedures on when and how to involve law enforcement in response to an incident. Training records show staff have been trained on Emergency Intervention as required. The licensee is contacting law enforcement in accordance to their Emergency Intervention Plan when there is an immediate risk of serious harm to a child or others. There are no deficiencies cited at this time. A copy of this report was discussed and provided to Administrator Nina Davis.

On 6/30/22 at 2:55PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility to review training records, per the agreement established at the Noncompliance Conference on 9/23/21. The agreed upon terms were that the licensee would be subject to increased monitoring for at least 12 months and the licensee is to conduct monthly training on any of these topics: trauma-informed care practices, safe vehicle operation, proper de-escalation procedures when following residents in a vehicle, and firearm storage and safety. The 4PM shift's staff were also not facility managers. R1's roommate reported R1 left at 9:30PM and that staff were doing regular checks. S1 reported the last check in was at 11PM. It is possible that S1 called the advice nurse about the chest pain around the same time that S1 went upstairs and did the check ins, but it is also possible that due to their chest pain, S1 may not have been able to make it upstairs to check on youth. It is possible that a lack of supervision from either a lack of check ins or the delay in finding a replacement staff due to not having an on-call staff allowed for R1 to AWOL and travel to another city. R1 has a known history of being an AWOL risk and having relationships with older men. The issue with invading the youths' privacy is an understandable concern. However, if a youth is asleep, the only way to check on them is to have sight of them so you do not disturb their sleep. Morning staff reported a teddy bear was in the bed when they tapped the "body" and pulled the covers, so even if night staff had done a check in by sight, they still may not have realized the youth had left. It was reported that the reason there was no on-call staff designated in the absence of a facility manager was because staff were unwilling to for concerns of not being properly paid. LPA was not able to determine if this was the case. The only staff designated facility responsibility and on-call status at that time was S2. Further, the Director and Assistant Director could not be reached. However, S2 was responsive and did assist in finding a staff to take over the night shift. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, based on LPA's observations and interviews with residents and staff, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove the alleged violation did or did not occur. Therefore, the allegation is Unsubstantiated. LPA is issuing an advisory per California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Section 84065. Staff/Child Ratios. Additionally, LPA is issuing an advisory per Health and Safety Code Sections 1522.4(a). The facility has since been licensed as STRTP, but this incident occurred when facility was still a group home. LPA advises the facility review STRTP ILS Section 87065. Direct Care Staff/Child Ratios, as there are additional requirements regarding on-call staff for STRTPs. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report left with Assistant Director La Tanya Harper and Interim Administrator Rashell Conner, who agreed to sign the report emailed by LPA Hawkins and return a signed copy to LPA.

R1 removes self from the vehicle, and as R1 steps off and away from the vehicle, the vehicle is propelled forward about a foot at approximately 5- MPH. R1's body is very close to the vehicle, and R1's hand is either still on the vehicle or had just been removed. From the driver's side, from where the video is shot, it is not clear that R1 would not be hit by the vehicle. However, R1 does not show signs of being hit. Individuals should not jump onto vehicles, and individuals should demonstrate extra caution when operating vehicles around others, especially if others are making attempts to place themselves on top of the vehicle. narrative: Staff did not call the police immediately for each time the resident left due to the resident following a pattern of returning within 15 to 60 minutes. Additionally, the resident was a known risk for unauthorized leaves, which the facility expressed concerns with to the resident's authorized representative, but the facility found 1:1 supervision inaffective for the resident due to the resident becoming agitated by increased staff monitoring and being near staff, resulting in 1:1 supervision being terminated for the resident. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the above allegation is found to be substantiated. Due to the known risk for unauthorized leaves and not reporting the leave(s) immediately to the police, per facility protocol, LPA is issuing a citation of California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Section Plan of Operation. See attached LIC 9099-D. LPA also advises that per Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87065.5, the facility shall increase the number of direct care staff when a resident requires special care and supervision due to behavior. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Assistant Administrator La Tanya Harper, whose signature on this form confirms receipt. Additionally, the resident was a known risk for unauthorized leaves, which the facility expressed concerns with to the resident's authorized representative, but the facility found 1:1 supervision ineffective for the resident due to the resident becoming agitated by increased staff monitoring and being near staff, resulting in 1:1 supervision being terminated for the youth. There is not sufficient information to determine if a violation led to the incident occurring. Additionally, based on confidential interviews and record review, drug use is not allowed in the facility, and it has either not been witnessed by some parties or staff have been observed to confiscate contraband when they become aware of it. The facility is reported to have a menu residents enjoy, staff make quality meals and accommodate residents' dietary needs and preferences, residents are able to make their own meals if they prefer, and the facility was observed to have a large store of healthy food. Further, based on confidential interviews, most residents report that staff do not bully and are not aggressive with residents. The specific documentation could not be clarified, and LPA was able to have access to medical documentation. However, LPA advises that the facility ensure medical documentation is accessible to care staff in case of an emergency so that medical information can be provided to authorized parties. Per the facility's program statement, "Transportation is provided to all youth/NMDs to school unless the youth/NMD prefers to walk to school in which in that case it is right for their age, developmental level, maturity and it's in their Needs and Service Treatment Plan," which was not followed. Further, Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section Transportation provides that facilities shall ensure transportation is provided to residents with any special arrangements agreed upon with the care team and documented in the needs and services. Based on confidential interviews and record review, staff perform room searches with two staff and the resident(s) present during the search. This policy/procedure is not listed in the facility program statement. Additionally, based on confidential interviews, multiple reports indicated that staff have made inappropriate comments and spoken inappropriately of or with residents, including referring to resident as nasty for making a mess and discussing a resident and their personal matters around or with other residents. One of these staff is no longer employed by the licensee. Based on confidential interviews, staff did open a resident's expected mailed ID in order to make a copy of it and has done this before. However, it is not a policy or a trend that staff will open residents' mail, and no mail is withheld from residents. Staff do request that residents open packages in front of staff in order to log it on residents' inventory list and to ensure the item is not dangerous or contraband. Resident reports indicate this has not been an issue for residents. However, this is not listed in the facility program statement, and residents have a right to confidentiality in the mail they receive. Lastly, based on confidential interviews, a resident requested to be taken to the emergency room for pain, but staff did not agree to transport resident. Resident and a peer called 911, and when the ambulance arrived, staff spoke to the medics, who then left. Later that night, the resident again expressed their concern of their pain, and staff called the advice nurse, who advised the resident be taken to the emergency room, and the resident was transported by ambulance due to the late hour. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the above allegations are found to be substantiated. LPA is issuing citations of California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Sections Plan of Operation and Health Related Services and STRTP ILS Sections Transportation and Personal Rights. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Assistant Administrator La Tanya Harper, whose signature on this form confirms receipt. narrative: Licensing Program Analyst Britanee Windom conducted a case management inspection on 04/27/22 at 9: AM based on the number of relevant law enforcement contacts reported by the facility, pursuant to Health and Safety Code section 1538.7. During this inspection, 7 out of Direct Care Staff and 5 out of 5 youth files were reviewed. 4 out of Direct Care Staff and 5 out of 5 youth were interviewed.(See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, April 27, 2022). The Plan of Operation including policies and procedures were reviewed. Minutes from the board of directors' meetings related to the facility's incidents involving contact with law enforcement were reviewed. Based on the analysis of the confidential interviews and youth file review including the needs and service assessments, monthly assessments, and crisis intervention plans, the licensee uses trauma informed and evidence based de-escalation and intervention techniques when staff is responding to the behavior of a youth residing in the facility. Interviews with youth and staff indicate the licensee prohibits calls or threats to call law enforcement as a form of discipline. LPA Windom observed documentation of completed training on policies and procedures on when and how to involve law enforcement in response to an incident. Training records show staff have been trained on Emergency Intervention as required. The licensee is contacting law enforcement in accordance to their Emergency Intervention Plan when there is an immediate risk of serious harm to a child or others. There are no deficiencies cited at this time. A copy of this report was discussed and provided to Administrator Tracy McWoodson.

On 10/19/22, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins made a visit to the facility regarding an investigation at the facility, during which a deficiency was observed and is being cited today. LPA met with Administrator Tracy McWoodson and informed of the purpose of the visit. During record review, LPA observed that some medications were not administered for a few days due to needing to be filled, and one medication was potentially administered incorrectly or logged incorrectly. A medication, Aripiprazole, was prescribed at 1 1/2 tablets at bedtime for 15 days and filled on 2/18/22 with 1 refill, administered for 15 days, and then filled on 3/18/22 with 0 refills. The facility continued administering daily until they ran out after 4/10/22. If the medication was only to be administered for 15 days, administration should have stopped after 4/1/22, and at 1 1/2 (1+1/2) dosage, the facility would be out of the medication after 4/1/22. However, after filling the 3/18/22 prescription, the records reflect that staff notated the medication was not administered due to needing to be filled. It is not clear from the records when the medication was filled, if the listed reason is accurate, or if the medication was administered correctly. The resident is no longer in care, so a medication count cannot be conducted. LPA is issuing a citation of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section Health Related Services. See attached LIC 809-D. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Administrator Tracy McWoodson, whose signature confirms receipt.

narrative: On 1/9/23, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins conducted a case management visit at the facility. LPA met with Administrator Tracy McWoodson and Clinical Director Phyllis Ritter and informed of the purpose of the visit. On May 31, 2024 at 10: AM, an unannounced Psychotropic Medication Inspection was conducted by Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Shikya Belfield and Celeste Aparicio, pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 1538.9 (a)(2). This inspection is a continuation of the inspection that began on May 21, 2024, at 10: AM. LPA Belfield and Aparicio met with Administrator Tracy McWoodson who assisted with the inspection. During the previous inspection, LPA Belfield and LPA Aparicio met with Executive Director Assistant LaTonya Harper. Staff and client file reviews and interviews were conducted. During the client file review of the initial inspection, LPAs observed no documentation indicating the child has been participating or offered the opportunity to participate in the development of their Needs and Services Plan (NSP), and NSP not being updated every 30 days from the date the child was placed in the facility in three of the three client files. Additionally, LPAs observed no child and authorized representative signatures available on the NSP in three of the three client files. During today's inspection LPAs conducted a walk through of the facility, photos were taken during the walkthrough, reviewed client Psychotropic Administration Records (PMAR), reviewed Centrally Stored Medication Log (LIC622), and LPA's observed administrator conduct a pill count for each client. Based on observations made during the pill count and psychotropic medication documentation review, LPAs determined the following: the centrally stored medication log for each psychotropic medication is not properly documented to include the correct pill counts and number of refills prescribed; the document prescription numbers on the PMAR's and centrally stored log were incorrect for one of three clients files; Psychotropic medication was logged on a PRN form instead of the PMAR. LPAs are issuing citations for violations of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) sections 87068.2(d) Children's Record, 87068.3(a) Modifications to the Needs and Services Plan, and 87070(b)(14) Children's Records, as described on the following page LIC809-D. Regarding LPAs observations made, the NSP's did not have child and authorized representative signature. The licensee is being issued a Technical Violation Advisory Note: STRTP ILS, Section 87068.2(g) Needs and Services Plans. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights were provided, and a copy of this report was sent to with Administrator Tracy McWoods, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

investigation_findings: 13On Thursday 11/05/20 at 1PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins conducted a visit to deliver findings of a complaint investigation of the above allegation. LPA met with Assistant Director La Tanya Harper and Interim Administrator Tracy McWoodson. Due to COVID-19 social distancing orders, this visit was scheduled as a tele-visit. During the investigation, LPA Hawkins conducted confidential interviews with staff, social worker, and probation officer. Based on interviews and record review, following an incidence of aggression that resulted in an altercation involving each youth in placement at the time, the police were called for assistance and resident R1 (See LIC Confidential Names) was 5150'd and taken to the hospital. A probation officer who oversaw this case reported that Probation would not pick up R1 because R1 did violate probation. R1's social worker reported that the facility told the social worker that they refused to pick up R1 and bring back into care, because they felt that R1 was not fit for congregate care. The social worker suggested they do a 14-day notice, and the facility refused. SubstantiatedEstimated Days of Completion:

narrative: The needs and services plan dated 10/21/21 includes the following: "Transition Plan: [R1]'s current plan is to graduate high school and move back with her grandmother or transition to a county connected independent living program. The staff and counselors at Lighthouse Mentoring Center are supporting [R1]'s connection with her grandmother and guiding and educating her on the resources available through the Independent Living Program. Additionally, [R1] is working on developing other independent living skills, such as securing, and retaining employment, budgeting and managing her own transportation." The complaint report was filed on 10/20/21 in response to an incident that day. The transition plan was updated after the incident. Administrator informed LPA that the plan was not updated before because the plan to manage own transportation had been verbally discussed and agreed upon at a CFT. This was, though, before R1 changed schools. Additionally, the facility did not have a record of bus routes that R1 was to utilize to make their way home, and Administrator was unaware of what bus route R1 would need to take to get home to the facility, which is a safety concern. Based on LPA's review of local bus routes, the 9-minute car ride home would have taken R1 an average of 2 hours to get home by bus. The only route that would be quicker (but still 90 minutes) costs more than the amount of money R1 is provided to self-transport. Multiple routes require multiple transfers, and R1 is a known AWOL risk, per interview and record review. Staff are able to transport youth to work after school on days R1 works, but the facility does not have a schedule for R1's job, because the employer does not provide these to R1. However, staff availability indicates that staff are available to pick up the youth after school. Further, the route home from R1's previous school was about 37 to 44 minutes by bus. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the above allegation is found to be Substantiated. There is one citation. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Administrator Tracy McWoodson, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

narrative: Residents upstairs call for staff, both of whom are downstairs. S1, who was upstairs with the residents, had gone downstairs prior to the incident to use the restroom. S1 reported that S2 was made aware of this and was nearby downstairs with another resident but may not have been able to see the residents upstairs. S2 reported that S2 was not made aware that S1 was using the restroom and that S2 was in the kitchen area with the fifth resident in care. S2 responded when called by the residents. The lighter, and per staff statements, multiple lighters on multiple occasions, were confiscated from R3. However, due to lack of supervision, the lighter could not be confiscated at the time of the incident, the incident of R3 using a dangerous item could not be prevented or intervened, and R3's injury could not be prevented. Further, resident and staff statements indicate that staff interactions with youth are not always trauma-informed and that multiple staff members at times use an inappropriate and disrespectful tone with residents when delivering information or explaining consequences. When staff share information with residents, the tone, word choice, and body language are important in delivery of that information. Additionally, if a resident responds negatively to a staff statement, staff are responsible for ensuring they use trauma-informed care, per policy procedures, to calm the resident, communicate their intentions, and to maintain the relationship between staff and residents and the health and safety of the resident. Staff tone and attitude contribute significantly to the environment in the facility. narrative: During another incident, one resident was downstairs in the front living room on a phone call monitored by the staff on duty. Another resident was upstairs, unsupervised. The front living room is visible from the upstairs landing and hallway, but the main kitchen/dining/family room area is not visible from the front living room. The resident upstairs came downstairs, entered the main kitchen/dining/family room, and exited the facility through the back sliding door. This resident then returned about 5 minutes later with contraband not visible to staff, and returned upstairs. The investigation found that the call the resident was on was not a required supervised call but that staff observe the resident on the phone to ensure the resident does not make unapproved calls afterward, as the resident does have a list of calls that need to be approved and/or supervised. Later, both residents were in one of their bedrooms and shared the contraband, which was learned to be a can of alcohol and a nicotine vaporizer pen obtained by the resident who exited the facility from an adult not affiliated with the facility. Additionally, multiple reports obtained described supervision at the facility as relaxed or that staff are disengaged or distracted on their phones. The incident report submitted for this incident also did not reflect that engagement or redirection was done. Lastly, the staff could have been stationed upstairs and had sight of the resident on the phone or could have engaged with the resident who exited the facility and continued listening for a break in the phone discussion or for redialing, or the facility could have increased staffing to meet the extra supervision needs of the resident with required monitored phone use. Regarding the third allegation above, the reports obtained indicate that due to a lack of supervision allowing residents to enter other residents' rooms, multiple residents have had their personal belongings stolen by other residents, and sometimes those items have been destroyed, including clothing, a journal, and a family photo. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met, and therefore the above allegations are found to be substantiated. LPA is issuing citations of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS), section Plan of Operation and 87065. Personnel Duties. See attached LIC 9099-D. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Administrator Tracy McWoodson, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

On 9/30/21 at 10AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Mariah Hawkins conducted an annual inspection. LPA met with Administrator Maurice Jones and informed of the purpose of the visit. Safety precautions were taken including screening call and mask-wearing. The Inspection Tool was used to conduct the inspection. There are two residents in care. LPA interviewed present residents and staff. The facility is maintained at a comfortable temperature, and hot water at the upstairs resident bathroom measured within permitted range, at 111. F. The facility, per the tool, was in compliance in all areas other than those listed below, for which citations or advisories were issued. 1. Staff Ratios. During visit, two residents returned home, and there was only one staff (Administrator), and no additional staff showed at their arrival. LPA issued an advisory of STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87065.5(b)(1). 2. Staff Ratios. The current LIC Personnel Report indicates there is one overnight staff who works 12AM-8AM Monday through Friday and one overnight staff who works 12AM-8AM Saturday and Sunday. LPA issued a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87065.5(b)(2). 3. Needs and Services. Residents records contained needs and services plans that were not being updated every 30 days. R1's (See LIC Confidential Names, dated 10/7/21) plan was dated 5/28/21 and had a "re-evaluate" date of 7/21/21, and R2's plan was dated 8/22/21 and had a "re-evaluate" date of 11/22/21. LPA issued a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87068.3(a). 4. Smoking on Site. During tour of facility, LPA observed 10+ cigarette butts in the back and side yards. Per Administrator, staff are aware that residents are smoking in their rooms and throwing the cigarette butts out of the window. Staff are doing contraband checks, but cigarette butts have not been removed from grounds. LPA issued a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87087(c). 5. First Aid Certificates. LPA observed that 5 of 10 staff files reviewed [Refer to LIC Confidential Names for staff names] did not include a valid/current first aid certificate. LPA issued a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87065.1(c)(6)(A). 6. Staff Training. LPA observed that 9 of 10 staff files [Refer to LIC Confidential Names for staff names] did not contain training documentation. Some staff were missing all staff training and had no training record in the training binder. Some staff had the initial training log completely signed off. Staff work at multiple facilities, and LPA has prior knowledge that some staff have completed initial training based on copies of their files at other locations. However, the training records in the staff files at this site would indicate that less than 15 hours of training were completed in 2020. Additionally, there is a training record in staff files that indicates 20 hours were completed in 2021, completed over two days, with 10 hours done each day. The dates are 1/12/21 and 3/30/21. Per Asst. Director La Tanya Harper, these dates are the completion dates for mulitple days long training courses. There is no training material for this training in the record, breakdown of time spent on each topic or how the hours were calculated, nor a certificate. LPA issued a citation of STRTP ILS Section 87066(b)(4). 7. Bedroom Sharing Arrangement. LPA observed that the resident records do not contain documentation of the bedroom sharing arrangements. LPA issued an advisory per STRTP ILS Section 87087(e). 8. Condition of Site & Grounds. LPA observed minor damages, including a cracked microwave door, two fist sized holes (one in bedroom, one in upstairs hall), and cracked/punched doors to two bedrooms. Damages do not appear to cause an immediate risk, and all items are functioning. Administrator showed LPA a list of items, including these damages, that have been sent to the director for repairs but have not yet been repaired. Per Administrator, the licensee is taking steps to address these damages. The facility is otherwise in good condition. Additionally, LPA observed two bent and broken window screens in the side yard. Per Administrator, residents break these off of the windows in order to throw cigarette butts out. LPA observed the screens had not been removed from the side yard. The screens are made of metal, which can be bent and worked into a dangerous item. The screens also are in the walkway, and while light in weight, they are large and could obstruct the passageway in an emergency. LPA issued an advisory per STRTP ILS Section 80087(a). 9. Health Screenings. Two staff files were missing health screening with TB test. LPA issued an advisory of STRTP ILS Section 80066(a)(10). One staff does not work on site at this location. An exit interview was conducted, appeal rights provided, and a copy of this report was left with Administrator Maurice Jones, whose signature on this form confirms receipt.

LPA also discussed that the licensee should continue to provide hiring updates but that the ratio requirements must be followed following this incident to ensure compliance. Lastly, LPA discussed the process of reducing the capacity, since the facility does not typically go over 6 residents, and doing so would make the ratio requirement for this facility the same as that for the licensee's other facilities. LPA is issuing a citation of Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) section 87065. Direct Care Staff/Child Ratios. See attached LIC 809-D. On April 23, 2025, Community Care Licensing (CCL) conducted an office conference with the Short-Term Residential Treatment Program (STRTP) applicant Ashley Martinez regarding their application denials for LLU Joshua Place (366000017) and LLU Joshua Place 2 (366000035). Present at the meeting was: LaCresha Cook, Regional Manager (RM), Ashley Martinez, Executive Director (ED), Ann Valenzuela, Licensing Program Manager (LPM), Charmaine Linley, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) and Kimberly Abdul-Malik, Treasurer/Board Member, was present via cell phone. The meeting was called to address concerns regarding the applicants submission of an incomplete application and history of noncompliance. RM explained that CCL is denying the applicant's STRTP applications for both LLU Joshua Place (366000017) and LLU Joshua Place 2 (366000035). RM further explained that as of April 23, 2025, the STRTP applications would be officially denied. The denial of the application is based upon failure to provide satisfactory evidence that the applicant can meet or conform to the licensing requirements in Health and Safety Code Chapter 3, commencing with Section 1500; Title California Code of Regulations, Division 6, Chapter 1, commencing with Section 80000; and the CDSS Short-Term Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards ("ILS"). This decision is based on the evidence set forth in the reports, statements, and other documentary evidence contained in the official files compiled by the department. The applicant disagrees with the information shared in the meeting and states that 90% of the information is included in the pending revisions. Applicant states she feels she is being unfairly treated and plans to follow up this matter with the chain of command within the Community Care Licensing Division. *** RM informed that a denial notice will be sent to the applicant explaining all reasons for the application denial and provided in Health and Safety Code Section 1526, an applicant may appeal a denial by submitting a written appeal within 15 days after the licensing agency mails the denial notice. The appeal should include the facility name, facility number, facility address and a copy of the denial letter. The appeal must be post marked or delivered on or before 15 days from the date of the denial letter. RM explained that if this decision is not appealed on or before the due date the denial will be final. RM informed applicant that the appeal request is sent to the following address: Jean Chen, Program Administrator, Statewide Children's Residential Program Office, P Street, MS 9-14-880, Sacramento, CA 95814. A copy of this report was provided to Ashley Martinez. The signed report will be placed in the facility application file.

narrative: On September 17, 2025, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Jessica Peete and Cynthia Urena met with Makade Behavioral Center applicant Jorge Cervantes to complete Component II, the face-to-face interview, for the Short Term Therapeutic Residential Program (STRTP) application process. Also present were Board Secretary Imelda Cervantes and Chief Operations Officer Akila Crane, who attended via Microsoft Teams, and the prospective Administrator Laura Hartney. The applicant previously attended Component I, the STRTP orientation, on February 25, 2025. The purpose of today's meeting was to address any questions or concerns and to review the application packet and process, ensuring that the applicant, designated administrator, and all relevant parties understand and can provide the services outlined in the Program Statement and Plan of Operations in compliance with Community Care Licensing regulations. LPA reviewed the application documents, addressing and correcting discrepancies on the LIC Application for Community Care Facility and LIC Applicant Information. Policies and procedures submitted as part of the application, including discipline policies, program description, population to be served, and personal rights, were also reviewed. The facility staff plan was discussed to ensure compliance. The applicant does not yet have direct care staff but stated that a temporary staffing plan is in place. LPA reminded the applicant of the required staff-to-client ratios and reviewed the relevant regulations outlined in STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) 87065.5. Additionally, LPA reviewed the qualifications and educational requirements for the Administrator, Social Worker, and Facility Manager. As the applicant is required to have three months of operating expenses, LPA reviewed the necessary financial LIC forms to ensure sufficient resources to operate the STRTP. LPA also discussed the required financial documentation, including the LIC Monthly Operating Statement and the supportive financial verifications. LPA informed the applicant and attendees of the next steps in the application process and requested the following documentation to be provided by or before the scheduled technical assistance meeting: Updated LIC Monthly Operating Budget LIC Personnel Report Administrator qualifications for prospective Administrator Laura Hartney Verification of social worker educational requirements LIC Designation of Facility responsibility with either the board meeting minutes or a resolution confirming the authorized designee is permitted to sign. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report was provided to the applicant

narrative: On 08/21/25, at 9: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Gilbert Marquez and Stefanie Mutialu met with Clinical Supervisor, Kelli Strickland and Vice President of Operations, Derrick Perry, for the purpose of conducting an annual inspection of the facility. The Facility is licensed to serve 11 ambulatory residents 12-21 years old and six infants 0-24 months of age. The current census is five clients. The facility is current with licensing fees. The facility is a single-story dwelling. A physical plant inspection was completed with Vice President of Operations, Derrick Perry and included the following checks: six bedrooms, one communal bathroom for the clients, kitchen, medication room, dining room, living room, seven staff offices, visitation room, sensory room, and outdoor living space. All beds were observed with appropriate bedding and mattresses were in good repair. Bedrooms contained adequate drawers and closet space. No bedroom occupied more than one client and one infant and not used for other purposes. The water temperature was tested in the clients' main bathroom which measured 117 degrees Fahrenheit which is within the appropriate range of 105 degrees to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. The first aid kit was accessible to all staff and had all required supplies. All required forms are posted including Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and the Emergency Disaster Plan. Clients' medications were observed to be inaccessible and stored in medication room. **Continued on LIC809C** **LIC809** Facility grounds are clean and free of debris. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors were tested by fire clearance; fire extinguishers are properly charged and serviced. The Facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods to prepare the items on the posted menu. LPA observed a minimum seven-day non-perishable and two-day perishable supply of food. LPA observed a bottle of "ALL" laundry detergent accessible to clients located on the closet top shelf in client bedroom #1 and a bottle of Clorox bleach spray, two containers of Lysol wipes accessible to clients in an unlocked cabinet in the unlocked laundry room. Per Facility Manager, Kathy McGinty, all cleaners, disinfectants, and toxic chemicals are locked up and inaccessible to clients, however, staff give these items to clients for use but sometimes clients do not return them. For this, the facility is receiving a type A citation. LPA also reviewed one of five client medication records. Per facility staff, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. Due to time constraints, LPA will return on another day to conduct client and staff interviews, and review staff and client files. Based on LPA observation of cleaning chemicals being unlocked in client bedroom #1 and accessible in laundry room, the facility is receiving a type A citation for violation of Title Section 80087(g) Physical Plant. An exit interview was conducted with the Clinical Supervisor, Kelli Strickland to explain this report, the LIC809D page, and a plan of correction for the deficiency. The appeal rights were discussed. A copy of the Facility Evaluation Report, along with LIC809D pages, the Confidential Names List LIC811, and the appeal rights were given to Clinical Supervisor, Kelli Strickland and additionally will be kept in the facility file.

narrative: On June 17, 2021, at 9: AM Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jesus Cervantes and Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Ann Valenzuela conducted an unannounced annual/post licensing inspection. The facility converted from a Group Home to a Provisional STRTP (Short Term Therapeutic Program) on June 27, 2019. LPA was met at the facility by Facility Director, Clete Menke. LPAs toured the facility inside and out at 10: AM. The facility is a one-story residence with five bedrooms and two bathrooms for the clients. Four bedrooms are arranged so that there is one client and their infant in a room. One bedroom is arranged so that there are two clients' sharing a room and two infants. There is adequate closet and drawer space for client's belongings. Individual beds were observed with clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. The bathrooms were clean and in good repair. The hot water was tested at 10: AM and registered at 115.1 degrees which is within the appropriate range of 105 degrees to 120 degrees. Cleansers/chemicals are locked and stored inside a locked cabinet in the kitchen. Sharp knives are inaccessible and stored inside a locked cabinet in the kitchen. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors were tested and observed to be in working order; fire extinguisher is properly charged and serviced. There are no guns or weapons in the facility as stated by the Operations Director. LPAs observed facility posted items in the hallway that included: Disaster Plan, Personal Rights, Grievance Procedures, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Client's medications were observed to be inaccessible and stored inside a locked cabinet next to the toddler play area. LPAs observed a minimum 7-day non-perishable and a 2-day perishable supply of food. There is one camera at the facility located on the wall in the kitchen/living room area. The facility outside grounds was also inspected and it was observed to be clean and well maintained. There are no bodies of water located on the premises. Emergency exits were free from obstruction. narrative: On 08/21/25, at 9: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Gilbert Marquez and Stefanie Mutialu met with Derrick Perry, Vice President of Operations for the purpose of conducting an annual inspection of the facility. The Facility is licensed to serve five ambulatory clients ages 12-21 years old and six infants 0-24 months. The current census is four clients. The facility is current with licensing fees. The facility is a single-story dwelling. A physical plant inspection was completed with Kathy McGinty, Facility Coordinator, which included the following checks: five bedrooms and two communal bathrooms for the clients, kitchen, medication room, dining room, living room, one staff office, playroom for the infants, therapy room, and outdoor living space. One bedroom is approved for two infants; all other bedrooms are approved for one infant. All beds were observed with appropriate bedding and mattress in good repair. Bedrooms contained adequate drawers and closet space. The water temperature was tested in client bathroom #2 which measured 115.3 degrees Fahrenheit which is within the appropriate range of 105 degrees to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. The first aid kit was accessible to all staff and had all required supplies. There is one camera at the facility located on the wall in the kitchen/living room area. All required forms are posted including Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and the Emergency Disaster Plan. Clients' medications were observed to be inaccessible and stored in medication room. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors were **continued on LIC809C** **continued from LIC809** tested and observed to be in working order; fire extinguishers are properly charged and serviced. The Facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods to prepare the items on the posted menu. LPA observed a minimum seven-day non-perishable and two-day perishable supply of food. During the inspection, LPA observed staff S4 change the diaper of a client's baby on a marble counter. The facility is receiving a type B violation. LPA also asked staff S5 if any of the babies were more than 24 months. S5 stated that one was 28 months old. The facility is receiving a type B violation. Medication Records of four clients out of four (C1 - C4) were reviewed with Vanessa Ruiz, Residential Staff Manager. Per facility staff, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. Due to time constraints, LPAs will return on another day to conduct client and staff interviews, and review files for clients and staff. Based on LPA's observation of a staff changing a baby that was not on the floor or using a changing table, the facility is receiving a type B violation. This is not in compliance with Interim Licensing Standards Section 87096.77(d) Personnel Services. Based on LPA review of client roster and short interview with a staff stating that a baby was over 24 months old, the facility is receiving a type B violation. This is not in compliance with California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division Section 80010(a) Limitations on Capacity and Ambulatory Status. An exit interview was conducted to explain the facility evaluation report, along with LIC809D page, the Confidential Names List LIC811, the plan of corrections, and the appeal rights were given to Licensee, and additionally will be kept in the facility file.

narrative: On June 28, 2021 at 10: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Carmen Escobar arrived at Maywright Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA was greeted and granted access by facility manager (FM) Ms. Sheila Evans. The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. There were four staff and five clients present at the time of the inspection. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during the inspection. At 10: AM, Ms. Sheila Evans led the physical inspection of the facility with LPA Escobar. The facility consists of four bedrooms and two bathrooms. The master bedroom is used as the staff office along with the staff restroom. The facility has a dining area within the kitchen area, a living room, a staff office, and a garage. The laundry area is located in the hallway that leads to the garage. There is a large shed in the backyard of the facility that is used as the clinician's office for therapeutic services as well as the case manager's office. There is a window and air conditioning within the building. All bedrooms have individual beds and drawer space for each client. Bedroom #3 has large holes in two of the walls and the bedroom door also has a hole in it. The dresser in this room is broken, drawers are broken. There is currently only one client in this room. The facility will be given a technical advisory for these issues as they occurred this morning before LPA's inspection began, during client fight. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed with appropriate linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair, however, the clients remove the linens to their beds. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. During the inspection, it was observed that the basketball hoop in the backyard has fallen over and is on the ground, creating a potential hazard. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Television, computer, board games, video gaming console, and basketball hoop, were observed for client's recreation time. There is no activities calendar posted, however, staff advise due to COVID-19, they are just getting back to scheduling outings and outside activities. LPAs conducted client interviews. Clients indicated that their basic needs are being met at the facility and core services are being provided. LPA Escobar began the review of staff files, however, due to time constraints, was not able to conclude the review. LPA Escobar will return to complete staff file review and interviews at a later date. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to Administrator, Mr. Jerome Jordan. Carbon monoxide detector is in appropriate working order and facility smoke detectors are also in working order. Fire extinguisher is properly charged and serviced. The facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods and appears to be following the posted menu. While the refrigerator in the kitchen had minimal food, both refrigerators in the garage were fully stocked. Per FM, the clients have access to one of the refrigerators for food/snacks. All required forms are posted including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Medications are locked and stored in a locked box within a locked closet in the staff office. The hot water in the staff and client restrooms was deemed to be at a safe temperature. Per facility staff, there are no firearms or weapons in the facility. Chemicals and/or poisons are locked in a cabinet next to the washer/dryer in the laundry area. Sharp objects/knives are locked and stored in a locked box in the locked closet in the staff office. First Aid Kits are also stored in this locked closet and are complete. A First Aid Manual was also available. It was observed that the licensee has cameras in common areas of the facility as well as the staff office. There is an exception on file for the facility to use the cameras and the facility continues to meet the terms and conditions of the exception, however, the surveillance system is currently not in operating order. Facility will advise when camera system is up and running again. The facility employs one Facility Administrator, six Facility Managers, three direct care youth counselors, one Case Manager, one Head of Service and one Program Director. Facility has not yet obtained Mental Health Certification, however, have submitted the application and are awaiting approval. Facility has obtained National Accreditation through CARF effective through February 28, 2022. Currently, the facility is up to date with Licensing fees for the facility, with a balance of $0. At 10: AM, five of five client files were reviewed during time of inspection. Client files are kept in a locked file cabinet within the staff office. Client 1 (C1), client 2 (C2), client 3 (C3), client 4 (C4), and client 5's (C5) files were reviewed at time of inspection, (See LIC 857) dated June 28, 2021. C3 did not have medical consent form in file. Needs and service plans for C1, C2, and C5 are not current/up to date. The facility will be cited under the Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) section 87068. Modifications to the Needs and Service Plan. C5 did not have proof of current TB test. Technical Assistance Advisory Notes (TA) will be issued for this issue. C3 and C4 are new clients and all missing documents from files will be gathered within 30 days for file completion.

On June 29, 2021, at 9: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Carmen Escobar arrived at Maywright Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). The purpose of the inspection was to complete the continuation inspection for STRTP annual inspection that was initiated on June 28, 2021. LPA already completed the physical inspection of the facility and reviewed facility client files on the first day of the annual inspection. During this annual inspection continuation, LPA Escobar reviewed ten personnel files to ensure they contained all required documentation per Title Regulations and Interim Licensing Standards (ILS). Personnel Files are usually maintained in a locked closet inside the staff office. All appropriate personnel who require caregiver background checks have received criminal record and child abuse index check clearances or exemptions. Eight of the ten files that were reviewed were for employees who converted from group home personnel to STRTP personnel. LPA observed the converted staff members were trained according to the STRTP training requirements for employees. File for staff 1 (S1) did not have current job evaluation. Nine of the ten staff files did not have not have employer verification forms in files. Technical advisories will be issued for the aforementioned staff file issues. Administrator Jerome Jordan states he has been the current administrator since 2018 at the facility, however, no documents or requests for administrator change were made to Community Care Licensing (CCL). Incorrect administrator remains on file. Per interviews conducted, the present administrator is not at the facility as required. Facility will be cited under Interim Licensing Standards section Personnel Requirements. Additionally, eight staff files did not have more than 24 hours of annual training recorded in training file. One staff did not have any annual training hours recorded. Facility will be cited under Interim Licensing Standards section 87065. Training Requirements. Lastly, it could not be determined that staff 10 (S10) meets the direct staff personnel requirements based on personnel record and accompanying employee questionnaire in file. Facility is being cited under Interim Licensing Standards section Personnel Requirements. Administrator Jerome Jordan is present at the facility a minimum of 20 hours a week, as verified by staff schedule and interviews. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during this inspection. LPA discussed the following with the Administrator and Facility Manager: incident reporting, including incidents related to Assembly Bill 388 law enforcement contacts as well as incidents involving emergency interventions. LPA discussed procedures for Child and Family Team (CFT) meetings, including an overview of required Core Services and Supports. On this second day of the continued annual inspection, two youth counselors (direct care staff), one Case Manager, one Facility Manager, and Facility Administrator, were present and were interviewed in regard to their job duties, training, and services provided at the facility. All staff were able to provide sufficient information in relation to the facility's STRTP program. Staff have no issues or concerns regarding the facility. Based upon the inspection of facility records and interviews with staff and clients, the Licensee appears to be meeting CFT and Core Services/Supports requirements. LPA requested the recent board meeting minutes be provided via email by July 6, 2021. LPA also requested an updated LIC500 be sent to LPA as soon as possible. A copy of this report, the advisory notices, and appeal rights, were provided to Facility Administrator, Jerome Jordan.

On October 7, 2022 at 10: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Karen Beal, Erika Lopez and Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Jennifer Smith arrived at Mayright Group Home Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPAs and LPM were greeted and granted access by Mr. Philip Roberts. The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. There were three staff and three clients present at the time of the inspection. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during the inspection. At 11: AM, Mr. Roberts led the physical inspection of the facility. The facility consists of four bedrooms and two bathrooms. The master bedroom is used as the staff office along with the staff restroom. The facility has a dining area within the kitchen area, a living room, a staff office, and a garage. The laundry area is located in the hallway that leads to the garage. There is a large shed in the backyard of the facility that is used as the clinician's office for therapeutic services as well as the case manager's office. There is a window and air conditioning within the building. All bedrooms have individual beds and drawer space for each client. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed and no more than two clients share a bedroom. All client bedrooms have clothing thrown on the floor, dirty dishes and empty food containers. Bedroom #1 has plywood boarding on two of the walls on the left side of the room and a missing window screen. Bedroom #2 has a ceiling fan light bulb that needs to be replaced, the window curtain rod is not secured to the wall and the curtain rod covering the closet is coming away from the wall. Bedroom #3 smells like urine, the wall near the bedroom door is dirty with unknown substance smeared on the wall, the wall has been patched multiple times and needs to painted, the client beds do not have any linens, the curtain for the closet is missing and there is a missing window screen. There was only one set of extra bed linens observed at time of inspection in the hallway cabinet. There was only four client hygiene boxes for six clients at time of visit. LPAs and LPM observed flooring seam cover is broken in the middle in between the laundry room and family room. There is exposed wiring in the hallway where the smoke detector has been removed. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Books and video games were observed for client's recreation time. The screen for the sliding backyard door is broken and laying against the side of the home. Carbon monoxide detectors are properly working. Fire extinguisher is properly charged and serviced. The facility had a low quantity supply of perishable and non-perishable foods at time of visit. Mr. Roberts stated that their shopping day is tomorrow Saturday October 8, 2022. The facility appears to be following the posted menu. The Visitation Policies, Personal Rights Form, Complaint Procedures and Activities Calendar were not posted at time of inspection. The menu was observed on a bulletin board in the kitchen which Mr. Roberts states it will be hung on the wall. The Foster Care Ombudsman poster was posted in the hallway. Medications are locked and centrally stored in a locked closet in the staff office. Per, Mr. Roberts the facility does not have a locked container for refrigerated medications but there is a refrigerator in the locked garage. Mr. Roberts also states that they do not have individual containers for clients to store contraceptives. LPAs attempted to test the hot water temperature in the client bathroom and the kitchen and the temperature was 81 degrees and did not deliver hot water. Per facility staff, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. Chemicals and/or poisons are locked in a cabinet in the laundry room. Sharp objects are locked and stored in the staff office. First Aid Kits are stored in the staff office and facility vehicle. The first aid kit is missing the first aid manual, scissors and thermometer. The board of director meeting minutes were provided. Facility has obtained National Accreditation through CARF effective through September 28, 2025. The facility licensing fees are current. Copies of the 2022 licensing reports were not available at time of inspection. Based on observation and record review, the licensee is being cited under the following: Title Regulations Physical Plant 80075(g)(1), 80088(b), 80087(a), 80088(e)(1) Interim Licensing Standards(ILS), Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Articles 1 through 10, Physical Plant 87088(c)(2), 87088(c) and 87088(c)(2)(A). Technical violations are being cited for the following: Title Regulations Physical Plant 80075(j), ILS Physical Plant 87075(b)(1)(A), Operational Requirements 87072.2(a)(3) and Health & Safety Code 1538.5(a)(3). Due to time constraints the annual inspection will be continued on a later date. An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to Mr. Roberts.

On June 14 , 2024, at 11:01am Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Nicole Strickland, met with Maywright Group Home, Administrator, Jerome Jordan, to deliver a case management deficiencies report. Information obtained by Community Care Licensing (CCL) revealed a concern regarding documentation on Child #1 (C1)'s Psychotropic Medication Administration Record (PMAR). When reviewing the PMAR for C1, LPA observed 34 refusals to take medication made by C1 and documented on the PMAR during the months of April and May 2024. LPA observed that C1 was administered the medication 23 times during April and May 2024. According to the Centrally Stored Medication and destruction record completed by the facility C1 started the medication on April 5, 2024. LPA observed and photographed the bubble pack on June 5, 2024, containing C1's medication which showed 19 pills still in the bubble pack not disbursed to C1. The number of refusals, the number of pills administered, and the number of pills left in the pack do not match. Additionally, while reviewing Child #2 (C2)'s PMAR for the month of June 2024, LPA observed the PMAR to note C2 was absent without authorization on 6/1/2024, 6/2/2024 and 6/3/2024 during the time C2 was to be assisted with C2's pm medication. LPA conducted a record review and was only able to obtain one incident report dated 6/1/2024, noting C1's absence without permission being submitted to CCL, on June 5, 2024. As of 6/13/2024 no documentation was able to be located as being submitted to CCL for C2's absence without permission for absences dated 6/2/2024 and 6/3/2024. The facility is being cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) 87070(b)(14)(H) Children's records (b)(14)(H) Staff initials for each time a psychotropic medication is taken by a child, as an indication that they supervised the child self-administering their psychotropic medication. The facility is also being cited for violation of California Code of Regulations (CCR) regulation 80061(b) Reporting Requirements (b) Upon the ****** occurrence, during the operation of the facility, of any of the events specified in (1) below, a report shall be made to the licensing agency within the agency's next working day during its normal business hours. In addition, a written report containing the information specified in (2) below shall be submitted to the licensing agency within seven days following the occurrence of such event. A copy of the report was discussed and provided along with appeal rights to Maywright Group Home, Administrator, Jerome Jordan.

narrative: The incident report also reported that C1 had no adverse side effects from the medication. Confidential interviews reported that the STRTP's medication protocol requires staff to give clients medication in the staff office. Before giving the medication, staff check the labels to ensure they have the right medication and verify the client's identity. Staff will then place the medicine in a cup to be given to the client and complete the Psychotropic Medication Administration Record (MAR). Corroborating confidential interviews admitted the incident took place and reported that S2 did not follow the STRTP's medication procedure. A Confidential interview reported that S2 failed to follow the procedure because they (S2) felt "rushed" and gave C1 the medication in the bedroom without verifying the medication was being given to the correct client. During the health and safety inspection, LPA was provided with C1's MAR, and the medication error was documented. However, the staff signature and initials were missing. LPA also observed all medications were centrally stored inside a locked box in the living room closet. All medication was observed to be in their original bottle, with labels unaltered, and stored separately in zip lock bags. Additional documentation provided to LPA shows staff received retraining on medication management on 02/13/2024. Furthermore, a confidential interview reported that S2 has not administered medication since the incident, and the staff was instructed to give the client medications in the staff office, according to the STRTP's standard procedure. Based on confidential interviews and a review of pertinent documents, the allegation that staff (S2) mismanaged a child's (C1) medication is substantiated. The preponderance of evidence standard has been met. The STRTP is cited with a violation of Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) 87075(a)(c) Health Related Services (a) In addition to California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Section 80075, the following shall apply (c) Psychotropic medications shall be used only in accordance with the written directions of the physician prescribing the medication... The STRTP was issued a LIC Technical Violation (TV) regarding Interim Licensing Standards 87070(b)(14)(h) Children's Records (b) The following information regarding the child shall be obtained and maintained in the child's record (14) A separate log for each psychotropic medication prescribed to a child documenting all of the following (h) Staff initials for each time a psychotropic medication is taken by a child... narrative: On 05/05/2021, the Department received a complaint alleging that staff did not prevent youth from AWOL's.
