Based on interviews conducted with staff it was revealed that multiple youth ran away on 04/27/21 and staff did try to prevent youth from leaving the facility by counseling youth not to leave and by following them off campus until they lost visual. Also, that staff does not use physical restraints on the youth when they ran away from the facility. Based on interviews conducted with youth it was revealed by two youths that staff did try to prevent youth from leaving the facility; however, one youth stated that staff did not try to stop youth from leaving. Based on conflicting statements this allegation could not be corroborated. It was alleged that staff did not prevent self-harming behavior while minor was in care. The facility staff denied the allegation. Based on interviews conducted with staff whom witnessed this incident it was revealed that on 04/28/21 during a meeting with staff the youth grabbed a pair of scissors, ran out of the office and left the facility. Interviews revealed that staff followed behind youth and alerted the San Dimas Sheriff's Department about youth making self-harming statements and having in possession a pair of scissors. Consequently, the youth was found by the San Dimas Sheriff's Department and was hospitalized and placed on a psychiatric hold for making self-harming statements. LPA interviewed the placement agency social worker whom indicated that the incident was reported timely and did not have any safety concerns with facility staff. Based on interviews conducted, one youth stated that staff did not try to prevent youth from self-harming and the other two youth disclosed that staff did call the police to report the youth had a pair of scissors. Based on conflicting statements this allegation could not be corroborated. It was alleged that staff made inappropriate comments towards minor. The facility staff denied this allegation. Based on interviews conducted with staff whom were present it was revealed that no one witnessed or heard a staff make inappropriate comments towards minor in care. It was revealed by youth that inappropriate comments were made by staff on 04/28/21 but that no one else witnessed it. Based on interviews conducted with youths it was revealed that one is affirming inappropriate comments were made and the other two denied witnessing or having heard any staff make inappropriate comments. Throughout, the interviews LPA observed conflicting statements regarding this allegation and was unable to corroborate whether the allegation was true. It was alleged that a facility client was sexually abused by another client at the facility due to neglect and lack of supervision. The investigation revealed that two facility clients engaged in a sexual interaction behind stage curtains in the recreational building while under the supervision of a facility staff. The sexual activity was discovered by another facility client who reported it to the staff. By the time the staff walked up to the stage area, both clients were securing their pants. The client who reported the incident to staff refused to make any statements to Investigator Spindola, but the staff told Investigator Spindola that the client told him that the two clients were having a sexual encounter behind the stage curtains. Confidential statements obtained from one of the facility clients indicated that the sexual abuse occurred, and he screamed for help during the incident but the staff was not in the immediate vicinity according to the client. The biological parent of the other client did not want her child interviewed regarding the allegation. Based on the fact that the facility staff allowed the clients to play behind a closed curtain for an undetermined amount of time, and the fact that this is the third similar incident that occurred in a couple of months, the allegation is substantiated. Based on the information gathered, the preponderance of evidence to prove the allegation was met, therefore the allegation is substantiated per California Code of Regulations Title 22 - refer to LIC9099-D for deficiencies. Per the new Civil Penalty laws, Health and Safety (H&S) Code section 1548(E), an Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP) determination is pending due to the substantiated allegation. If an ECP is warranted, a Community Care Licensing (CCL) representative will return to the facility to deliver the penalty assessment. narrative: On 09/15/2023, the Department received a complaint alleging that a facility staff was not providing adequate supervision during visitation (monitored visit). The STRTP Facility Director stated that staff should know how to monitor a visit and was unaware of the interaction that took place between the facility staff and county social worker on 09/14/2023 during an off-site monitor visit. The focused staff (S1) that was identified in the report denied the allegation. S1 disclosed that he provided at least seven monitored visits off-site that involved transporting the client to an approved location. S1 disclosed that he was monitoring most of the visits sitting inside the van as he believed that he was not doing anything wrong in the manner he was observing client #1 (C1). Staff alleges that he was "never instructed how to monitor a visit when off the property". The County Social Worker (CSW) who arrived at the approved off-site monitored visit stated that the facility staff (S1) was not observing the visit but was sitting in the van throughout the visit on 09/14/23. CSW spoke with the staff and reminded him that he is supposed to supervise the visits and remain within vision and hearing distance. A review of facility documents and statements obtained by the STRTP Director has determined that there is nothing written about how the staff is to monitor a visit. narrative: The reported allegations were addressed during staff and client interviews. The following was obtained during those interviews, from records reviewed, and during the facility inspection: Personal Rights - Minors are treated equally; they are provided with the same incentives and choices. Minors have access to private calls in the staff office of each cottage. Phone calls are not allowed or only monitored based on documented restriction from authorized representatives and/or court orders. Staff implement different approaches in redirection and de-escalation, depending on each incident. Restraint is only implemented when a minor becomes a danger to self and others, and this is documented in detail. The minor is assessed in the health office by a nurse after a restraint; minor is also assessed by a clinician. Staff are Pro-Act certified and undergo renewal of certification every two years; there is also a refresher class offered every quarter. Other - Incident reports are documented by staff or multiple staff, depending on the phases of their involvement. A campus supervisor and the director will review the reports and may follow up with staff to ensure clarity. They may provide additional information in the required supervisor field/section of the report and check for grammatical errors before submitting it to county placement agencies and the Department. There are cameras in certain public areas which supervising staff and management can view and minors report incidents they were involved in or witnessed. Neglect - Any violations reported or witnessed are addressed; staff may be placed on administrative leave pending an internal investigation and/or terminated. The facility maintains the required direct care staff ratio per shift. There are staff on campus in addition to the direct care staff such as the campus supervisors, the unit manager and the director. The facility also maintains on call/per diem staff. There are two clinicians daily who are supervised by a clinical manager. They work directly with minors on site and through tele-health after hours, but can be available on campus as needed. The facility has its own training unit; staff receive training every fiscal year. The training unit has a system of keeping track of the training hours and classes of each staff. A monthly report is generated and reviewed to ensure staff meet their required training classes. Refresher classes are available to all staff. Minors are not allowed in the maintenance yard; the area is restricted to maintenance staff. The storage area is gated and locked at the end of the workday. Minors can ask staff to safeguard certain personal belongings in the staff office. Only staff have access to the staff office. Furthermore, the facility already addressed similar allegations in reports reviewed during the investigation. Records show staff who had to be re-trained to maintain compliance and staff who were placed on administrative leave then terminated, as a result of confirmed violation(s) during internal investigation(s) and/or the Department's investigation(s). Based on information obtained through interviews and records review, there was no corroborating evidence found so the allegations are unsubstantiated. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence found to prove that the alleged violations occurred. Copies of the licensing reports were provided to the facility representative at the conclusion of today's inspection. Appeal rights forms were also given and explained. There are no deficiencies to be cited at this time.

narrative: On March 16, 2021, Humberto Flores, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), conducted an unannounced Case Management inspection, via phone call, at Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) McKinley Children's Center and talked to Talesha Payne, Program Director. The purpose of the inspection was to deliver the findings for the below incident reported via Special Incident Report (SIR). According to the SIR, on 3/19/20, Child Ref #1 (C1) (see Confidential Names form LIC811 dated 3/16/21) was horse playing with his peers outside of Kiwanis Cottage and then C1 began insulting staff and striking the Cottage windows with his fists. After several redirects from Staff Ref#1 (S1) C1 began to walk away from the Cottage. C1 then quickly made a turn saying, "you thought" and returned towards the cottage kicking the door. C1 then walked away towards the recreation center and returned near his cottage and dismantled a yellow mop bucket top wringer and approached Kiwanis cottage. S1 counseled C1 to make positive choices. As C1 approached Kiwanis cottage, Staff #2 (S2) witnessed C1 attempting to throw the mop at Kiwanis' window. Thus, due to C1's escalating behavior, C1 was escorted (restrained) away from the area with S2 (Right) and S1 (Left) at 1:12pm-1:14pm (both ProAct trained) to Gregory cottage. LPA Flores obtained copies from C1's files: Child and Family Team Meeting (CFT) copy report, Needs and Services Plan, Placement Agreement, Restraint Debriefing Form and Discharge Summary. The documentation reviewed revealed that C1 was transitioned to a standing restraint from 1:14pm to 1:15pm with S1 and S2 remaining in their positions. C1 continued to threaten staff and attempted to free himself from the restraint. C1 was transitioned to a floor assisted restraint with staff remaining in their positions and Staff Ref#3 (S3) securing C1's legs (also ProAct trained) from 1:15PM - 1:24PM (9 minutes). S1 offered deep breathing coping skills for C1 to practice deescalating. cont.# C1 began to take deep breaths and informed staff he was ready to comply with instructions. C1 was then asked to have a seat on the couch to take space and wait for Nurse Genevieve Andrade, to follow up with him. STRTP Management team was updated. The agency nurse conducted the medical assessment of C1. On 3/26/20, a CFT meeting was conducted and C1 agreed to growth in the following areas: provoking, instigating, substance use, fights with peers and how to use coping skills when bored. On 9/10/20, C1 transitioned to the care of his biological mother. No further inspection is needed at this time. A copy of this report and LIC811 was provided to the facility representative. Exit interview conducted.

On April 28, 2021, at 12:30/PM, Humberto Flores, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA),` conducted an unannounced Case Management Inspection, via phone call, to McKinley Children's Center Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) and spoke with Talesha Payne and Patricia White, Assistant Director. The purpose of the inspection was to gather information regarding the below incident reported in a Special Incident Report (SIR). The STRTP reported that on 07/09/2020, around 5:20PM, Lead Campus Supervisor Robert Vazquez requested that Staff Manuel Vigil conduct a community search of San Dimas High School, as there was a report of children on the roof of the Administration building burning an item. Upon Manuel arrival, the Fire and Sheriff Department were seen conducting a perimeter search to locate the fire and the individuals responsible for starting the fire. LPA Flores investigated this incident and interviewed Talesha Payne and Patricia White. LPA Flores requested documentation from the Children's files, the documentation was provided by the facility representative. cont.# The statement obtained and documentation provided revealed that on 07/09/2020, around 2:20PM, Children Ref #1 (C1), Ref #2 (C2) and Ref #3 (C3) walked away from staff and off facility grounds, despite numerous attempts to counsel them against these actions. Campus Supervisor Robert Vasquez was immediately contacted about this situation. The staff continued to follow and attempt to counsel the Children against these actions, but lost visual of them, as they ran through Lone Hill Middle School. A search of the immediate and surrounding area was conducted, but the staff was unable to locate the Children. The San Dimas Sheriff's Department was contacted to file a Missing Persons Report. C2 and C3 were seen running from the scene, C1 required medical attention. Staff Manuel Vasquez informed Law Enforcement that the Children are clients of the STRTP. C1 was transported to a medical facility to receive services due to being intoxicated and a 3-inch gash on his head that he sustained while on runaway status. Around 6:03PM, C2 and C3 returned to the STRTP on their own. A self-search was conducted, and no contraband was found. On 07/11/20, around 10:37AM, San Dimas Sheriff Deputy Zuniga arrived at the STRTP due to the filing of a Suspected Child Abuse Report (SCAR) for a separate incident. cont.# Campus Supervisor Gilbert E. immediately contacted the Director of STRTP, Talesha Payne about this incident. During Deputy Zuniga interview, she met with C1, C2 and C3 individually to determine the next steps. Upon completion of her interviews, she consulted with her sergeant and it was determined that the Special Victims Unit (SVU) would take over the case, as it was noted as an Indecent Exposure Case Ref #1 (EC1). During the SVU investigation, it was discovered that while on runaway status C2 dry-humped C1 while the boys were drunk on the roof of San Dimas High School. Talesha Payne disclosed the C1, C2 and C3 further disclosed that C1 and C2 had been consensually "touchy-feely" on multiple occasions while on runaway status. The Detective informed the Director of STRTP that due to the nature of the case, she was not able to share the details about the incident. No further citations were given to the Children, the Detective from SVU recommended a change in placement for C2 due to this being an ongoing investigation. The County Social Worker for the Children were notified about this incident. No further inspection is needed at this time. A copy of this report and LIC811 was provided to the STRTP representative. Exit interview conducted.

On April 28, 2021, at 11:50AM, Humberto Flores, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), conducted an unannounced Case Management Inspection, via phone call, to McKinley Children's Center Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) and spoke with Talesha Payne and Patricia White, Assistant Director. The purpose of the inspection was to gather information regarding the below incident reported in a Special Incident Report (SIR). The STRTP reported that on 08/24/2020, around 1:10AM, Child Ref #1 (C1) (see Confidential Names List LIC811 dated 04/28/2021) was placed on a Psychiatric Hold due to making statements that he was attempting to harm himself due to not wanting to be detained by the Probation Department. C1 further stated that he was going to run away to kill himself and there was nothing that any of the staff could do about it. LPA Flores investigated the incident and interviewed Patricia White. Documentation from C1's file was requested by LPA Flores and provided by the facility representative. cont.# The statement obtained and documentation reviewed revealed that on 08/23/2020, around 8:30AM, C1 exited his assigned cottage with a blanket, walked over to the volleyball court, and laid on the blanket. C1 was joined by Children Ref #2 (C2), Ref #3 (C3) and Ref #4 (C4). Staff Ref #1 (S1) sat outside on the grass to supervise the Children. Initially, C1 was noted to be awake, alert and oriented; but then C1 stated he was not feeling well and alleged consuming over one hundred "triple c's" (cough and cold tablets). C1's breathing was shallow with pupils dilated 7mm. C1 began pulling at his hair and ripping it out. When C1 was prompted to sit up to obtain his vital signs, he began to sweat profusely and became verbally non-responsive. Paramedics were called at 8:57AM, C1 was transported to the Emergency Room, where he received medical assistant. C1 was medically cleared at 5:30PM. After C1's arrival at the STRTP, C1 disclosed that he was attempting to harm himself due to not wanting to be detained by the Probation Department. C1 further stated that he was going to run away to kill himself and there was nothing that any of the staff could do about it. The Psychiatric Mobile Response Team (PMRT) was called for further evaluation, upon its arrival, it was determined that C1 needed to be place in a psychiatric hold for further evaluation. cont.# No further inspection is needed at this time. A copy of this report and LIC811 was provided to the STRTP representative. Exit interview conducted.

On August 9, 2021, at 8:30AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAS) Claudia Portillo and Humberto Flores, conducted an unannounced Annual Inspection at McKinley Children's Center Short Term Therapeutic Residential Treatment (STRTP) and met with Patricia White. LPAs stated the purpose of the inspection to the STRTP representative. During the inspection a copy of the Register of Facility Clients and Personnel Report was provided upon request. The following topics were inspected: PHYSICAL PLANT: A tour of the facility was conducted, along with Patricia White. The License is placed in a prominent place, in the reception are of the facility. Children's foster rights were posted in all Cottages: Whittier, Kiwanis, Campbell and Gregory. LPA Flores observed that the facility is clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair. The passageways and ramps are unobstructed. There is swimming pool located in the south west area of the facility that is fenced, locked and inaccessible to the children. cont.# The disinfectants and cleaning solutions were stored away from the kitchen areas, food preparation areas to the children. The food is safe and of the quality and the quantity necessary to meet the needs of the clients. Each meal meets at least 1/3 of the recommended in the USDA Basic Food Group Plan-Daily Food Guide. Supplies of staples non-perishable foods for one week and perishable foods for two days are maintained in the facility. Medications are locked and accessible only to employees supervising stored medications. The temperature in the rooms that clients occupy are maintained between 68 and 85 degrees (F) and the hot water temperature was at 110 degrees (F). Emergency Intervention Plan: LPA Portillo reviewed the program statement and PROACT instruction manual and identified the training that is provided for all staff. The staff receive on-going training to maintain certification. A monthly log is utilized to document manual restraints to assist with the Bi-Annual Restraint Report. Disaster Preparedness Plan: LPA Portillo reviewed the disaster and mass casualty plan and other provisions by reviewing the program statement. The facility conducts monthly fire and emergency evacuation drills. Drills are documented and kept in the facilty for at least one year. # CLIENT RECORDS: LPA Flores reviewed the three (3) client file records. Needs and services plans for all three clients were trauma informed, culturally relevant, and age and developmentally appropriate and identified the child's needs: reason for placement, education, personal care and grooming, ability to manage money, visitation information, mental health services and placement information CORE THERAPEUTIC SERVICES: During the inspection review, LPAs were able to see that the facility is providing the Short-Term Therapeutic Program (STRTP) core services and support to the individuals in placement. The facility has trauma informed, culturally relevant, age, and developmentally appropriate. The facility is also providing trauma informed core services through agreements with other agencies. The facilty has a culinary arts program, cultural sensitivity, tennis, equine therapy and a music program for all clients in care. OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS: During the inspection review, LPAs observed the facility maintained an updated roster of the clients with pertinent information. The facility administrator and manager are the responsible and capable staff for communicating with emergency personnel in the facility. The facility has developed, maintained and implemented written complaint procedures. Further inspection is required on a separate day.

On August 18, 2021, at 9:00AM, Humberto Flores, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), conducted an unannounced Case Management Inspection at McKinley Children's Center Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) and met with Melissa Dalziel. The purpose of the inspection was gather information regarding an incident reported via Special Incident Report (SIR). The STRTP reported that on Wednesday, 01/27/2021, at approximately 12:37PM, Child Ref #1 (see Confidential Names form LIC811 dated 08/18/2021) was restrained for been non-responsive to the staff instructions and due to his unsafe behavior C1 was restrained. LPA Flores investigated the incident and interviewed Staff Ref #1. A review of C1's file was conducted, and copies were made and obtained upon request. The information revealed that on 01/27/2021, C1 left his cottage due to being on scooter restrictions and proceeded toward the nurse's station with staff S1 following him. When C1 arrived at the nurse's station, C1 climbed onto the roof of the nurse's station building using a maintenance ladder that was left unattended and lining against the nurse's station building. cont# Staff Ref #2 (S2) arrived and redirected C1 to come down from the roof. C1 got off the roof and was non-responsive and began to take various items off a maintenance cart and began to throw them at staff. C1 was redirected by S2; however, he continued and was non-responsive. Due to C1 unsafe behavior, C1 was placed in a standing restraint at approximately (12:37PM-12:42PM, duration 5 minutes). S2 was on the right and S1 on the left (both Pro-Act. Trained). At 12:39PM PM, Staff Ref #3 (Pro-ACT Trained) arrived and switched out with S1 on the right. S3 attempted crisis communication with C1, but he was unresponsive. The restraint was conducted in the area between the nurse's station building and the cafeteria. Due to C1 continuous attempts to release himself by maneuvering his arms, C1 was transitioned to a floor restraint at 12:42PM. Staff Ref #4 (S4) (Pro-ACT Trained) arrived and switched with S1 on the left side at 12: PM. At approximately 12: PM Assistant Director Patricia White was contacted to approve an extension over the initial 15 minutes. While in the restraint, C1 continued to threaten to harm staff resulting in the continuation of the restraint. At 12: PM, S1 grabbed C1's legs due to repeatedly attempting to roll over and release himself from containment. At 12:57, Staff Ref #5 (Pro-ACT Trained) arrived and switched out with S1 on the legs. The nurse was notified at approximately 12: PM and Nurse Jonathan Alcantara arrived at approximately 12: PM. cont.# During the floor restraint C1 made several attempts to lift his body to free himself from containment, C1 maneuvered his arms attempting to pull them into his body as well as attempting to lift his legs up and down. Staff #6 (S6) arrived and attempted to fresh face with C1, however, C1 continued to struggle making threats to punch staff. According to the SIR, S2 was contacted and approved the 30-minute restraint extension. After several minutes, C1 agreed to talk with S3 and was released from the restraint at 1: PM when C1 appeared to be at baseline behavior. Case Manager Claudia Espinosa notified C1's County Social Worker via voicemail at 4:25 pm. C1 was assessed by On Call Clinician Adesha Porcil at 4:15PM. STRTP management was notified. During the file review LPA Flores did not observe in C1's file the written approval to continue the restraint after the initial 30 minutes from the Administrator. A copy of this report, LIC811 and LIC9102 was provided to the STRTP representative. Exit interview conducted.

Both children approached the volleyball net, next to Unit 2, C1 told C2 that if he did not return the skateboard he would pour his root beer soda on C2. C2 became visibly upset and told C1 not to do it because he was wearing clothes that C2's mother had giving him for his birthday. S1 got in between both children to prevent a fight between both children and asked C1 not to pour drink on C1 and for C2 to return the skateboard to C1. S1 got out of the way to allow C2 to return the skateboard, then C1 poured his drink on C2's pants and C2 threw the skateboard at C1 like a "chest pass" and hit C1 in the forehead. C1 was then transported to the Emergency Room where he was examined. C1's laceration was glued and closed. C1 was giving home care instructions not to wash the area for 7 days. C1 disclosed that C2 did not have the intention to hurt him and that they were good friends before the incident and are still good friends. On the same date of the incident C1 apologized to C2 and vice versa. No further inspection is needed at this time. A copy of this report and LIC811 was provided to the STRTP representative.

On August 23, 2021, at 9:00AM, Humberto Flores, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), conducted an unannounced Case Management Inspection at McKinley Children's Center Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP) and met with Patricia White. The purpose of the inspection was to gather information regarding an incident reported via Special Incident Report (SIR). The STRTP reported that on 02/08/2021, Children Ref #1 (C1) (see Confidential Names form LIC811 dated 08/20/2021) was restrained and escorted out of the cottage for 2 minutes because he refused to exit a staff office and did not return a dangerous item. LPA Flores investigated the incident and interviewed Patricia White. A review of C1's file was conducted, and copies were obtained upon request. The information revealed that on 02/08/2021, in Whittier Cottage, C1 entered the kitchen area while Child Ref #2 (C2) was in the kitchen, Staff Ref #1 (S1) verbally redirected C1 to exit the Kitchen to wait and enter once C2 exited. C1 became visibly upset and ignored staff. C1 then began to repeatedly open and close the refrigerator door forcefully. cont.# After several verbal redirects, C1 exited the kitchen and walked toward the hallway. C1 then began to slam the door repeatedly. S1 offered C1 to take space outside with staff but he did not comply. C1 then stopped slamming the door after another resident encouraged him to stop. S1 then fresh-faced with Staff Ref #2 (S2) and entered the staff office to update the communication log. Moments later S2 opened the staff door to place an item inside. C1 then pushed through staff and entered the office without permission. S1 verbally redirected C1 to exit but he did not comply. At this time, S2 exited the cottage to shadow another child that exited without informing staff. C1 opened the staff desk drawer and began to take several of the items, among them a push pen. S1 offered C1 to do an arts and crafts activity with staff. S1 radioed Campus Supervisors for additional assistance. Staff Ref #3 (S3) and Ref #4 (S4) arrived to assist. Due to C1 refusing to leave and having an unsafe item in his hand he was escorted out by S3 right side and S4 (Both Proact trained) at approximately 1:45 p.m. - 1:47 p.m. (duration 2 minutes). Once C1 was escorted out of the cottage he was released and S1 successfully retrieved the push pen. C1then began to walk away from staff. After several minutes being on school grounds, C1 took space with at the basketball courts. cont.# C1 debriefed this incident with staff on 02/09/2021. The onsite nurse conducted a check on C1 on 02/09/2021 around 6:56PM and re-integrated into the STRTP program. No further inspection is needed. A copy of this report and LIC811 was to the STRTP representative. Exit interview conducted.

narrative: On 2/11/2022, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Daiquiri Boyd, visited Michigan House to discuss an incident report that was sent in in August of 2021. LPM Angela King requested that LPA look into the incident and the facts of the incident. LPA spoke with Nadia Smith, House Manager, regarding the incident. The client was able to keep his electronics and they worked out a plan to ensure that this doesn't happen again.

LPA asked Ms. Smith why the minor's bicycle was locked. Ms. Smith explained that the minor requested the lock for his bicycle because the other residents in the home would use it and leave without permission on his bicycle. The facility staff purchased a lock for the minor. On June 26, 2022, the minor was upset and wanted to leave the facility without permission. The minor broke the lock off and did leave the facility. LPA asked Ms. Smith why would the minor have to break the lock off if he has the keys. Ms. Smith explained that the minors in the home do not keep their own keys. When they want their keys they request it from staff and staff will get it for them. LPA asked Ms. Smith if the bicycle was locked to prevent minor from leaving the facility without permission. Ms. Smith stated that the minor locks his own bicycle so others don't take it. They did not lock it up to prevent him from leaving the facility. On the day of the incident, minor was upset and didn't wait for the key and broke the lock off and then left. Ms. Smith explained to the LPA that staff is aware that they are not to lock up minor's personal belongings without their permission unless it is something they are not allowed to have in the home (contraband). There were no deficiencies cited during this Case Management for the incident of June 26, 2022

On August 3, 2023, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) was met at the facility by Staff Charles Smith. Mr. Smith contacted Facility Manager, Nadia Smith which arrived at the facility shortly thereafter. The purpose for the inspection is to conduct a Case Management with regards to incident reports dated May 13, 2023 and May 14, 2023. Incident report dated May 13, 2023 stated that minor refused to take medication and lost points due to this. This incident report was also not signed by facility personnel. This incident report in question was vague with details and specifically stated that the minor lost points for not taking medication. Mr. Smith stated that he is the staff that is responsible for completing and submitting incident reports for the facility. Mr. Smith explained that he did not complete the incident reports in question as he was off on vacation during that time. Mr. Smith stated that the facility does not take away points for not taking medication and is not sure why that was put in the report. Ms. Smith stated that while Mr. Smith was out on vacation another staff completed the report. Ms. Smith agreed that this incident report was not properly completed with information and that clarification should had been stated that the loss of points was due to the disrespect (Inappropriate language) to staff and not because of not taking medication. Incident report dated May 14, 2023 was vague and lacked information for a complete incident report. AWOL protocols were followed but that was not conveyed in the report due to the incompleteness of the report. Ms. Smith also acknowledged that the reports were not signed and not reviewed before being submitted to Community Care Licensing. Ms. Smith stated that all staff will undergo re-training on incident report writing. An Advisory Note -Technical Violation was issued on this date, no deficiencies cited during this inspection.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Behavioral Tech Manager Robert Smith and Facility Manager Steven Anderson, who assisted with the inspection. The purpose of this CM is to close the Case Management opened on 4/5/2024. The incident that occurred on 1/25/2024 involved staff from Mile High conducting a restraint on a child in placement at a Resource Family Home (RFH). It was alleged the restraint was conducted inappropriately, and that matter has since been referred to Solano County for investigation, as the RFH is licensed by them. LPA investigated the incident to determine how Mile High/MSK Solutions is involved in the RFH, and where the two blend together. LPA conducted this case management investigation by conducting confidential interviews with one child, one staff, the Program Director, The Executive Director, the Facility Manager, an individual associated with Mile High (P1) on 4/5/2024, 4/10/2024, 4/15/2024, 4/19/2024, 5/7/2024, and 5/23/2024, and by reviewing Incident Reports relating to the incident from both Mile High and another agency who witnessed the incident. Through investigation, LPA was informed by P1 that they are not a staff at the Mile High Mountain Top house or Legend house, but is the Executive Director's personal assistant. However, before LPA was informed of this, LPA requested P1's schedule for when they are working at the Mile High houses from the FM, who informed LPA that P1 is only scheduled at, "the Ranch," and that, "that's what [their] timesheets say." LPA requested these timesheets, however when the Director responded, LPA was informed by the Director that P1 is paid privately by him, and not through Mile High; LPA did not receive any timesheets. P1 is associated to both Mile High houses, beginning in 2021. Both the FM and P1 explained to LPA how the incident and restraint occurred. This explanation was in contrast to what was reported by witnesses. LPA was informed that the Facility Manager was called to assist P1 at the Resource Home in containing the youth in care due to the rapport FM already has with the youth, and FM responded, assisting with the restraint and de-escalation. LPA was informed by one staff, that staff from Mile High go to that Resource Home, "every week or every day," "multiple staff, a few staff from Legend house...morning shift and evening shift people." However the staff did not remember any staff names. When asked if staff leave their shift at Mile High to assist at the RFH, the staff confirmed they do and depending on C1's behaviors, they would be gone for about a couple of hours. The staff referred to the RFH as, "the Ranch." LPA learned from ED that MSK Solutions, the Licensee of Mile High homes, has another property called, "the Ranch." MSK Solutions had previously submitted intention to license that location as a facility with CCL on 10/11/2023, however then rescinded that request on 10/24/2023. LPA has visited the location and found that it is marked by a driveway arch that states, "Mile High Sky Ranch." LPA was informed that the Director lives there and it is licensed through Solano County as a Resource Family Home, where a previous client of Mile High is placed. ED informed LPA that the Director rents the home from ED, however it is not related to Mile High/MSK. LPA also learned that the clients at the Mile High houses sometimes visit the RFH to tend to the animals there. FM provided LPA with his timesheet from January 2024, obtained from a time tracking app the facility uses called a uAttend, as well as the LIC500s (Personnel Reports). FM also showed LPA the Line App which the staff and management use to communicate, and the Paychex app, which keeps staff paychecks. An office meeting will be scheduled with MSK Solutions at a future date to obtain more information regarding facility staff involvement at the RFH. An exit interview was conducted with Facility Manager Steven Anderson and a copy of this report was provided to FM.

narrative: At 9: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Alyssa Burgess and Orlando Areizaga made an unannounced annual continuation inspection at the facility's Administrative Office where their files are stored. No one answered the door and LPA called Administrator Steven Anderson, who stated he will be on his way. Later, LPAs checked the door again and Office Assistant Corri Collins answered, stating LPAs could not access the office, as there would be a meeting happening soon. LPA informed OA that they need to complete the annual and as the files are located at the office, they are there. OA informed LPA that a supervisor is not available, and LPAs may not use any place in the office. LPM Jodean Hall called Administrator to help facilitate the annual inspection. Administrator arrived and LPA provided him a list of all information needed to complete the annual. LPAs took a break to allow Administrator time to gather the documents and arrived at the Legend Home facility at 12: PM to continue the annual as agreed. At 12: PM Administrator arrived with the documents. LPA was provided the licensing documents retained for the past three years. The most recent report presented was dated 5/10/2023. The facility did not maintain Licensing Reports for the past three years as required. There was no manual restraint log. The facility is conducting disaster drills on a monthly basis, however does not conduct them at least once per shift, per six months. The Administrator brought staff files for staff from the Mountain Top house and needed to return to the Admin office to get Legend Home staff files. LPAs reviewed one Administrator file and one Clinician file. Once Administrator returned with the correct files, LPAs reviewed one Facility Manager file, and two staff files, finding: All staff are fingerprint cleared and associated as required. The Administrator and Clinician meet all requirements. The Clinician's (MH1) CPR/First expired 11/30/2024. On 4/7/2025 and today 4/8/2025 when LPAs arrived at the facility, S1 was the only staff present, who does not meet the education and experience requirements of a Facility Manager. There were no qualified Facility Managers present until Administrator arrived to assist. LPAs advised Administrator about the exception request process. All staff reviewed met the annual training requirements. LPAs reviewed four client files and found: The Needs and Services Plans (NSPs) did not include any information about clients having the need to be routinely searched. Through interviews and based on LPA observation, clients get searched with a metal detecting wand, and have their possessions searched, when they enter the facility as a standard practice. This is a violation of the clients' right to be free from unreasonable searches. The two clients observed to be searched (C1 and C2) on 4/7/2025, and C2 on 4/8/2025 had no indication in their NSP for the authorization of routine searches. Administrator stated C1 and C2 had no need to be wanded/searched. Administrator informed staff during this inspection. There was not a staff person designated to facilitate/plan the planned activities and there was no planned activities calendar. LPA was not provided a current record of mental health services provided to the clients for the past 12 months despite requesting one. A record of mental health services was provided to LPA on 3/7/2025 for an unrelated reason, and today, LPA was informed that is the record she should use, as directed by Interim Executive Director Jamek Johnson. The record shows that all clients have not received "psycho therapy" since the end of January 2025. LPA interviewed one staff and one Administrator on this date. LPA found they were knowledgeable about their roles and the clients. LPA advises for some refreshers on the mandated reporter process. One client's JV223 dated 6/24/2024 is expired. There is an email dated 5/8/2024 requesting review for renewal, however no other follow-up included in the file. Administrator is unsure if the client no longer takes psychotropic medications because they were refusing them, or because the JV223 expired. LPA issued an advisory note to inform LPA of the reason. On this date the facility is being cited for sections of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 5, Sections 87072(c)(10), 87065(f), and 87089.1(g) on the attached LIC809-Ds. LPA also issued Technical Violation advisory notes, which are not citations. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report, confidential names list, and appeal rights were provided to him.

narrative: There were also multiple incidents in which one client was sexually inappropriate with another client by flirting, trying to show their genitals, dry-humping, and more. Interviews revealed that for the majority of the time, staff did intervene to stop this from occurring, however some clients stated that it was not at all times. One staff stated these incidents sometimes occurred quickly and out of view of staff. Clients stated they would often rough-house with each other, and some stated staff would tell them to stop. In one incident, a client allegedly poked another client in the anus. When staff became aware of the allegation, it was immediately reported and investigated by the facility. After the facility investigated, they issued a discharge notice for the client on an emergency basis to keep the other clients safe. Based on interviews LPA found there was a clear pattern of one client being physically inappropriate and aggressive with other clients in the home, and while action was taken with the aggressing client it is unclear if action could and should have been taken sooner, based on the information provided. During interviews with seven clients, six staff, the Clinician, the Administrator, and the Executive Director, LPA was informed that the house is clean. Clients have chores and do them daily. If a client does not do their chore, staff clean up after the clients or incentivize other clients to cover the chore for more points. Additionally, all individuals interviewed except for one stated that a mess does not last more than a day, and most of them stated it lasts less than hours. One client stated it might last up to a day and a half. One client stated that after a client was in the bathroom sometimes there would be pubic hair, feces, urine, and soap. One staff stated the floors are sticky sometimes. LPA has visited the facility unannounced on many occasions over years, and has not observed the home to be messy or dirty. (continued)... During interviews with clients, staff, a witness, Administrator, and the Executive Director, LPA learned that a client had their money stolen on at least one occasion, but possibly more than once. The client stated the money was locked up with staff and it went missing. Other clients stated another client stole the money, or that they heard that it was a staff. The Administrator stated it was looked into and it was unclear, as sometimes the client kept their belongings in their room instead of locking it up, as well as brought money in without telling staff how much there was. The Executive Director was unsure of the outcome and thought that management had figured it out, as well as stated that if the money was lost by staff, then it would be replaced. All clients stated they are allowed to lock their personal belongings up with staff for safe-keeping, and some choose to do so. Staff repeatedly encouraged the client to safeguard their money. One staff stated they brought up the missing money during management meetings, and it was brushed off. Additionally, in LPA's review of the client's allowance sheets, there were some errors and entries that were unclear. LPA brought this to the attention of the ED, who discussed this with Administrator. In another visit to the facility for an annual on 3/6/2024, LPA observed a random sample of a client's allowance sheet in which LPA again observed errors. LPA addressed this with the Administrator during that inspection. Based on conflicting information, and lack of information, it is unclear if in this instance the facility failed to safe-guard the client's money. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur, therefore the allegations are unsubstantiated. narrative: During interviews, one staff stated that due to the facility's consequences/level structure, it does not meet the clients' mental health needs as a therapeutic environment. One client felt the facility gives, "shitty," therapy, however they met with the therapist twice a week. The client refused to see the facility psychiatrist, and saw their Kaiser psychiatrist instead. LPA was informed by the Clinician and one client that this client sometimes refused to engage or participate in the mental health services offered to them by Mile High. Another client stated they did get therapy at the facility, but stated it was not all that they needed. When asked what else they needed, the client stated they did not know and it was only something, "someone," told them. One client stated there are Behavioral Techs at the facility but all they want to do is take them to the library and not talk to them, but the client also stated they refused to meet with mental health staff to have their mental health needs met, so it is unclear if they actually did not meet the client's needs. During other interviews with all other clients, they confirmed their mental health needs are met. There are Behavioral Techs who are in the facility daily to meet with the clients about their mental health and clients meet with the Clinician at least twice a week. Additionally, LPA was informed by the Clinician that a psychiatric nurse practitioner comes to the facility to assess the clients' medications and make recommendations. The facility has a psychiatrist as well who diagnoses clients and prescribes them medications. Based on LPAs interviews which were conducted and record reviews, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegation is found to be SUBSTANTIATED. On this date the facility is being cited for a violation of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 5, Section 87089.1(a). In another client interview, LPA was informed that Admin, "yells all the time." The client stated Admin yelled at a client to get out of another client's room. Another client stated ED yells at the clients, but it is only to get his point across and not to scare them. The other clients denied ED yells at them. LPA learned from the Program Director that ED is also the one to address the clients' behavior and consequences with them. LPA was informed that it is true that ED could have a softer approach with some of the more, "sensitive," clients, and they, "could see how some kids can perceive some things negatively, though it is never inappropriate." LPA was informed that ED will explain to clients the consequences of their actions and they won't like it. One staff stated that ED speaks to the clients, "very bold, disrespectful, and yelling and cursing." When asked for an example of this, the staff stated ED says, "I don't give a shit," "I don't give a damn." The staff stated however, that it is nothing abusive. Another staff stated ED has said to clients before to, "cut this bullshit out." When asked about cussing to the clients, ED stated that he sometimes does talk to the clients in their language, or paraphrases what they say to him. ED stated he does not yell at the clients, but is a straight-talker with them. Based on this information it is not clear if ED and Admin do yell at the clients, or if it is a perception by the clients due to the nature of the conversations, the language used, and/or the natural voices of the ED and Admin. During interviews with seven clients, six staff, the Clinician, the Administrator, and the Executive Director, LPA was informed that the house is clean. Clients have chores and do them daily. If a client does not do their chore, staff clean up after the clients or incentivize other clients to cover the chore for more points. One staff stated the floors are sticky sometimes. LPA has visited the facility unannounced on many occasions over years, and has not observed the home to be messy or dirty. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur, therefore the allegations are unsubstantiated. C1 explained that ED and FM pulled C1 off of the bed to restrain them by taking their arms up and putting them on the bed on their stomach, "to where I couldn't breathe." C1 explained then ED was, "talking crap," to them and pinching them on their arm, which left bruises. FM was not doing anything that was hurting C1. The restraint ended when the police arrived. narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced post licensing inspection at the facility and met with Reyes Bonilla, Program Director (PD), and Tegre Miles, Executive Director (ED), who assisted with the inspection. LPA utilized the CARE Tool for this inspection. LPA and PD conducted a walk-through of the facility. LPA observed one deficiency: In the clients' bathroom, the water tap delivered water at 125.6 degrees, which is 5.6 degrees too high. LPA issued a Technical Violation advisory note for this. The water heater was turned down during this inspection. LPA completed the Physical Plant and Operations domains from the CARE Tool, and no other deficiencies were found. LPA was unable to complete this inspection on this date and will return on another date to do so. An exit interview was conducted with ED and PD and a copy of this report will be emailed to them with a read receipt, which will serve as their confirmation for receiving the document.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced post licensing inspection at the facility and met with Reyes Bonilla, Program Director (PD), and Steve Dogan, Administrator, who assisted with the inspection. LPA utilized the CARE Tool for this inspection. LPA completed the rest of the domains in the CARE Tool, and found: two out of five clients reviewed had not had a recent TB test completed and five out of ten staff reviewed did not meet the 40 hour annual training requirement. LPA issued two type B citations for these deficiencies. LPA also found that the majority of all clients' Needs and Services Plans reviewed had either no signatures, or one or two signatures; there was a lack of visitation information in the files; there was not a complete manual restraint log, however there were incident reports with attached descriptions; the length of time for each hold was not clear in the descriptions; two staff did not have complete proof of education or verified experience in their files; the facility was utilizing "fines" to be repaid back from a portion of the client's allowance to a fund for activities; and room sharing compatibility assessments were not completed. LPA issues Technical Violation advisory notes for these issues. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and PD and a copy of this report will be emailed to them with a read receipt, which will serve as their confirmation for receiving the documents.

During the inspection, LPA Hill met with Steven Dogan, Administrator and inspected the facility inside and out. During the facility tour of the facility, LPA Hill observed the medication storage location is currently in a restroom on the first floor as the normal medication storage location is on the second floor but there is currently a youth in isolation in that room. LPA did interview one youth during the inspection at 3: PM. LPA reviewed two staff personnel files on site at the facility at 2: PM. LPA interviewed two staff on site at the facility during the inspection at 12: PM. LPA observed that of the two youth taking psychotropic medications one has authorization by a parent/guardian and another has a current JV223 that expires in November 2021. Facility was cited for Facility cited for violation of Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Regulation 87070(b)(12)(H) and (E) Children's Records. LPA observed that the Psychotropic Medication Administration Record (PMAR) document was not signed upon administration of psychotropic medications for C1 (see LIC811 dated 9/9/21) on 9/8/21, 9/9/21 and C2 on 9/3/21. Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Connie Goldie and Alyssa Burgess, made an unannounced required two-year annual inspection and met with Administrator, Steve Dogan who assisted with the inspection. LPAs and Facility Manager Jamilliah Cabunoc conducted a walk through of the facility and observed: three client bedrooms, one media room, one kitchen, on garage, the living room area, staff office, and backyard. The facility was clean and in good repair, aside from one client bedroom which had a boarded window from a client behavioral incident. Plans to repair the window are in effect. Also in that bedroom, there was a hole in the wall from a punch or kick. This is also planned to be repaired. LPAs interviewed three clients. LPAs reviewed two client files. Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess returned to the facility's Administration Office located at Georgia Street, Vallejo, CA 94590 to complete the file review for the Annual Inspection started yesterday, 2/23/2022. LPA reviewed 3 client files and 6 staff files, including the Administrator and Facility Manager. Yesterday and today, LPA found in the client files, that all clients were missing their original Needs and Services Plans (NSPs), however, Administrator was able to retrieve them and show to LPA. Also missing were certain details in the NSPs, described in the attached citations and advisory notes. All clients were missing evidence of mental health services received. All clients had a health screening, TB test record, school information, placement agreements, required signed documents, JV220s and JV223s if necessary for psychotropic medications, consent forms, authorized representative information and cash/personal valuable records. All clients receive an allowance and can use the facility telephone. Based on the level system, the clients may also earn personal phone privileges. For the staff records reviewed, LPA found: all staff had the appropriate criminal record clearances and association to the facility. All staff met the education and experience requirements. All staff had their health screening and TB test. All but one staff had their required annual hours of training. The one staff who's annual training is not complete, was prevented from completing the requirement due to COVID-related travel issues. Additionally, three out of six staff reviewed had expired CPR/1st Aid training. On this date, the facility is being cited for the following violations of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 4 and the California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 1, found during this annual inspection on 2/23/2022 and 2/24/2022: 1. 87095.61(f)(3) 2. 87095.61(f)(6) 3. 87065.1(d)(6)(A) 4. 87070(b)(14) 5. 87087(e) 6. 87068.2(b) 7. 80075(k)(7) Eight Technical Violation Advisory Notes (not citations), were issued for the other issues found during this inspection. Additionally, LPA issued two Technical Assistance Advisory Notes to the facility, which are not citations. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report, all Advisory Notes, Confidential Names List, and appeal rights were emailed to him with a read receipt which will serve as the record of receipt.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced inspection at the facility and met with staff Thomas Hermann, who assisted with the inspection. Present at the facility was one client and one staff. Another staff arrived not long after. There were no facility managers at the facility. Administrator Steve Dogan arrived a little bit later. On this date, the facility is being cited for a violation of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 5, Section 87065(f), Personnel Requirements. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator Steve Dogan and a copy of this report and appeal rights were given to him.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Facility Manager (FM) Tom Hermann who assisted LPA with the inspection. CCL received an incident report dated 1/27/2024 stating that client C1 (see confidential names list dated 2/7/2024) went to C1's room and was yelling because C1's door was removed, "as part of [C1's] suicidal watch." Earlier, C1 had barricaded in C1's room, so C1's door was removed. Staff intervened when C1 was yelling and C1 then did property destruction and threats. In another incident report dated 1/27/2024, it stated that earlier in the day, C1 was kicking a pool table, yelling at staff, and was attempting to harm themselves with a piece of plastic, which the staff was able to remove. LPA interviewed FM Tom Hermann and Administrator Steve Dogan. An emergency Child and Family Team Meeting was held on 2/5/2024 for C1. LPA reviewed CFT Notes and Action Plan and found they discussed placement. However, they did not discuss C1's safety in the facility, or any of the behavioral issues C1 has been displaying, C1's recent mental health struggles, or psychiatric hospitalizations. Program Director Reyes Bonilla will be requesting the next CFT be moved up sooner to be able to adequately address these issues. PD will inform LPA when this meeting is scheduled. After the meeting, the facility will send the notes to LPA. After investigation into these incidents LPA has found that while the intent behind removing the client's door was for safety, it is not clear that the steps to ensure it was not a personal rights violation were taken. LPA is issuing an advisory note, which is not a citation, to address this. Additionally, the incident report describing C1 attempting self-harm with a piece of plastic was limited in details to evaluate the danger of the plastic. LPA advised Administrator Steve Dogan to include more information in the incident report, such as where C1 was scratching with the plastic, what was the piece of plastic from, was it sharp, were there any marks on C1, etc. An exit interview was conducted with Program Director and a copy of this report was sent to Administrator Steve Dogan and PD.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced Plan of Correction (POC) inspection at the facility and met with Facility Manager (FM) Tom Hermann who assisted LPA with the inspection. On 12/29/2023, LPA issued the citation: Type B - 87065(f): Personnel Requirements. The licensee shall designate at least one facility manager to be present at the facility at all times when one or more children are present. This requirement was not met as evidenced by: Based on observation and statements, the facility failed to have at least one facility manager present at all times one or more clients are present. This is a potential Health, Safety, or Personal Rights risk to clients in care. POC: By POC due date of 1/29/2024. The facility will have trained all eligible staff as facility managers, with the topics specified in section 87065.1(b)(5)(A-M) and will submit the monthly staff schedule for February 2024 with facility managers noted on all shifts with children, and will submit the training records. Administrator Steve Dogan sent LPA the POC during LPA's inspection. No further action is necessary. LPA advised Administrator to ensure that POCs are sent timely, by the POC due date, to prevent the assessment of civil penalties for the failure to correct. An exit interview was conducted with PD and a copy of this report and clearance letter were sent to Administrator Steve Dogan and PD.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess and Health Program Specialist (HPS) Kayla Haith made an unannounced annual inspection at the facility and met with Administrator Steve Dogan, who assisted with the inspection. LPA, HPS, and Administrator conducted a walk through of the facility. LPA observed: three client bedrooms, one media/relaxation room, one dining room, kitchen, laundry area, garage, living room, three bathrooms, and staff office. Medications were inaccessible as required. Client Medication Administration Records were completed as required. There were separate Psychotropic Medication Administration Records for the psychotropic medications as required. There was an adequate amount of perishable and non-perishable food as required. The facility was clean. There was available foodware, in good condition. The hot water in the clients' bathroom measured at 143 degrees Fahrenheit, which is outside the required range of 105-120 degrees Fahrenheit. Clients had appropriate bedding and hygiene supplies. All clients had clothing as required. One client dresser was in disrepair with broken tracks/drawers. Outside in the backyard, there was an approximately 5 inch in diameter drain hole which was uncovered. There were no paper towels or soap in the media room bathroom. One seat out of eight passenger seats in the facility van had a broken/inoperable seat-belt buckle fastener. Disinfectants and knives were inaccessible to clients. LPA interviewed one staff. The staff was knowledgeable about the facility, however LPA recommends a refresher on mandated reporter requirements, and abuse reporting process. LPA and HPS went to the facility's administrative office located at Georgia Street, Vallejo, CA to conduct a file review and found: The board is meeting as required, and minutes are maintained. Board minutes were accessible to LPA. There are two clients placed currently, so the ratio is kept at 1:3, and staff are currently not conducting restraints unless another trained staff or Administrative staff come in to assist. LPA did observe the facility Pro-Act certified trainer's certification to be up-to-date. The facility plans to train additional staff on emergency interventions. All staff in the roster were fingerprint cleared and associated as required. All files were accessible to CCL as required. The client who is taking psychotropic medications had an accurate and updated JV223 as required. LPA was unable to complete the inspection and will return on another date to do so. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report was provided to him.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced annual continuation inspection at the facility's Administrative Office located at Georgia Street, Vallejo, CA 94590. LPA met with Administrator Steve Dogan, who assisted with the inspection. LPA reviewed two of two client files and found: one client refused all medical and dental appointment efforts. The clients have all identifying information completed. Both clients are receiving mental health services as required. Both clients have Needs and Services Plans as required, however both were out of date by more than one month, and in one case, more than two months. One NSP is missing the signature of one client. Both NSPs are missing information about money management, crisis management plans, including any known limitations of the use of emergency interventions, and behavior interventions, and the anticipated duration of placement, including the transfer plan. Neither NSP includes how the clients' family members are integrated in the treatment process, including post-discharge, and how sibling connections are maintained to the extent clinically appropriate and consistent with any applicable court orders, and in accordance with the client's best interest. Neither client file documented when the client's case plan was received by the County. The facility did not receive one case plan and there was no documentation of efforts by the facility to obtain it. During this inspection, Administrator reached out to the County and obtained the case plan for that client. Additionally, there was no documentation in either client's file of the steps taken to facilitate outreach to the family members of the child, including siblings. All other requirements were met. LPA reviewed the facility's Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) plan and found: The facility is compiling their CQI data during their Accreditation period, and they include all required elements, except for peer-review amongst other STRTPs with a similar population. LPA reviewed 5 staff files which included the Administrator, Social Worker/Head of Service, Facility Manager, and Staff. LPA found: all staff were fingerprinted and associated to the facility as required. All staff reviewed met training, education, and experience requirements. All staff had a valid Driver's License. All staff files had required identification information. One staff's CPR/First Aid was expired by just over a month. This staff is an on-call part-time staff. All other staff reviewed had valid CPR/First Aid certificates. The Administrator's Administrator Certificate expired on 12/17/2023. Administrator sent in his renewal by certified mail on 12/16/2023 and is waiting for his certificate. LPA observed that the Department is currently processing renewals received on 7/24/2023, as they are back-logged. LPA observed signed Board of Director statements from five out of seven of the members of the Board. All chair-holding members have signed. On this date, the facility is being cited for violations of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 5, Sections: 87070(b)(18), 87068.2(b), 87068.2(f), and 87068.3(a). LPA also issued Technical Violation Advisory Notes, which are not citations. LPA will return on another date to interview two clients and one more staff. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to him.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Administrator Steve Dogan who assisted with the inspection. This inspection is to close the case management opened on 5/6/2024. The incident was in regard to a client (C1 - See Confidential Names List dated 7/10/2024) having to go to the emergency room due to asthma symptoms, and did not have an inhaler. LPA reviewed medical records, medication records, and emails. The client was placed on 3/23/2024, and on 3/25/ Administrator emailed the County Social Worker, informing her that the client stated they need an inhaler. The County Social Worker was not aware that the client needed an inhaler, and the client did not come to the facility with one. On 3/31/2024, as stated in the incident report dated 4/1/2024, the client went to the ER for shortness of breath, but did not want to stay to be seen. On 4/1/2024, the client was again taken to the ER by the facility to be treated for asthma symptoms and was prescribed medication to assist with them. On 4/19/2024 the client had a doctor's appointment and the doctor did not prescribe an inhaler, but assessed the client to have allergies. Since then, the client has had no other symptoms. LPA found the facility took the client to be treated for symptoms as required, and the facility was not informed prior to placement that the client needed an inhaler as the County Social Worker was not aware, and the client did not come to the facility with one. This case management is now closed, no further action necessary. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report was provided to him.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced Plan of Correction inspection at the facility and met with Administrator Steve Dogan, who assisted with the inspection. On 7/10/2024, the facility was cited: 87072(c)(11). The plan of correction that was agreed upon by LPA and Administrator was, "By POC due date of 7/11/2024 the ED and FM will have been refreshed on de-escalation techniques, observed by Admin, and will submit a document acknowledging the different steps that could have been taken prior to restraint." LPA advised Administrator on 7/10/2024 that even if the citation and finding was disagreed with, the POC still needs to be completed as required. On 7/11/2024, Administrator emailed LPA informing her that they would not be completing the POC as they will be appealing, which is their right to do so. However, the POC was still required to be completed. LPA and Admin further discussed the citation-->POC-->appeal process. On this date, the facility is being assessed a Failure to Correct Civil Penalty in the amount of $700, which is $100 per day that the citation was not corrected after the POC due date of 7/11/2024. Further failure to complete the POC will result in a continuation of $100 being assessed for every day the POC is not submitted. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to him.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Facility Manager Steven Anderson, who assisted with the inspection. The purpose of this case management inspection is to deliver the findings to the case management which was investigated by the Department's Investigations Branch Investigator (IB) Nathan Gonzalez, regarding an incident report received by the Department on 4/15/2024 by the facility. The reported incident stated that one client (C1) had been sexually assaulted when C1 was forced by a client (C2) to perform oral sex on C2 on the night of 4/15/2024. See confidential names list dated 8/9/2024. IB conducted this investigation by reviewing police reports, facility file information, and by conducting confidential interviews with one County Social Worker, three clients, three staff, the facility Administrator, and the facility Program Director, on 5/1/2024, 5/21/2024, 5/23/2024, 6/20/2024, 7/13/2024, 7/17/2024, and 7/23/2024. IB had also requested staff and Administrator write-ups relating to the incident from the Program Director on 7/17/2024, 7/26/2024, and 7/30/2024, which IB never received. IB found through their investigation that on 4/16/2024 a staff informed the Program Director that a non-consensual sexual encounter had occurred between clients. Clients were interviewed by Law Enforcement (LE) and informed LE that they were forced to smoke marijuana with C2 and play truth or dare. During truth or dare, C2 forced C1 to perform oral sex on them, under threat of physical violence. One staff (S1) was present at the facility during this incident and had called the Administrator of the facility, who was the on-call staff that night, three times for assistance with other escalated client behaviors with no response. S1 admitted to feeling that she, "neglected," some of the clients who were upstairs during her shift. Staff reported to IB that they are directed to supervise clients from the upstairs media room during overnight shifts, and S1 acknowledged that she should have more effectively supervised the clients from the media room. Administrator confirmed to IB that he missed three calls from S1. Administrator informed IB that he and S1 were both reprimanded for this incident. The Program Director informed IB that staff are to follow the emergency phone call procedures when needing management assistance, however S1 did not think to do that in the moment. Based on information obtained by IB, IB found that S1 and Administrator failed to provide adequate supervision to clients during the early morning of 4/15/2024, which resulted in C2 sexually assaulting C1 while in care. On this date the facility is being cited for violations of the California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division 6, Chapter 1, Section 80078(a), Responsibility for Providing Care and Supervision, and Section 80044(c), Inspection Authority. See attached LIC809-D. An exit interview was conducted with FM, and a copy of this report, confidential names list, advisory note, and appeal rights were provided to him.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Facility Manager Tom Hermann, who assisted with the inspection. Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess and Regional (RM) Manager Margo Castaneda made an announced case management inspection at a separate location and met with Tegre Miles, Executive Director (ED), and Reyes Bonilla Program Director (PR) who assisted with the inspection. Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs) Tamara Hill and Orlando Areizaga made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Steven Anderson, Administrator to discuss the inspection. On 2/3/ The Licensee, MSK Solutions, was informed by the Department's Audit Section that they will be receiving a solvency audit for both of their licensed STRTPs: Mile High Legend Home #487005982 and Mile High Mountain Top #487005059. The Department informed the Licensee of the reason for the audit, and all required information needed to perform the audit. The due date for submission of the required information was 3/3/2025. On 3/7/2025, the Department followed up with the Executive Director (ED) Tegre Miles regarding not having received the required documents to conduct the audit, nor a request for an extension of time. On 3/12/ ED responded with their concerns, and that they intended to finish everything by the coming Friday (3/14/2025). The Department responded to ED addressing their concerns and granting an extension until 3/14/2025. Failure to submit the required documents would result in the completion of the audit, documenting noncompliance with the Department's Inspection Authority. On 3/17/2025, ED responded to the Department with their concerns, however no documentation was provided. On this date the facility is being cited for violations of the California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division Chapter 1, Section 80044(c) Inspection Authority of the Licensing Agency, Section 80062(a) Finances, Section 80063(a) Accountability, and Section 80064(a) Administrator Qualifications and Duties. A repeat civil penalty in the amount of $250 is assessed for violation of Section 80044(c). Civil penalties in the amount of $100 per day will continue to accrue until the POC is met. LPA Hill did advise the administrator, Mr. Anderson, that while they have a plan of correction date of 5/15/25, civil penalties will continue to accrue on the citation related to Inspection Authority until the documents have been provided to the Audit Section per the request. LPA Hill advised the agency that they need to provide the requested documents as soon as possible to prevent further accrual of the civil penalties. LPA Hill advised that the civil penalties include an initial penalty of $250 plus $100 per day until the document(s) have been provided per the audit request. An exit interview was conducted with Mr. Anderson and a copy of this report and appeal rights was provided

narrative: On January 06, 2023, at 2:20 am, Licensing Program Analyst's (LPA's) Eduardo Barragan and Lucero Jauregui went to Milestone Group Home and met with Beverly Boone, Executive Director and Desiree West, Clinical Director.. The purpose of this visit was to address a deficiency that was noted. On November 09, 2022, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Lucero Jauregui and Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Ann Vallenzuella were at the facility and they overheard staff calling C1 by a name that C1 did not identify as. C1 then started yelling at staff saying, "I already told you that's not my name," yet the staff continued to call C1 by the name that he did not identify as. Additionally, on December 08, 2022, LPA's Barragan and Jauregui came to the facility to speak with a client and staff. While visiting on December 08, 2022, LPA's were informed that C1 was not being called the name that he identified as. C1 stated that he had verbally told staff the name he identified as, yet staff was refusing to call C1 the name that he identifies as because "they felt uncomfortable." LPA's then spoke with Beverly Boone, Executive Director about the concern and Beverly Boone mentioned that some staff did not feel comfortable with calling C1 by his preferred name; therefore, staff wouldn't call C1 by the name. Based on interviews, the Licensee did not ensure that C1 was accorded dignity within his personal relationships with staff, due to staff not calling him by his preferred name One deficiency is being cited on today's visit. An exit interview was conducted and plans of correction were discussed. A copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to Beverly Boone, Executive Director and Desiree West, Clinical Director.

Multiple confidential interviews disclosed that the grievance protocol is posted on the wall. LPA observed the grievance protocol and complaint hotline number posted in the facility. During a previous visit, LPA noticed that on the LIC 500, multiple staff members have the title of Administrator. Also, during previous interviews, multiple staff members referred to multiple other staff members as administrators. CCL expectations and standards are that each facility only has one administrator. During the staff interviews, LPA determined that only one staff member fulfills the roles and duties of the administrator, while the other staff just carry the title. The facility is not in violation of any rules or regulations, but LPA is advising a language and title change for the facility to only reference and reflect one administrator per facility. This will remove any confusion and set proper expectations for each facility for roles and responsibilities based on who is ultimately in charge/responsible as the facility administrator. No deficiencies cited. Exit interview conducted. LPA left a copy of this report.
