narrative: During that AWOL incident, the client ingested glass in the presence of staff when they caught up to her and was hospitalized because of it. LPA addressed the client's dangerous ingestion of harmful objects previously with the facility during Case Managements dated 3/13/2020 and 6/25/2020. On 6/25/ LPA issued an advisory notice advising staff to ensure they take into consideration clients' previous behavior patterns to assess at what point they should physically intervene when a client is being unsafe. The same client ingested glass pieces and broke her tooth while biting a pen during an incident that lasted from 2: PM to 3: PM on 3/30/2020. Staff did not physically intervene until after the client was able to self harm by ingesting the items. During IB's investigation an individual stated that the client needed 1 on 1 supervision. IB found that the lack of supervision allegation that a resident was hospitalized from incident that occurred while in care is SUBSTANTIATED, or true. Additionally in IB's investigation there were statements made about staff treating the clients poorly. This was addressed by LPA during a Case Management dated 12/23/2020. LPA cited the facility on that date. During IB's investigation, another staff's name was mentioned who treated the clients poorly, however that staff no longer works at the facility. IB found that the facility did not report the incident to the authorized representatives timely. The mother of the child did not know there was an incident until she was contacted by the hospital days later requesting permission to anesthetize the client in the hospital. The assigned County Social Worker was not notified until days after with a partial report. Then, the CSW received a full report the following week. IB found the allegation that the facility did not report the incident to the authorized representatives to be SUBSTANTIATED, or true. On this date the facility is being cited for violations of the California Code of Regulation, Title 22, Division 6, Sections 80078(a) and 80061(f). At 11: AM an exit interview was conducted with Administrator. A copy of this report and appeal rights was emailed to Administrator with a read receipt which will serve as her signature.

narrative: Regarding the allegation that staffs' behavior posed a risk to clients in care, this concerned two areas - staff being on their phones and not paying attention to clients, and one male staff being inappropriate with one client in care. During interviews, all but one interview corroborated that the male staff was not inappropriate towards that client, even when the client was being inappropriate towards him. The staff met with the client and the client's therapist to help in setting boundaries. The staff made all attempts and efforts to stay away from that client. LPA found no basis in the accusation that this staff was inappropriate towards the client. LPA learned that staff used to be on their phones sometimes when they were not supposed to. The facility addressed this at the time by discussing phone rules with them while they are working. Even though staff would be on their phones sometimes during working hours, they also communicated with each other about work, or taking work notes. While the staff may or may not have been on their phones when they weren't supposed to be, there was not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that this did or did not pose a risk to clients in care, therefore LPA has found this allegation to be unsubstantiated. Regarding the allegation that staff withheld food from clients while in care, statements made during interviews were conflicting. All staff denied this allegation occurred. Two clients stated it occurred, however gave different stories about how it occurred. One client denied this ever occurred. Based on the conflicting information, LPA found that while this allegation may have occurred or is valid, there was not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that it did or did not occur, therefore LPA has found it to be unsubstantiated. For the allegation claiming that staff inappropriately restrained a client while in care, LPA also received conflicting information. Two clients stated they have not been in, nor observed an inappropriate restraint from any staff. All staff denied inappropriately restraining any client in care. One staff stated that one staff does grip too tightly during restraints, but does not bend or twist the client in an inappropriate way; the holds are appropriate. Based on the conflicting information, LPA found that while this allegation may have occurred or is valid, there was not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that it did or did not occur, therefore LPA has found it to be unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted with FM, and a copy of this report and appeal rights was emailed to FM with a read receipt which will serve as the record of receipt.

narrative: One staff stated clients were not denied any meals, "unless they were off baseline and weren't acting right we'd be like, 'you get a snack,' it's too late for dinner." The staff stated that even when they made the snacks (items like chicken nuggets or something similar), the clients always ate something, and this happened on at least two occasions. One staff denied that clients had food withheld and stated if there were escalations during mealtime they would call another staff over to help and ensure the clients got to eat. Another staff stated if there were escalations during dinner time, the clients would get sandwiches. The Clinician and Administrator had no knowledge of food being withheld. Regarding the allegation that staff caused an injury to minor in care, confidential interviews revealed the following: one client does not remember that happening. One client stated they do not think this happened. Another client stated there was an escalation one time where a staff grabbed a client by the wrist, hard, which was not during a restraint. One client stated they had bruises and their arm hurt after being restrained. That client stated the staff intentionally hurt them and grabbed them hard. The client also stated they did not receive medical care for the injury, however this was unable to be corroborated. All staff and Administrators denied having knowledge that medical care was not obtained when any client needed it. One staff stated they never witnessed any staff hurting a client. One staff stated they have hurt a client before unintentionally during restraints due to clients squirming, however when told that the client was hurting, the staff loosened their grip or rearranged. When asked if the staff has ever lashed out physically to a client, the staff admitted that they may have held onto a client tighter. The Clinician stated that staff have, "probably," hurt a client during a restraint because that's the nature of them, "the fight between bodies." One staff thought they remembered one client's arm hurting after a restraint but did not remember the details. Both Administrators had no knowledge of this occurring. While staff may have unintentionally caused discomfort to clients during restraints, there was not a preponderance of the evidence that staff caused injury to them. Although the allegations may have happened or are valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violations did or did not occur, therefore the allegations are unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted with FM and a copy of this report and appeal rights was left with her. When one Administrator was asked what does taking clients' shoes after an AWOL have to do with safety, the Administrator stated, "if the client shoes were taken we would go back and look at why were the shoes taken for AWOLing, it would just have to be looking at who that kid was and why," which did not answer the question. The Administrator stated that sometimes clients AWOLed with no shoes on. The Clinician confirmed that staff took away clients' shoes, but stated clients were not made to go outside without their shoes. When LPA asked one staff what the circumstances would be that a client would not have their shoes, the staff stated, "if they AWOLed and they wouldn't have shoes." LPA asked the staff if that is because staff would take clients' shoes if they AWOLed, which they responded yes." This instruction came from the supervisors. Two staff and one Administrator stated that clients would also AWOL without their shoes. Interviews with staff revealed client shoes would be confiscated from clients for up to two days. When LPA asked one staff why the shoes are taken away, the staff stated, ""so it's easier to restrain [them] and not let [them] run away." When LPA asked one staff if a particular client had to be outside without shoes on, the staff confirmed and stated, ""we took [the client's] shoes off all the time, well not all the time, but it was more of a repeated offence in the same day, so we would take [the client's] shoes." Interviews with clients revealed that clients did have to be outside without their shoes on. One client stated that they would have to go to the, "timeout shelter," outside when the client was off baseline. This included when the client did not have any shoes on, and the client was not permitted to put them on. Another client stated when they went outside their shoes were confiscated, so the client was not able to put them on. The client also stated that on one occasion they had to go outside in the timeout shelter with no shoes on when it was rainy and cold outside. Staff confirmed that the timeout shelter was used to take timeouts for the clients. Another client stated their shoes were taken away for it, "being a danger," that they would AWOL, and they had to do PE outside with no shoes. Two clients stated the shoes would be confiscated for up to a week. LPA learned from interviews with staff that they are no longer taking clients' shoes, and this only happened in the past. Based on interviews LPA conducted, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegation is found to be SUBSTANTIATED. Although the facility is now a Group Home, at the time of this allegation they were still a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program, therefore Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 3.1 (2020), Section 87072(d)(11), Personal Rights is being cited on the attached LIC 9099D. An exit interview was conducted with FM, and a copy of this report and appeal rights was left with her.

narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess had a call with Administrator Misty Jackson to complete this case management inspection. LPA met with Administrator via Google Duo, a video conferencing application. LPA also met with Administrator Kamiko Lucas. At 9: AM, LPA conducted a virtual walk-through of the facility, led by Administrator. LPA observed no deficiencies. CCL received an incident report on 10/27/2020 dated 10/19/2020 reporting that during a facility outing on a hike, client C1 (see confidential names list dated 11/5/2020) appeared tired at the end. C1 stopped to take a break and staff waited with her. Staff noticed C1 becoming disoriented by mumbling her words. Client then collapsed and was unresponsive. Staff called for assistance and 911. Other staff arrived with water for C1 but C1 was unresponsive. First responders arrived 15 minutes later and client was transported to a hospital, and later transported to a different hospital and a Liver Transplant unit for further treatment. On the same hike, another client, C2, became dehydrated. LPA is investigating what was provided to clients during the hike as far as food and water, why client went to the Liver Transplant unit, and what the outcome is. The incident report did not describe the outcome of C1's health. In speaking with Administrators Misty Jackson and Kamiko Lucas, LPA learned that C1 brought her own 32 ounce water bottle on the hike and had it refilled once, as well as got an additional 8 ounces. Clients had lunch for 1 hour. The hike was 7 miles, easy level, and they could go as slow as they wanted. C1's condition is improving and she did not need a liver transplant. LPA collected contact information for staff and C1's parents. LPA learned that C2 was provided with food and water as well. This case management requires further investigation into C1's case before a resolution can be made. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator Lucas, and a copy of this report was emailed to her with a read receipt which will serve as her signature.

facility_name: MOUNTAIN VALLEY CHILD AND FAMILY-BAR DU
narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess had a call with Administrator, Misty Jackson, to deliver this case management inspection. LPA met with Administrator via Google Duo, a video conferencing application. On 7/24/ CCL received an incident report dated 7/19/2020 describing a client in crisis who left the facility and walked to Walmart. While in Walmart, the client hid from staff, grabbed some items, went into the bathroom, then left Walmart. The client approached strangers asking them to call Law Enforcement (LE), but they did not respond. Staff attempted to talk to the client but the client was not receptive and ran away to a nearby Shell gas station where she again solicited help in calling LE, but was denied. LE arrived and the client told them that she was being mentally abused at this facility. LE counselled the client and eventually she returned to the facility. The client wanted to call her mother and someone else that she was not permitted to call. Staff asked the client to take a time-out before the call with her mother. The client left the facility again and LE was called. LE attempted to talk to the client but the client walked back towards the facility and picked up rocks and threw them at the facility vehicle, breaking the windshield and driver side window. LE detained the client in handcuffs and returned her back to the facility. Staff made a plan with the client and she was released from the handcuffs. The client started a time-out but stopped and picked up a "log-sized" stick and charged into the facility vehicle's windshield, breaking it more. LE instructed the client to put the stick down but she did not. LE pulled their taser out and threatened the client that they would use it if she did not put the stick down. The client refused and LE told her to get on her stomach, which she did. The client was then placed in handcuffs and detained once more. The client was taken to Juvenile Hall. LPA investigated this case management by interviewing six clients and three staff on 8/12/2020, 12/15/2020, and 12/23/2020. During interviews with clients, they stated at least one staff in particular has been speaking to clients in a way which is aggressive, intimidating, and mentally abusive. During LPA's interviews with the clients, both former and current, they brought up this staff's name independently and gave similar kinds of examples for how this staff spoke to them and others in an inappropriate or abusive way. During LPA's interviews with staff, they denied that staff had said the things that were alleged. Staff stated that the accused staff is a firm or strict staff, but denied any abusive behavior. The accused staff denied all abusive claims, but did state that she has had trouble with her tone and how she comes off to the clients. The staff stated that because of that she could possibly be seen as abusive by the clients, however that is not the case. The staff stated she has been working on this issue with her tone of voice, as well as keeping the clients accountable so they can successfully graduate from the program. The staff recognized that she needed to correct her tone because the clients can come from environments in which people were abusive. The staff explained that she is the staff that enforces rules and holds the clients accountable, which they do not like. Based on all the information given, it is evident that while the staff many not have set out to intentionally cause harm to the clients with the way she speaks, that is the effect it has had on the clients. Clients stated this has created a negative affect on their mental health and emotional health, and has affected their behavior and program success. The way the staff speaks to the clients is at times not trauma-informed and has resulted in the clients feeling mentally abused. On this date the facility is being cited for a violation of the Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 3.1, Section 87072(d)(11). At 4: PM, an exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report along with appeal rights was sent to her by email with a read receipt which will serve as her signature.

narrative: Licensing Program Analysts (LPA) Alyssa Burgess and Monica Roberts made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Administrator (Admin) Misty Jackson and Facility Manager (FM) De'Jana Crockett, who assisted with the inspection. LPAs and staff conducted a walk-through of the facility and found there to be clean and adequate bedding, supplies, an adequate amount of perishable and non-perishable food, the house was at a comfortable temperature, there were no obstructions in the halls or walkways, and there was an adequate amount of silverware, plates, and cups and they were in good condition. LPAs observed one window screen in an unoccupied client room to be in disrepair, the excess refrigerator in the shed to be dirty, and ziplock bags in the chemical cabinet, which would be used for food. LPA instructed staff to move the ziplock bags, that the refrigerator needs to be cleaned, and the screen repaired. License and complaint procedure were posted. LPAs observed the facility vehicle to have a cracked windshield, spidering across the entire windshield in three directions, the air conditioning in the car works, and the car turned on. LPAs observed no evidence of smoking in the facility or on the grounds as required. There was no cushioned material under the swingset, and the swingset was secured to the ground as required. There was a vent grate coming off of the side of the trailer building, which needs to be secured. The kitchen water temperature measured at 129.5, which is above the required range of 105 to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. The blinds in the kitchen were not clean. LPAs reviewed the clients' allowances and found all to be accurate. LPAs reviewed the client medications and found all Medication Administration Records to have all required elements on them, and all client medications were maintained appropriately. LPA reviewed the disaster drill logs and found the facility to be conducting them as required. On this date the facility is being cited for a violation of the California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Division 5, Chapter 1, Section 80074(c) Transportation, and 80087(a) Buildings and Grounds. narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced case management inspection at the facility and met with Facility Manager (FM) De'jana Crockett who assisted with the inspection. LPA spoke with staff and clients regarding the facility. During confidential interviews with three staff, one Administrator, one Clinician, and two clients, LPA found that in the past around 2020, clients have been made to be outside for extended periods of time, and denied entrance into the facility. One client stated a client had to stay outside the facility for a few hours after returning from an AWOL. Another client stated they were not allowed inside of the facility because they were a, "danger," to the others. The client stated they were outside for the whole day, and this happened on about three occasions. One staff confirmed that client had been outside for many hours before, and was not allowed inside. The staff described that client as a, "trouble-maker." The client had AWOLd and was self-harming. The client had repeatedly run away that day and when returned, the staff and another staff were told to keep the client isolated and in timeout, so for a half a day, that client was made to stay outside in the timeout spot. When LPA asked that staff if the client was ever outside overnight, the staff stated no, however, "for almost all day [the client] would be out there for her not being respectful or being off baseline. We would separate [the client] from the girls and let her be isolated." LPA asked the staff how often that client or other clients would be left outside like that and the staff stated, "if I had to guess...[the client] was our main problem-child and we had to deal with her everyday and I would say she was out there four to five times a week...when she was bad, she was bad, so we would rather have her outside than disrupting the group inside." The staff stated that client was, "out there sometimes all day." When LPA asked the staff if that client had to be outside in the dark, the staff confirmed the client did. When LPA asked the staff if the client was locked out of the facility, the staff confirmed, and stated it was because the client wanted to harm the other clients inside the facility so the client was locked outside to protect the other clients inside. One staff stated that if clients are escalated outside, they do not want the clients to come inside and harass the other clients, or break things, so they keep them outside. Another staff confirmed that clients have to stay outside the facility until they are calm. LPA asked the staff about the client being locked outside, with staff there, and the staff confirmed this, stating, "yeah, until she calmed down." The Clinician confirmed that one of the clients was kept outside a lot, and not allowed back in. The Clinician explained, "their standard is they have to show they are back in program to come back in." The Administrator stated they do not keep clients outside for hours, "but an incident could last for hours with a client that's outside." The Administrator also confirmed that clients could be outside in the timeout shelter at nighttime if they are off baseline. Administrator also confirmed that if a client is outside and wants to come in to harm another client, they are not allowed inside. Based on the collective information gathered, LPA found that the facility inappropriately kept clients outside of the facility. Although the facility is now a Group Home, at the time this occurred they were still a Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program, therefore Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards, Version 3.1 (2020), Section 87072(d)(11), Personal Rights is being cited on the attached LIC 9099D. An exit interview was conducted with FM, and a copy of this report and appeal rights was left with her.

And (c)(8)(B) "All restrictions shall be documented in the child's needs and service plan or the facility's discipline policies, and be signed by the child's authorized representative." narrative: The first allegation is whether "Direction Following" and timeouts outside during days of extreme heat were inappropriate forms of discipline. Online research concluded there were 12 days in August and 9 days in September 2022 that temperatures exceeded 100 degrees, of which 10 were consecutive days. However, resources did not conclude on a specific duration that was unhealthy to be outside but identified other risk factors to consider like water intake, type of clothing, and specific time of day. The facility's program statement regarding their "Positive Discipline Policies" does not include specifics on direction following and timeouts. In addition, the agency does not have an extreme weather policy that addresses how their program will adjust client discipline or other outdoor activities. All client interviews reported generally being outside up to 20 minutes for disciplinary type reasons. However, due to the other risk factors are unknown like water intake, type of clothing, and specific time of day, it is not possible to determine if the regular discipline practices were inappropriate during this specific time. The next allegation is whether staff is rude or yells at clients. All staff and client interviews lacked any specific details or situations that could be compared or corroborated. Interviews were consistent that some clients and staff talk loudly in the facility, but less clear if the yelling is directed at clients. Some interviews said there were no incidents of disrespectful or rude behavior or language by staff. However, since inadequate details were available, it is not possible to confirm whether the allegation occurred or not. Based on the investigation, records reviewed and interviews conducted, the complaint finding is UNSUBSTANTIATED at this time meaning that although the allegations may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred. narrative: LPA found that sometimes, "Animal Direction Following," is employed, which consists of various relatively quick tasks the clients have to do to tend to the animals to make up for time out of program, specific to the animals. Based on interviews with all staff and clients, LPA learned this is not done for an excessive amount of time. Additionally, staff will take off more time the clients have to work off, than the client actually worked off doing the extra chore. Direction Following in general is when a client is out of program, they accrue time they then have to work off by doing another chore. Based on interviews with all staff and clients, LPA learned that during, "barn chores," staff help the clients clean the animal stalls and tend to the animals. These tasks take about 45 minutes to an hour, and the duty is rotated between the two Mountain Valley houses. Some clients felt that barn chores was a punishment because they did not like doing the tasks. Based on information gathered from all interviews, the barn chores and Animal Direction Following are not inappropriate discipline, and are not unreasonable. LPA found during interviews with the clients, staff, and Clinicians that an SLL is utilized when a client harms themselves or are generally being unsafe. When asked what consequences/punishments are given to clients, one Facility Manager (FM) first stated, "a safety level lower--anything that's self-harming, cutting, dangerous behaviors, that's a red. So, that just means like if we go on outings, they're not safe enough to go on outings for that week." LPA asked that FM why clients are punished for being unsafe and the FM stated that it is not a punishment, but restrictions put on the client because they are not being safe to go on an outing. FM stated that some clients do take it as a punishment. During LPA's interview with one Clinician, when asked what consequences are given, the Clinician also mentioned the SLL, and one of the reasons given for how a client can get that is by self-harming. LPA found that the way an SLL is framed, it can be perceived as a punishment for being unsafe. During interviews, three clients felt that a SLL for self-harm behavior was a punishment/consequence. Due to this ambiguity, LPA has found the allegation that staff inappropriately disciplined children in care to be unsubstantiated. While the SLL itself is not inappropriate, nor is it disciplinary, it has been perceived as such by the clients. LPA is issuing an advisory note to the facility to modify this framework and language used surrounding SLLs. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violation did or did not occur, therefore the allegation is unsubstantiated. An exit interview was conducted with Administrator and a copy of this report along with appeal rights was left with her. narrative: The incident of this complaint was said to have potentially occurred during class time when the two Mountain Valley facilities combined clients for school for a period of time, where C1 touched another client's thigh and near their private parts. LPA learned that this class arrangement was due to the Teacher at the Gerber facility being out on leave from October 2023, and returning in the beginning of January 2024. During that time, the Bar Du teacher covered classes for about a month until another staff obtained their Teaching credentials and took over. During interviews with the staff and two teachers, one teacher stated C1 will, "push the limit," of the boundaries with other clients. One teacher informed LPA that when they observed C1 tickle another client's upper back, they immediately stopped it from happening and had C1 removed from the setting. The staff and two teachers all stated the clients from both houses were rarely at the same house at the same time. If the Bar Du house was in one room for class, the Gerber house was in another room. The staff stated that occasionally they would have joint times where they might watch a movie together. Both teachers and the staff have knowledge of C1's propensity to touch other clients. The staff did not have any knowledge of C1 inappropriately touching the other client, and neither teacher remembered a time they were together. One client who was affected during the previous incidents in 2023 informed LPA that since that time, C1 has not been touching other clients inappropriately. The client informed LPA that staff do intervene and tell any client pushing boundaries to stop, however the clients do not listen. Additionally, C1, "usually does it when staff aren't looking." Staff follow clients around, and clients have to ask staff before going anywhere, including the hall and to their room, to maintain supervision. C1 denied having any connection with the other client they were alleged to have touched inappropriately for this complaint, that they rarely saw them, and staff would separate them, and be more watchful of C1; staff would have more staff present and make sure no one gets too close. C1 denied inappropriately touching the other client and informed LPA that since the previous incidents that were investigated in 2023, C1 has not been touching any clients. C1 informed LPA when other clients go into each others' rooms, staff tells them to get out of their room, and staff watch in the hallway. C1 stated that when dating, there is no touching, no boundary crossing, and staff are, "extra watchful." C1 stated if they are sitting too close, they have to move apart, and they cannot be alone with each other. Also, staff listen to the conversations they have with each other. C1 is romantic-relationship-focused and regularly seeks out clients to form relationships with. During an interview with a client who has been recently romantically involved with C1, the client informed LPA that staff were aware of their relationship and enforced heightened rules of keeping boundaries, no sitting close, no note passing, no reading each others' things, no sitting on the same couch, and no whispering to each other. LPA was informed of one incident in which C1 touched their leg and they later informed the Clinician, who addressed it with C1. Additionally, C1 tickled their upper back one time, which the Teacher immediately addressed. The client stated staff watched them, "24/7." The client had no knowledge of C1 touching the other client inappropriately. Despite multiple attempts, LPA was unable to interview the client who was alleged to have been touched inappropriately. narrative: On 05/27/22, at 9: AM,, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Connie Goldie, met with Mental Health Worker (MHW) Anthony Tran to conduct an unannounced Annual/ Required inspection of a single story, four bedroom, 2 bath home. At 10: AM, MHW Tran greeted LPA Goldie and shared that Program Manager (PM) Misty Jackson was shopping.MHW stated that the census was 6 clients. PM arrived at 10: AM and stated that the current census was six clients. An Entrance Checklist was provided to the PM Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Connie Goldie conducted a tour with Misty of a 4 bedroom, two bath house that began at 10: AM outside.. LPA Goldie observed outdoor area free of debris and window screens in good repair. In the entry way LPA Goldie observed Foster Youth Rights were posted along with youth in care schedules. LPA Goldie advised PM to obtain updated Foster Youth Rights posters. We proceeded to the office area, where LPA Goldie observed the license, the emergency intervention plan, and locked and appropriately stored medication. LPA observed two shared bedrooms with clean linen, a closet and cubbies for personal belongings. Bedroom two had a non-functioning smoke detector and no batteries on had to replace. LPA Goldie stated this is an immediate safety risk and PM agreed. The tour continued to the kitchen where PM opened all cabinets, perishable food for two days and non-perishable food for five days, adequate table ware and clean sink and stove were observed. Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Tamara Hill, Angela Carmack, Licensing Program Manager III, Valerie Garrett, Staff Services Manager I, Specialist made an unannounced annual inspection on 9/17/24 at 10: AM and met with Misty Jackson, Program Manager. Licensing staff and Ms. Jackson conducted an inspection of the facility inside and out and observed that the facility was in substantial compliance with the physical plant, inside of the facility and outside. LPA Hill observed that the facility has a separate but attached room for clients to conduct schooling, therapeutic services, and activities. The facility is licensed for six ambulatory clients in two dual occupancy rooms, and two single occupancy rooms in the facility. Licensing staff observed that the agency has a separate animal area that contains chickens, horses, pigs, rabbits and that the clients in the facility are responsible for the care and upkeep of the animal areas as part of the animal therapy program and chores. LPA Hill observed that the facility had four different carbon monoxide detectors, two were in the kitchen and activity areas, one in the staff/administrator's office, and one in the hallway outside of the client sleeping area. Fire extinguishers were last services on 1/30/2024. Water in the client bathrooms measured 112 degrees Fahrenheit and the toilets and shower functioned as required. The facility had the required two day perishable food supply and the seven day nonperishable food supply as required. LPA Hill obtained updated copies of the COA Accreditation Certificate, Mental Health Program Approval certificate, Emergency Intervention Log, and facility sketch during the inspection. LPA Hill conducted interviews with staff and client in care. LPA Hill did advise the agency that the window tracks need to be cleaned and that the rug in the meeting room needs to be fixed as the adhesive appears to not be making contact and the rug is curling. LPA Hill did issue advisories during today's inspection related to Disaster Plan including the emergency power plan and preservation of medications (if refrigeration is needed) and the plan needs to be updated and staff training needs to be provided upon hire and annually, disaster drills need to be conducted on the overnight shift (which could be just having a conversation with the clients in care on what to do), Emergency Intervention Log needs to articulate the de-escalation techniques used prior to manual restraint/hold and it must be documented that licensee/administrator conducted a review of the restraint after the incident. LPA Hill also advised that clients should be able to articulate a child and family team meeting, what is in their needs and services plans and how that documents comes about from the Child & Family Team Meeting. When discussing this with Ms. Jackson, it was indicated that the facility is planning to transition back to Group Home but that there is no date set for that at this time. LPA Hill did not issue a citation for this as further discussion is needed about this as the agency indicated that they do IEP meetings, Individual Educational Plan Meetings where they discuss behaviors and that they call them IEPs because the placing agency is educational. LPA Hill advised the agency that the previous Program Statement and Plan of Operation was approved in 2018 but is not current to standards since their initial licensure. While the agency is planning to transition, they are not current with the Interim Licensing Standards, Version 5. If the agency does not transition to Group Home, they will need to update their current Program Statement and Plan of Operation to be consistent with the Version 5 of the Interim Licensing Standards. LPA Hill asked that the program advise their LPA on their plan. LPA Hill did request that the following documents to be sent to Licensing by October 1, 2024, for the update of the facility file: LIC610, Facility sketch of the grounds including all areas to be used or visited by youth in care, Surety Bond, and LIC309. No citations were issued during the inspection and all documents were provided at the conclusion of the annual inspection.

narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Alyssa Burgess made an unannounced annual inspection at the facility and met with Administrator Misty Jackson and Maintenance Staff/Supervisor Toby Briglia, who assisted with the inspection. The facility has not had any clients or staff in about four years. The facility has been empty and in-operational since then. LPA observed a kitchen, a dining room area, a living room, three bathrooms, classroom/office, staff office/laundry area, three client bedrooms, linen closets, and the outside areas which included the pool, the two storage structures, and the grounds. The facility does have a current Accreditation and Mental Health Approval, as well as a fire clearance. The license was present in the facility, but not posted. Clients personal rights were posted as required. The fire extinguisher was up to date. The rooms had all required equipment and furniture. There was bedding and other linens kept in bags in the closets. The mattresses were clean and in good repair. There was dust on surfaces throughout the house, along with some minute mouse droppings in several locations. There was some small dead gnats on the window sills. The electricity is operational and the sinks delivered hot water. The pool is surrounded by a fence which meets requirements, and has a lock to secure it. The outdoor activity space was in generally safe condition, however the wooden decking on the balcony had some planks which were sticking up and nails not fully nailed in. There was a swing-set which was anchored to the ground, however there was no protective material underneath it. The facility's board is meeting as required, and minutes were made available during the annual inspection at the Bar Du facility on 10/29/2024 & 10/30/2024. The facility has a program statement, and understands that all client and staff records need to be maintained as required if and when children are placed. First Aid box contained sufficient supplies and is located in the staff office in each house. LPA observed cleaning supplies and disinfectants to be locked during inspection. Medications are stored in the medical office and distributed by the nurse; the office is not accessible to clients. The passageways from the front to the back of the homes are unobstructed. Smoke detectors were tested and are in working order. LPA observed carbon monoxide monitors. Fire extinguishers are located in several locations within the facility, and are up-to-date. LPA observed both homes to be clean, safe, sanitary and in good repair. LPA Walker-Flores reviewed staff files and all which were reviewed were complete and up to date. Criminal record clearances were reviewed, and the facility is in compliance. Staff files reviewed have required training hours, education, and fingerprint clearances. Staff files contained Child Abuse, DOJ and FBI clearances. Child files were also reviewed. Medical consent forms were signed by authorized representative and current. Additionally, each child's file had a record of vaccinations and contained Identification and Emergency Information. Children's Needs and Services plans were reviewed. Foster Child (FC)5 and FC6 files did not contain Needs and Services plans and could not be produced or located during inspection. Administrator sent the Needs and Services plans to LPA via email after the LPA left the facility, however, these service plans did not contain required signatures. continued on 809C Facility cited per Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) 87070(c)(1) The following additional information shall be maintained in the child's record: a copy of the child's original needs and services plan; verification, signed by the child and his/her authorized representative(s), that they were offered the opportunity to participate in plan development and verification that the authorized representative(s) have approved the plan. Staff was distracted during medication distribution and accidentally administered psychotropic medications to FC1. Staff then directed FC1 to vomit. The complaint alleges that facility failed to report an incident to the appropriate parties. On 10/21/21, C1 was involved in a restraint that resulted in an injury which required a trip to the emergency room. LPA obtained emails that show the placing agency was not notified of the incident from the agency until 10/25/21. Documentation shows the district contacted the agency and requested the report. Based on the documentation and interviews, the agency did not report the incident to the appropriate parties according to regulation. The complaint alleges the client's mental health needs are not being met. Consistent statements in interviews indicate there was an incident where S2 allowed C1 to use her Amazon account. The incident resulted in S2 owing C1 the unused funds on the account and taking multiple weeks to return the money. This resulted in C1 being upset with his therapist. Statements in interviews and documentation show that C1 did not participate in therapy sessions and often refused. IEP team meeting notes show that C1's lack of participation in therapy could have been a result from the incident involving the Amazon account. IEP notes show that on 09/28/21 the incident was discussed, and a new therapist was requested by C1 and legal guardian which was denied. On 10/20/21 documentation shows C1 was still requesting a new therapist and sessions were not improving. During the meeting on 10/20/21 placing county requested a new therapist. Agency stated that they do not have any other therapist available. Placing agency requested services be contracted out which agency did not provide. C1 was discharged from the program on 11/19/21. Based on documentation and corroborated statements in interviews, the agency did not ensure mental health supports as appropriate to the needs of the child. Based on the information provided during interviews and gathered from documentation, it is determined the preponderance of evidence had been met therefore the allegations have been substantiated. On this date the facility is being cited for violations of the California Code of Regulation, Title 22, Division 6, Sections 87095. Documentation and Reporting Requirements and 87089.1(d) Mental Health. Exit interview conducted and appeal rights provided. Complaint alleges that a restraint resulted in further injury. C1 had a prior injury that occurred while skateboarding. C1 stated he fractured his wrist while skateboarding. On 09/30/ C1 was taken to the emergency room due to wrist pain following a restraint. A case management was conducted on 10/08/21 to follow up on the incident. Agency sent LPA an email which stated the team was reviewing alternatives to restraints but had concerns over safety. On 10/21/ C1 was again taken to the emergency room due to shoulder pain following a restraint. During the restraint, C1 threw his head back causing staff to sustain a bloody and swollen nose. Consistent statements in interviews show that C1 was a difficult child to restrain and seem to escalate during the process. C1 was discharged from the agency due to agency no longer being able to meet his needs and safely restrain him. Due to the prior injury and the behavior of C1, the allegation that a restraint resulted in further injury is unsubstantiated, meaning that although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violation occurred. Exit interview conducted and appeal rights given.

The purpose of the visit was to conduct a Required, Two-year Annual Inspection of the facility. The inspection was completed on 12.20.24. The facility was licensed on 12.23.22. LPA utilized the CARE Tool to complete the inspection. LPA conducted an inspection of the physical plant and checked for all necessary requirements. The facility was clean and organized and maintained an acceptable room temperature. The facility is on a large campus with many buildings. There are no more than 2 clients sharing a bedroom in a dorm like setting. The facility has 3 client bathrooms. All bathrooms were observed to be clean and fully functioning. The dining hall is separate from the dorms. Each client had a closet and dresser in good repair. Mattresses and bedding were observed to be clean. Clients were able to decorate their rooms with their personal belongings. The facility has a properly fenced pool, and opportunities for clients to access sports equipment. LPA observed the proper postings including facility license, complaint hotline, client personal rights, and emergency disaster plan. Smoke alarms, fire extinguishers and a first aid kit were observed to be current and within regulations. LPA observed the kitchen to have 3 restaurant sized refrigerators and freezers with at least 2 days of perishable food and 7 days of non-perishable food on hand. LPA observed client medications were stored in a locked file cabinet in the locked medical office. Client files are primarily electronic with paper files for clients locked in the Head of Service's office. The facility has no outstanding fees. The facility currently has 13 clients, with a licensed maximum capacity of 16. Staff to client ratio is 1 to 4. LPA reviewed 3 staff files. Staff files had completed criminal record clearances, and all required initial and annual training. All first Aide and CPR certifications were up to date for staff. Continued C LPA reviewed 3 client files. All clients had signed Admission Agreements on file. Client files had completed initial Needs and Services Treatment Plans, signed by clients and staff, and updated Needs and Service plans every 30 days. Needs and Service Plans detailed adequate supportive services the facility offers to the clients. Clients were current on physical and dental exams. Six were taking court ordered psychotropic medications and had current JV-220's on file. LPA interviewed 3 clients and 3 staff. No citations were given on this date. A signed copy of this LIC-809 and LIC 809C report was provided to Administrator An exit interview was conducted.

Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Tina Thorn arrived unannounced at the facility for the purpose of a case management following a record review of drug tests conducted on youth at the facility. Licensing Program Manager (LPM) Hillary Hall conducted the record review. LPM reviewed Incident reports, and records from the facility indicating 6 youth were drug tested 10 times during the time period of 8/24/24-12/27/24. Drug testing results provided to the Department did not include reported testing of 3 youth, referenced in an Incident report occurring 12/21/24. Of the 10 drug tests documented, three were done for reasons listed as return from home pass or day pass. All documented tests were negative for illegal substances. LPM reviewed the Program Statement for the facility and found no policies and procedures regarding drug testing youth. LPA Elena Soto-Gonzalez interviewed facility Head of Service on 12/30/24, who indicated the facility does drug testing when they have a concern the youth may have used illegal substances. LPM spoke with Program Director (PD) Paige Woodard on 2/4/2025 who indicated there were no known written or internal policies on drug testing the youth and the staff are not trained on drug testing. LPM spoke with representatives from five different Probation Departments. Two of these departments were unaware their youth had been drug tested at the facility, with one department specifically not authorizing the tests. Two departments had given verbal permission for the facility to drug test the youth, but were unaware policies or procedures were not outlined in the facility program statement regarding testing, with one of these counties choosing to no longer authorize testing by the facility. The fifth department contacted indicated they have not placed youth at the facility recently, but have detained multiple youth from the facility who had been drug tested following a return from home or a visit. One citation is being issued per Title Division 6, Section 80022(k): Plan of Operation: (k) The facility shall operate in accordance with the terms specified in the Plan of Operation and may be cited for not doing so. A signed copy of this 809 and 809D was provided to the facility.

On 05.15. Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Tina Thorn received an incident report regarding a verbal altercation between staff and youth preceding a physical restraint given by staff. On 05.27. LPA followed up with Paige Woodard, Program Director who agreed to email details about the incident. On 05.29. LPA received an email from Program Director explaining the incident in more detail. The email stated that the staff was placed on administrative leave while an investigation was being completed. On 06.04. Program Director called LPA to report that the staff had been terminated from his position due to inappropriate conduct. On 06.12. LPA spoke in person with Program Director as a follow-up and to request that written confirmation of staff's termination be sent to LPA. On June 24, LPA received an email from Program Director with written confirmation that the staff involved had been terminated on 06.04.25.

Regarding the allegation that staff inappropriately restrained a minor resulting in injuries and staff handled minor in a rough manner, LPA obtained photos of a minor who sustained bruising and fingernail mark injuries from staff after being in a restraint. No full serious incident report was submitted to the Department regarding the restraint to detail staff's involvement. The client indicated they were running away, which does not provide justification for use of physical restraint. Regarding a lack of supervision for the clients resulting in unsafe behaviors, there was an incident in which four clients were able to sneak out of their dorm rooms during the night unnoticed, to break into a principal's office. During the months of July-September 2024, 19 (24) hour serious incident reports were submitted to the Department without corresponding final reports being submitted. There were two reports involving the use of a restraint with no final report submitted to the Department. Staff interviewed were unable to explain to the LPA what the process is to report incidents. Based on LPA's observations, interviews which were conducted, and records reviewed, the preponderance of evidence standard has been met, therefore the above allegations are found to be Substantiated. Four citations are being issued for violating Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) Section 87061(i)(7)(E ):Incident Reports, ILS Section 87072(c)(17), Title 22, Section 80028(a): Responsibility for Providing Care and Supervision, and Title Section 80061(b): Reporting Requirements. A signed copy of this LIC-9099 report, the LIC-9099C, and LIC-9099D were provided to the facility. An exit interview was conducted. Appeal rights were provided. Regarding allegations of staff not addressing minors' health care needs, interviews with staff and clients indicated the facility has a medic on site. However, some interviews denied medical care as being available for clients when asked. Staff and clients reported that clients had access to three meals and a snack daily, but statements differed regarding the quality and quantity of the snacks, and the process for how to address when a client misses a meal. One staff reported that if a client acts up, they are not given a meal. Regarding the allegation of staff hitting a minor with a vehicle resulting in injuries, interviews were inconsistent. One staff reported that one client was hit by a golf cart and appeared to be injured, but when asked about their injuries, the client denied it. When LPA conducted additional client and staff interviews, none had knowledge of the incident. No incident report was submitted to confirm any other client or staff involvement. Regarding the allegation of staff not intervening when a minor engaged in self-harm, interviews were inconsistent. An incident did occur in the stabilization room involving electrical wiring. Client and staff interviews provided inconsistent statements regarding whether the wiring was exposed or not, and accessible to clients. LPA reviewed a video of a client pulling the electrical wire and getting shocked; however, interviews were inconsistent regarding whether there were holes or cracks in the electrical casing. Based on LPA's observations, interviews which were conducted, and records reviewed, although the allegations may have happened, or are valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the violations did, or did not, occur. Therefore, the allegations are UNSUBSTANTIATED. A signed copy of this LIC-9099 report, the LIC-9099C, and appeal rights were provided to the facility. An exit interview was conducted.

narrative: Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Nicole Strickland arrived unannounced to the facility to conduct interviews with Child #1 (C1) and Child #2 (C2) regarding former placement of C1 and C2 and not relating to this facility.

On November 8, 2021 at 9: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPAs), Jesus Cervantes, Sarah Alvizo, and Adrian Mendez, arrived at New Alternatives #5 to conduct an unannounced annual inspection. LPAs met with Administrator, Meaghan Critchlow, who led a tour of the facility. LPAs toured the facility inside and out at 9: AM. The facility is a one-story residence with ten bedrooms and eight bathrooms for the clients. There are currently nine clients in placement. The facility consists of a front house and back house. The front house is designated for the clinic, therapy room, visitation room, and staff offices. The back house consists of a common area, kitchen, pantry, laundry room, ten client bedrooms, eight client bathrooms, medication room, and one staff office. The client bedrooms are set up so there are two clients to a bedroom and one client per bed. Cleaning solutions and hazardous items were not observed to be stored in a locked room inside of the kitchen. At 10: AM LPA observed two 90 oz bottles of dish soap under the kitchen sink which was not locked and secured. This poses an immediate health, safety, or personal rights risk to the residents in care, the facility will be cited. The facility immediately secured the dish soap and secured them in a locked cabinet. At 10: AM, LPA observed expired food and spoiled vegetables in the facility client refrigerator. This poses an immediate health, safety or personal rights risk to persons in care. Facility immediately disposed of the spoiled and expired food. The client's bathrooms were observed to be clean. At 11: AM, the hot water in the client's bathroom was measured to be 108.1 degrees Fahrenheit which is within the appropriate range of 105 degrees to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. Sharp knives were stored in a locked kitchen drawer. Medications are stored inside of a locked cabinet in the medication room. The facility's smoke and carbon monoxide detectors were observed to be operable. The fire extinguishers are properly charged and serviced. There are no guns or weapons in the facility as stated by the administrator. The Personal Rights form and Foster Care Ombudsman poster were posted in the facility. See Page Two LPAs observed a minimum 7-day non-perishable and a 2-day perishable supply of food. The exterior of facility was also inspected and observed to be clean and the landscape well maintained. Emergency exits were free from obstruction. There is no swimming pool or other body of water located on the facility premises. Administrator, Meaghan Critchlow is present at the facility a minimum of 20 hours a week. Licensee has obtained Mental Health Certification and is valid through March 13, 2022. Licensee has obtained accreditation through CARF International and is valid through September 30, 2023. Personnel files are maintained on site. At 9: AM, LPA's reviewed ten of ten staff files. All files contained all required documentation per Title Regulations and Interim Licensing Standards (ILS). All appropriate personnel who require caregiver background checks did have criminal record and child abuse index check clearances. At 1: PM, LPAs reviewed nine client files for nine of nine clients and all files did have the necessary documents required per STRTP regulations. Based on this inspection, the facility is not in compliance. The facility is being cited for Title 22, Division Six, Regulation 80087(g), Disinfectants, cleaning solutions, poisons, firearms and other items that could pose a danger if readily available to clients shall be stored where inaccessible to clients. This poses an immediate health, safety, or personal rights risk to the residents in care. The facility is being cited for Title 22, Division Six, Regulation 80076(a)(7), (a) In facilities providing meals to clients, the following shall apply: (7) ...All foods shall be selected, transported, stored, prepared and served so as to be free from contamination and spoilage and shall be fit for human consumption. Food in damaged containers shall not be accepted, used or retained. Due to time constraints, LPA will return to the facility to conduct a continuation of staff and client interviews. Exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report, along with Appeal Rights was provided to Administrator, Meaghan Critchlow.

On May 8, 2024, at 09: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jacqueline Garcia met with New Alternatives Inc. # Short-Term Residential Treatment Program (STRTP), Administrator, Michael Armas, to deliver a case management deficiency report. During the review of an incident that occurred on 04/20/2024, information obtained from the Special Incident Report (SIR) that was submitted from the facility to Community Care Licensing (CCL) revealed a concern regarding a "Bear-Hug" one-person restraint was utilized to de-escalate a client in crisis. LPA reviewed the facility Emergency Intervention Plan provided in the Program Statement, which entails that staff are trained to use Pro-Act interventions. Pro-Act interventions do not include a "Bear-Hug" one-person restraint. This is a violation of STRTP Interim Licensing Standards Version 5, 87095.22 (a)(4) Emergency Intervention Plan. The facility is being cited for violation of STRTP Interim Licensing Standards Version 5, 87095.22 (a)(4) Emergency Intervention Plan. The emergency intervention plan is to be designed and approved, in conjunction with the licensee, by an individual with the qualifications of a behavior management consultant as defined in Section 87001(b)(1). "The plan must include procedures that explicitly include and support recognized trauma-informed principles, approaches, and trauma specific interventions, de-escalation and harm reduction techniques. The licensee will include descriptions and details in the written procedures to demonstrate how the licensee will ensure prevention of personal rights violations". A copy of the report was discussed and provided along with appeal rights to New Alternatives Inc. #5, Administrator, Michael Armas.

narrative: On November 7, 2024 at 09: AM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Sarah Lo, arrived unannounced at New Alternatives, Inc. # Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA was greeted and granted access by Susan Shannon, Senior Manager and Att Yuwana, Program Director, arrived shortly after. The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during the inspection. Susan Shannon, Senior Manager and Att Yuwana, Program Director led the physical inspection of the facility. The front building consists of a Therapy room, a Visitation room, a Clinic office, a Quality Assurance office, a Residential Director, a Clinic Director office, and an activity room. The back building consists of nine bedrooms, seven toilets rooms, one half bathroom and one full bathroom. There is a common area with a couch and television for clients to rest, a staff office, a dining room, a kitchen, a laundry area, a storage room and a medication room. There is a shed in the backyard of the facility used to store miscellaneous items. All bedrooms have individual beds and drawer space for each client. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed and no more than two clients share a bedroom. LPA began a physical plant inspection and included the following checks: Facility grounds are clean, free of debris and hazards free. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. Books, TV, basketball court, bicycles, scooters, roller skates and games were observed for client's recreation time. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors were tested and observed to be in working order; there are two fire extinguishers in the front building and four fire extinguishers in the back building and are properly charged and serviced. LPA observed a minimum 7-day non-perishable and a 2-day perishable supply of food to prepare the items on the posted menu. There was a variety of snacks available for clients as well. (continued on LIC 809c) Refrigerators are located in the front and back building and are maintained in a good temperature. The facility outside grounds was also inspected and it was observed to be clean and well maintained. Emergency exits were free from obstruction. All required forms are posted including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster, the Emergency Disaster Plan, etc. The medications are locked and centrally stored in the back building inside a locked room. The medication records were reviewed and observed to be completed with dates and staff initials on dispensing records. The chemicals/poisons are locked in a closet inside the kitchen area in the back building and inside the staff room in the front building. All sharp objects are locked and stored in the locked cabinet in the kitchen area. There are two First Aid Kits and are stored in the medication room and in the front office. Individual beds were observed with clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. Seven bedrooms contained two twin beds and two bedrooms contained one twin bed. The facility has seven toilets that are attached to the bedrooms with two bedrooms sharing one toilet, one half bathroom containing a shower and bathtub and one full bathroom containing a shower, bathtub and toilet for the clients to use. The hot water in the client's bathrooms were deemed safe and measured between 105 to 120 degrees Fahrenheit. Per Susan Shannon, Senior Manager, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. The Program Director, Att Yuwana, is present at the facility a minimum of 20 hours a week, as verified by staff schedule. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during this inspection. The facility employs one Program Director, four Supervisors, twelve Child Care Workers, one Clinical Director, and two Clinicians. The board of director meeting minutes were provided. Licensee has obtained National Accreditation through CARF and the Accreditation is valid through September 30, 2026. The facility annual licensing fees are paid to current. Licensee has mental health approval and good until March 13, 2025. LPA reviewed five out of seven client files during the time of inspection and each file met the minimum requirement per the Interim Licensing Standards (ILS). All client records reviewed had the required documents including admission agreements, personal rights, medical history, immunization records, medical consent form, and an initial or updated needs and services plan on file. Client files were kept in a locked file cabinet within the staff office. (continued LIC 809c) LPA reviewed five staff files and each file met the minimum requirement per the Interim Licensing Standards (ILS). All personnel records reviewed have the verification of Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigations, and Child Abuse Index Check clearances. All staff have proof in file of acknowledging confidentiality and mandated child abuse reporting requirements. All personnel records reviewed met the required education and experience requirement. All personnel records reviewed had a completed physical exam on file. Due to time constraint, the annual inspection will be continued at a later date to conduct staff and client interviews. Based on the findings of today's visit, the facility will be cited for one Type B violation. A exit interview was conducted. A copy of the report was discussed and provided along with appeal rights to Att Yuwana, Program Director.

narrative: It was reported that clients were able to use the staff shower however, clients were refusing to use the restroom due to the restroom being dirty. Confidential interviews revealed that sometime in late October to early November, a plastic panel was installed in the bathroom shower located near clients' rooms. Confidential interviews revealed that the need to install the plastic panel was due to water continuously falling out of the shower causing water damage to the wall and base board of the bathroom. Confidential interviews revealed that the panel was installed in phases and after completely being installed, clients were unable to use it for the sealant to completely dry. Confidential interviews revealed that a sign was added to the shower informing clients not to use it. Confidential interviews did not reveal an exact time of how long the note remained posted and how long the shower remained in out of use status. Confidential interviews revealed that clients were instructed to use the second full bathroom located in the facility which can be used by both clients and staff. Confidential interviews revealed that staff informed clients to utilize the alternative bathroom shower while the other remained inoperable. Confidential interviews revealed clients were not utilizing the alternative shower due to it being small and "dirty" however, other confidential interviews revealed that the shower was not dirty but rather old. During a walk-through inspection completed by LPA Saeteurn on November 14, 2024, LPA Saeteurn was able to confirm that the shower located in the bathroom near client rooms had a plastic panel added and was being used once again by clients. Additionally, an inspection of the alternative bathroom near the facility kitchen revealed the shower was smaller in size compared to the bathroom near client bedrooms, and it appeared worn with superficial cracks on the tile flooring. Confidential interviews revealed that clients are encouraged to clean after themselves, however, the facility has also hired staff who are responsible for the cleaning of the facility. Additionally, during the walk through performed by LPA Saeteurn on November 14, 2024, a staff member was seen cleaning the facility grounds. Based on interviews and observations, the allegation that facility staff did not ensure client's shower was clean and in good repair is unsubstantiated. Although the allegation may have happened or is valid, there is not a preponderance of evidence to prove the alleged violation occurred. Continued... An exit interview was conducted with Tracey Renwick, Facility Administrator. A copy of this report and appeal rights were provided and reviewed with Tracey Renwick, whose signature on this report confirms receipt of these documents.

On December 19, 2024, at 2: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jacob Salem met with New Alternatives #16 (NA) Michelle Jenks, Administrator to deliver a case management deficiencies report. According to information obtained by Community Care Licensing (CCL), the female clients' personal rights were not upheld during contraband searches that occur when clients return to the facility after school. Confidential interviews indicated that after female clients were asked to lift their bra wire, they were also instructed to jump repeatedly and shake their bra. Confidential interviews indicated that these contraband searches occurred primarily outside by the front gate and that female clients were checked next to or within seeing distance of male staff and peers. A confidential interview indicated that participating in this search with males present caused discomfort and embarrassment for at least one client in care. Confidential interviews indicated that female clients who attend a different school went through the contraband search process inside a private office with no other clients present or within line of sight. Confidential interviews indicated that the bra check described above occurred regularly for female clients, rather than as a response to suspected possession of contraband. Confidential interviews indicated that staff apply disciplinary consequences when clients refuse to participate in the bra check. Conflicting confidential interviews indicated that clients are allowed to refuse the bra check, but that staff place clients who refuse on enhanced supervision. Confidential interviews indicated that staff do not touch clients during the contraband search process. Based on confidential interviews, the facility is being cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards version 5, section Personal Rights (c)(15) "The licensee shall ensure that each child, regardless of whether the child is in foster care, is accorded the personal rights specified in Welfare and Institutions Code Section 16001.9, and below, as applicable: ... To be accorded dignity in their personal relationships with staff and other persons." Continued... ...CONTINUED Facility staff did not accord female clients dignity by conducting inappropriate searches outdoors in the presence of male staff and peers, which poses a potential health, safety, or personal rights risk to clients in care. An exit interview was conducted, and a signed copy of the report and appeal rights were provided to Michelle Jenks, Administrator.

narrative: ...CONTINUED Confidential interviews indicated that prior to the punch, staff attempted to intervene in the verbal mistreatment from C2 towards C1 while C2 was preparing for a physical altercation by removing their rings. The Department also received an allegation that staff did not seek timely medical attention for a minor (C1). Specifically, it was reported that C1 did not receive medical care or have someone examine C1's eye after being punched. Confidential interviews indicate that staff (S2) examined C1's eye, offered C1 an icepack, and suggested taking C1 to the nearby hospital. Confidential interviews indicate that C1 declined medical attention and was not injured from the punch. Confidential interviews indicate that staff provided enhanced supervision of C1 for the remainder of the evening as a precaution. The Department also received an allegation that staff did not properly report an incident involving a minor (C1). Specifically, it was reported that staff did not report the altercation between C1 and C2 after the incident occurred. A record review of SIRs and emails received from the facility revealed that a full report was sent to CCL and the County Social Worker. Based on confidential interviews and records reviewed, the allegations that staff did not prevent a minor (C2) from attacking another minor while in care (C1), staff did not seek timely medical attention for a minor (C1), and staff did not properly report an incident involving a minor (C1) are unsubstantiated. The allegation may have happened or are valid, but there is not a preponderance of the evidence to prove that the alleged violations occurred. A short-term residential therapeutic program is a residential facility operated by a public agency or private organization and licensed by the department pursuant to Section 1562.01 that provides an integrated program of specialized and intensive care and supervision, services and supports, treatment, and short-term 24-hour care and supervision to children and/or nonminor dependents. The licensee shall employ direct care staff to meet the needs of children as specified in 87065.2 and provide adequate care and supervision to children. Facility staff (S1, S2) failed to provide adequate supervision by remaining outside the door in the hallway upon refusal of C3 to leave Bedroom 4. (Continued) The facility is being cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) standard 87065.2 (b)(1) Personnel Duties (b) Direct care staff shall perform the following duties: (1) supervision, protection, and care of children at all times, individually and in groups. A copy of this report, LIC 811, LIC 809-D, and appeal rights were reviewed and then provided to Michelle Hicks.

narrative: On August 21, 2025, at 09: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA') Jessica Peete and Cynthia Robinson (LPM) arrived at New Beginnings Residential Treatment Facility Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA's were greeted and granted access by Facility Manager Michelle Lofton; later joined by Administrator Jalisa Brown. The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual/random inspection of the facility. At 9: AM, LPA Peete began the physical plant inspection; Facility Manager Jalisa Brown assisted LPA in touring the facility's interior and exterior grounds. During the facility inspection, LPA observed cameras in the common areas. The cameras are not pointed toward client bedrooms or bathrooms. According to Administrator Brown's statement, the video cameras do not capture audio and do not replace staff supervision. The facility consists of four client bedrooms and two bathrooms, one of which is a staff bathroom, that clients still have access to and are able to use. All toilets, sinks, and showers are maintained in safe, sanitary, and operating condition. Additionally, the water in each bathroom measured between 105°F and 120°F. The facility features a dining area, kitchen, living room, laundry room, garage with a visitor area, and a therapist's office. The facility's outside grounds have two sheds, in the backyard, which are utilized as offices by the Program Director and Head of Service. There are four locked storage containers containing client files, and one shed housing holiday decorations and miscellaneous items. All client bedrooms have individual beds with adequate drawers and closet space for each client. In addition, LPA observed that each client's bedroom was equipped with a small combination safe to store personal items or contraceptives. The clients' bedrooms are arranged so there are no more than two clients per room. LPA observed that all client beds had the appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. Extra linens and toiletry items are stored in the garage and hall closet closest accessible to clients as needed. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space, and all exits and entrances are unobstructed. A toddler play area and patio furniture were observed in the backyard, along with other age-appropriate games and activities located in the garage, for the client's recreation time. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are in appropriate working order. The fire extinguishers are properly charged and placed throughout the facility. The facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods. Licensee maintains an adequate supply of food and a variety of snacks for clients. LPA observed a minimum of seven days of non-perishable food and a two-day perishable supply, and the facility appears to be following the posted menu. Cleansers, chemicals, and cooking knives are inaccessible to clients. Cleaners and chemicals are stored separately from all food items in a locked cabinet located in the garage. The cooking knives and all other sharp items are stored in the staff office, located inside a locked cabinet. All required forms are posted, including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Medications are locked and centrally stored in the staff office. No observable safety or health hazards were observed during the physical plant inspection, and no deficiencies were cited. LPA Peete reviewed the facility's operations, disaster preparedness, emergency interventions, and core therapeutic services. The core therapeutic services demonstrated that the appropriate services and supports for clients are trauma-informed, culturally relevant, and age- and developmentally appropriate. All required documentation was observed, and no deficiencies were found in the above-mentioned areas. LPA Robinson completed a review of five client files (C1 through C5). During the file review, it was noted that five of the clients did not have the required tuberculosis test. The licensee was cited with a type B violation of the Title California Code of Regulations 80069(c)(1) Client Medical Assessments. LPA Robinson also completed one client interview (C2), C5 declined. Based on observations made during the inspection, a deficiency is being cited (see LIC D). Due to time constraints, LPA's will return to complete the inspection at a later date. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report, along with appeal rights and the LIC Confidential Names List, was provided to the facility Administrator, Jalisa Brown.
