On November 9, 2023 at 2:08 pm Licensing Program Analyst (LPA), Nicole Strickland, met with New Beginnings Residential Treatment Facilities - Raja Program Director, Michelle Hicks, to deliver a case management deficiencies report. On September 27, 2023, LPA Strickland conducted a records review of six facility staff (Staff #1 [S1], Staff #2 [S2], Staff #3 [S3], Staff #4 [S4], Staff #5 [S5] and Staff #6 [S6]). Information obtained by Community Care Licensing (CCL) revealed five out of six staff members S1, S3, S4, S5, and S6 do not hold a valid First aid/CPR certificate as required by Short-Term Residential Therapeutic Program Interim Licensing Standards (ILS) v.4. Record review revealed S1, S3, S4, S5, and S6 had certificates for CPR issued by the NationalCPRFoundation.org. LPA confirmed with the organization that the certificates held by the staff members did not include a first aid component to the training. LPA gathered further information about the training program issuing the certificates for first aid which revealed the training provided to the staff does not meet the requirements as set forth in ILS v.4 standard 87065.1(b)(8)(A) SUPERVISION, EVALUATION AND TRAINING REQUIREMENTS (A) completion of cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and first aid training shall be demonstrated by current and valid CPR and first aid cards issued by the American Red Cross, the American Heart Association, a training program approved by the State Emergency Medical Services Authority pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 1797.191, or from an accredited college or university. Record review revealed New Beginnings Residential Treatment Facilities Program Statement/ Plan of Operation dated 4/09/2019 page 4 states, The Human Resource Department is responsible for maintaining comprehensive documentation of training education received for staff, peer partners and volunteers. Proof of successful completion of the training is verified by certificates, timesheets, and participants sign-in logs. Record review revealed the facility failed to verify S1, S3, S4, S5 and S6's training certificates were valid and met the requirements set forth in ILS v.4 standard 87065(b)(8)(A). This is a violation of ILS v.4 87022(f) ****** PLAN OF OPERATION The facility shall operate in accordance with the terms specified in the plan of operation and may be cited for not doing so. The facility is being cited for violation of Interim ILS v.4 standard 87065.1(b)(8)(A) SUPERVISION, EVALUATION AND TRAINING REQUIREMENTS and violation of ILS v.4 standard 87022(f) PLAN OF OPERATION. A copy of the report was discussed and provided along with appeal rights to New Beginnings Residential Treatment Facilities - Raja Program Director, Michelle Hicks

On December 18, 2023 at 2: PM, Associate Governmental Program Analyst (AGPA) Kim Robinson met with the short-term residential therapeutic program (STRTP) director, Michelle Hicks and administrator, Senida Zamora, in order to assess an Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP). On November 9, 2023, the Department concluded a complaint investigation alleging the direct care facility manager (S4) neglected to properly supervise and provide timely medical attention for a 16-year-old client #1 (C1). As a result, C1 was found unconscious from an overdose and later passed away. The allegation was determined substantiated, and the STRTP was cited from Interim Licensing Standards Section 87072 (c), Personal Rights and Section 87078(a) Responsibility for Providing Care and Supervision. An immediate civil penalty of $500.00 was assessed. See the Confidential Names List, LIC 811, dated November 9, 2023. Based on the findings from the medical report, consistent interviews and findings from the Riverside County Sheriff report the Department has determined that an enhanced civil penalty is warranted for S4's lack of supervision and prompt medical attention for C1. As a result, C1 suffered an overdose and loss of life while under the direct care of STRTP S4. Pursuant to the Enhanced Civil Penalty law, the Health and Safety Code 1548 (e)(3) states a violation the Department determines "resulted in the death of a person receiving care through a short term residential therapeutic program" the Department will issue an immediate civil penalty of $7,500.00. An exit interview was completed, and appeal rights discussed. A copy of this report, the Confidential Names List, and a Civil Penalty Assessment - Serious Bodily Injury/Physical Abuse (Form 421-D) were provided to the administrator. The signed copy will be retained in the facility file.

Confidential interviews and record review reported after C1 was observed to be unconscious S4 called S2 who was not at the facility at the time of the incident for assistance. Confidential interviews and record review further confirmed S2 arrived at the facility and began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) as well as instructed S4 to call 9-1-1. Confidential interviews reported S4 did not attempt or assist with any CPR or any life-saving measures until directed by S2 to call 9-1-1. Based on confidential interviews and record review the allegations alleging due to a lack of care and supervision minor (Child #1 [C1]) overdosed while in care and Minor (C1) did not receive medical treatment in a timely manner are substantiated. The complaint allegations are valid because the preponderance of evidence standard has been met. Facility is cited for violation of Interim Licensing Standards(ILS) v.4 standard 87078(a) RESPONSIBILITY FOR PROVIDING CARE AND SUPERVISION (a) In addition to California Code of Regulations, Title 22, Section 80078, the following shall apply, and ILS v.4 standard PERSONAL RIGHTS (c) The licensee shall ensure that each child, regardless of whether the child is in foster care, is accorded the personal rights specified in Welfare and Institutions Code Section 16001.9 as applicable. The facilities violation of ILS v.4 standard PERSONAL RIGHTS (c) which resulted in C1 not receiving prompt medical assistance when C1 overdosed requires the facility to be assessed an immediate civil penalty per Health and Safety Code 1548(c)(1). An Enhanced Civil Penalty (ECP) determination is pending. If an ECP is assessed a Community Care Licensing (CCL) representative will return to the facility to deliver the penalty assessment. A copy of the report was discussed and provided along with Civil Penalty assessment and appeal rights to New Beginnings Residential Treatment Facility - Raja Program Director, Michelle Hicks.

narrative: On May 14, 2021 at 11: AM, Licensing Program Analyst conducted an unannounced follow up case management inspection with (STRTP) New Beginnings Residential Treatment Shalom Administrator, Stacy Rougely via tele inspection. LPA communicated with Ms Rougely regarding a special incident report (SIR) that was submitted to Community Care Licensing (CCL) on March 15, 2021. The SIR disclosed that on March 14, 2021, staff #1 (S1) knowingly transported four clients (C1, C2, C3, C4) from Yucca Valley to Perris out of ratio. Confidential interviews revealed that S1 stopped at Shoe City and left the four clients in the van unattended for an unknown amount of time. Interview with S1 disclosed that on 3/14/21, S1 transported four clients with the knowledge that regulations are three to one ratio in the vehicle but that facility manager (FM) had given S1 permission due to the STRTP being short staffed. S1 admitted to having C1, C2, C3, and C4 with her on the transport. Interview with ADM disclosed that S1 normally works Sunday through Wednesday and does not usually transport clients but that on 3/14/21 the STRTP was short staffed. The facility is being cited for violation of the STRTP Interim Licensing Standards (ILS),Section 87065.5 (a) (1) Direct Care Staff/ Child Ratios. This is based on confidential interviews and record review, staff#1 (S1) transported four clients (C1, C2, C3, C4) out of ratio due to STRTP being short staffed on 03/14/21. This poses a potential risk to chidren An exit interview was conducted and a copy of this report, LIC 811, and appeal rights were provided via email to Stacy Rougely for signature. On June 23, 2021 at 10: AM, Licensing Program Analysts (LPA's) Anastasia Flores and LPA Valerie Wilson, arrived at New Beginnings Residential Shalom Facility (STRTP). LPA was greeted and granted access by Facility Manager, Ajah Jelks. The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual inspection of the facility. There was one facility manager and one therapist present at the time of the inspection. Two clients were in school and one client was on home pass. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during the inspection. At 10: AM, Ajah Jelks led the tour of the facility. The facility consists of four bedrooms and two bathrooms. The facility includes a dining area, kitchen area, living room and laundry room/garage utilized for storage. The facility has a staff office and bedroom #4 is utilized by therapists. All bedrooms have individual beds and drawer space for each client. The facility ensures that there is one client per bed with appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. During inspection, bedroom #2 did not have an operable fire alarm, however it was fixed and working prior to leaving the facility. Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. There is adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. The screen by the kitchen table, sliding screen door to backyard and two screens on the master bedroom need to be replaced and there was no screen on the master bathroom window. Program Director called maintenance and is having them fixed and replaced on 06/26/21. Gym equipment and other activities were observed for client's recreation time. All facility smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors are in appropriate working order. The facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods and appears to be following the posted menu. All required forms are posted including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Medications are locked and centrally stored in the staff office. At 10: AM, the hot water in the kitchen was measured to be 110.4 degrees, master bathroom #1 was measured at 11: AM to be 113 degrees and at 11: AM bathroom #2 measured at 113.4 degrees. Per facility staff, no firearms or weapons are allowed in the facility. Facility appears to be meeting the terms and conditions of their license. () Administrator Stacy Rougely, is present at the facility a minimum of 20 hours a week, as verified by staff schedule and interviews. Appropriate staff/client ratios were verified during this inspection. The facility employs one therapist, one facility administrator, one facility manager, nine direct care staff, one head of service and one Program Director. Facility has obtained Mental Health Certification effective 04/09/2019. Licensee has obtained National Accreditation through CARF effective through 11/30/2022. Licensing fee payments have been paid and there is currently a balance of zero. At 11: AM, six of six client files were reviewed during time of inspection. There were required documents not up to date in the client files, but due to time constraints, deficiencies and/or advisory notes will be issued on a separate date. Personnel Files are maintained off site at the corporate office in Riverside, Ca. However, during inspection staff files were brought to the facility for review. At 12: PM, personnel files were reviewed to ensure they contained all required documentation per Title Regulations and Interim Licensing Standards (ILS). At 12: PM, LPA's reviewed 10 staff files. Staff files were complete with First Aid/CPR certificates, certificates for training hours, and all required documents were signed and present. All appropriate personnel who require caregiver background checks have received criminal record and child abuse index check clearances or exemptions. There were six staff files that needed updated medical records. At 2: PM, LPA's interviewed three direct care staff and one facility manager that were present, in regard to their job duties, training, and services provided at the facility. All staff were able to provide sufficient information in relation to the facility's program. Four of five clients present during inspection volunteered to be interviewed, one client refused. All four clients indicate that their basic needs are being met at the facility and core services being provided as well. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report and appeal rights were provided to Administrator, Stacy Rougely.

On August 26, 2025, at 12: PM, Licensing Program Analyst (LPA) Jessica Peete arrived at New Beginnings Residential Shalom Treatment Facility Short Term Residential Therapeutic Program (STRTP). LPA was greeted and granted access by Administrator Nannette Lewis.The purpose of the visit is to conduct an annual/random inspection of the facility. At 12: PM, LPA Peete began the physical plant inspection; Administrator Lewis assisted LPA in touring the facility's interior and exterior grounds. During the facility inspection, LPA observed cameras in the common areas, the therapist office, hallways, and the outside perimeter, both front and back of the home. The cameras are not pointed toward client bedrooms or bathrooms. According to the Administrator's statement, the video cameras do not capture audio and do not replace staff supervision. The monitors in the staff office display live feed from the facility's cameras. The facility consists of four bedrooms, three of which are client bedrooms; bedroom four is utilized as the therapist's office. There are two bathrooms, one of which is a staff bathroom, that clients still have access to and can use. All client bedrooms have individual beds with adequate drawers and closet space for each client. The client bedrooms are equipped with a small combination safe for storing personal items or contraceptives and are arranged so that there are no more than two clients per room. LPA observed that all client beds had the appropriate clean linens, pillows, comforters, and mattresses in good repair. Extra linens and toiletry items are stored in the garage and entryway closet, accessible to clients as needed. All toilets, sinks, and showers are maintained in safe, sanitary, and operating condition. Additionally, the water in each bathroom and in the kitchen measured between 105°F and 120°F. The facility also features a dining area, kitchen, living room, garage with a washer and dryer, and a designated central storage area with extra household supplies and hygiene products. The storage is accessible to staff as needed to ensure the STRTP is maintained with sufficient supplies. The Facility grounds are clean and free of debris and observable hazards. The facility maintains its fire clearance, and all exits and entrances are unobstructed. LPA observed adequate indoor and outdoor activity space. The facility's outside grounds were observed to be well maintained, free of debris, and in good condition, with patio furniture that appeared suitable for client use. Additionally, LPA observed age-appropriate games and activities for the client's recreational time. The facility smoke detector and carbon monoxide detector are in appropriate working order. The fire extinguishers are properly charged and placed throughout the facility. The facility maintains an adequate supply of perishable and non-perishable foods, including a variety of snacks for clients. LPA observed a minimum of seven days of non-perishable food and a two-day perishable supply, and the facility appears to be following the posted menu. Cleansers, chemicals, and cooking knives are inaccessible to clients. Cleaners and chemicals are stored separately from all food items in a locked cabinet located in the garage. The cooking knives and all other sharp items are stored in the entryway closet. The Medications are locked and centrally stored in the staff office. All required forms are posted, including the Grievance Procedures, Visitation Policies, Personal Rights form, and Foster Care Ombudsman poster. Additionally, the facility maintains two vehicles for client transportation. Both vehicles are in good working condition and have current registration and valid insurance. No observable safety or health hazards were noted during the physical plant inspection, and no deficiencies were cited. LPA Peete also reviewed the facility's operational requirements and no deficiencies were noted for this area of the inspection. Based on observations made during the inspection, no deficiencies are being cited. Due to time constraints, LPA will return to complete the inspection at a later date. An exit interview was conducted, and a copy of this report, along with appeal rights, was provided to the facility Administrator, Nannette Lewis.
